games.title: Scrapwing
games.pitch: Shoot down raiders and bolt their guns onto your hull. Lose them and you fly bare.
games.hook: The first drone pops in under two seconds and drops a glowing cannon; you fly into it, it clanks onto your hull and your fire visibly doubles. The ship you are flying grows in front of you.
games.loop: Vertical shooter with auto-fire. Your ship is a small reactor core (8px hitbox) with 6 fixed hex sockets around it (a second ring of 6 opens after the first boss). Seeded enemy formations come in waves of 8-20 s. Kills drop parts (25%, always from elites): Blaster (straight stream from its socket), Fan (3-way spread angled the way its socket faces), Seeker (a slow homing missile every 1.2 s), Plate (no gun, takes 3 hits). Touching a part snaps it into the nearest free socket on the side that touched it, so where you catch parts shapes the ship. Three of the same type in adjacent sockets fuse into one tier-2 module (bigger, glows, double damage) and free two sockets. Enemy bullets that hit a module knock it off: it tumbles away and can be caught again within 2 s. A bullet on the core ends the run. Every 5th wave is a boss built from seeded parts (a hull silhouette, 2-4 turret pods, an armoured weak core); each pod you destroy drops a guaranteed tier-2 part. Score is kills times a chain multiplier that resets when you lose a module.
games.controls: One thumb: drag anywhere and the ship follows with a 70px upward offset so it stays clear of the thumb (relative drag, capped speed). Fire is automatic. Keyboard: arrows/WASD move.
games.progression: A sector is 5 waves plus a boss. Each sector adds one enemy type (sweepers, mine layers, laser gates with a 1 s glow tell, shielded carriers, splitters, snipers that aim at modules), adds about 12% bullet density, and tints the nebula. Bosses gain a pod each sector. There are 8 sector archetypes, then they loop with a 'hard' modifier (faster bullets, armoured pods). Checkpoint: the run is saved at each sector start (core plus 2 Blasters), shown as 'Sector 4'. Keeping a tier-2 build alive is the reason to play another 3 minutes.
games.art: Warm scrapyard nebula, not navy: the sky is layered magenta-to-amber gas (#2a0f2e base, #8a2f4a mid, #f08a3c glow lanes) with two parallax dust layers, a huge banded gas giant (#d9774b with cream rings) drifting past slowly, and big foreground wreck silhouettes (#140812) sliding by fast for speed. Light comes from a low amber star at top-right, so ships carry a warm rim on that side. The player core is brushed steel with a cyan reactor (#5ff2ff). Modules are colour-coded: Blaster #ffd23f, Fan #2ec4b6, Seeker #ff4f8b, Plate gunmetal #6b6f7a with rivets. Raiders are matte black-violet with orange engine flares. Only enemy bullets use hot white cores with a pink halo, so threats always read. HUD: riveted metal corner plates with stencil numerals, a small live hull schematic bottom-left showing filled sockets, and a hazard-stripe boss bar. Shell theme: industrial salvage (hazard stripes, stencil type, bolt heads).
games.audio: Synthwave at 128 BPM in a minor key: saw-bass arpeggio, square lead, noise hats. Bosses move to 140 BPM with a detuned lead and a heavier kick. SFX: a two-tone metallic clank when a module attaches, a chime and 'whoomp' when three fuse, a different pew for each module type (pitch-varied), noise explosions with a pitch drop, a clatter as a module is knocked off, and a rising alarm sting when a boss enters.
juice: Module attach: ship squash-and-stretch, a spark burst at the socket, a clank, a short haptic tick
Fusing three into tier-2: white flash ring, parts slide together, 60ms hitstop, a chord
Knocked-off module tumbles away with a fading trail and a dashed 'catch me' ring for 2 s
Boss pods blow up in a chained sequence with 80ms hitstop each; the boss death plays 0.4 s of slow motion and a big shake
Score popups count up and the chain multiplier punches in scale at each step
games.teach: Wave 1 is five slow drones that never fire, and a ghost hand shows the drag. The first kill always drops a Blaster with a pulsing arrow. Fire auto-starts so shooting needs no teaching. Wave 2's bullets are slow and sparse, with a one-line 'Bullets knock parts off. Protect the core.' that fades out.
games.scenes: art: a fully built ship (6 modules, two tier-2 glowing) firing into a boss with 3 turret pods against the amber nebula and gas giant, no HUD. shot1: early wave 2, a Fan part falling toward the ship and the attach sparks visible. shot2: sector 3 boss fight with a pink bullet pattern, a module tumbling off and the hull schematic in the HUD.
games.feasibility: Low-to-medium risk. Sockets are fixed positions, so there is no free-form ship building and fusion is an adjacency check on 6-12 slots. Bullets and enemies live in fixed pools (512 bullets) with circle collisions. Bosses are data: a seeded list of pod positions and patterns on one hull sprite. Glow sprites are pre-rendered to offscreen canvases (no shadowBlur per frame); additive blending only for the reactor and explosions. Formations are generated from seed plus wave index. Debug hook: ?debug exposes window.__game {start(seed, sector), step(ms), lose(), state()} and a scene(name) for art capture, so Playwright can start a run, give modules and force a loss.

games.title: Pipistrelle
games.pitch: Fly a little bat through pitch-black caves. Chirp to paint the walls in echoes.
games.hook: The cave starts completely black. Your first tap sends out a sonar ring, and the cave appears as glowing dots wherever the sound hits stone, then fades. Moths flash gold in the echo. You get that 'I can see with sound' feeling in the first two seconds, and you want to chirp again straight away.
games.loop: Each cave is a seeded side-on level 6 to 10 screens long. Its tunnels branch, and it holds one moonlit exit. The bat flies freely. Drag works as a relative stick: the bat accelerates along the drag vector, and when you let go it glides with damping. The world is dark apart from a 24px glow around the bat and faint 'memory' lines (alpha 0.06) on walls you have already echoed. CHIRP: a ring expands at 600px/s out to a 420px radius, and 120 rays are cast once against the cave grid. Each hit spawns an echo point coloured by surface (rock teal, water blue, web white, moth gold, hazard crimson) that fades over 2.2s. Chirp cooldown is 0.6s. A SHRIEK reaches twice as far, but its cooldown is 3s and it wakes nearby roosting hazards. ENERGY drains slowly. Moths (erratic fliers, seen only as gold flecks in echoes) restore it. Bumping a wall costs a little energy and stuns the bat with a squeak, so walls are never instant death. HAZARDS are all telegraphed. Stalactites drop when you pass under them (pebble tick plus a shimmer in the echo). Spider webs slow you until you wiggle free. Underground rivers carry a current. Owls wait in side chambers and swoop when shrieked awake. PUPS hang upside down in nooks. Fly through one and it joins a trailing line, and each pup adds +1 to the score multiplier. Reaching the exit banks moths × multiplier and starts a 15s night-sky bonus over treetops (free moths), then the next cave. The run ends when energy reaches 0.
games.controls: One or two thumbs. The first touch drags anywhere as a relative stick to steer. A quick tap (<180ms, <10px move) from that finger, or any tap from a second finger, chirps. Press and hold the second finger for 0.5s to shriek. Keyboard: arrows/WASD to fly, Space to chirp, Shift to shriek.
games.progression: Cave 1 is wide and safe. New elements arrive one at a time: cave 2 webs, 3 falling stalactites, 4 rivers with current, 5 crystal chambers (crystals re-echo a second, delayed reveal, a free bonus), 6 wind gusts through chimneys, 7 owls, 8 flooded sections with drip lines. After that caves mix elements, get narrower and longer, and moths get rarer. Each cave is seeded from (runSeed, caveIndex), so a cave plays the same on retry. The save holds the current cave number, energy and rescued pups, so the run resumes at the cave entrance. The best score is moths banked.
games.art: World: a living limestone cave at night. Base darkness runs from #05060d to #0b1022. All visibility comes from additive echo glows (pre-rendered radial sprites drawn with 'lighter'). Rock echoes teal #4ff0d8, water #3a7bff, webs #e8f0ff, moths gold #ffcf5a, hazards #ff4a6b. The background is two parallax layers of stalactite silhouettes (#0e1530) that light up dimly when the echo reaches them, which gives depth. The exit is a moonlit arch with cool #9fc6ff spill light and drifting dust motes. The bat is drawn in code: membrane wings with visible finger bones, a 6-frame flap (procedural wing-bone angles), big ears, tiny fangs, warm brown #8a5a44 body with a cyan rim light on every chirp. HUD: sonar style. Concentric partial arcs in the top-left fill as the cooldown recovers, energy is a row of moth-wing pips, and pups are tiny hanging-bat icons. No panels anywhere, just thin glowing lines on black. Shell theme: ink-black with cyan radar rings, and the title is drawn as an echo-dot logo.
games.audio: Music: sparse cave ambient at 70bpm. A low sine drone plus glassy pentatonic triangle plucks through a long feedback delay, and water-drip percussion (short sine pings at random-but-seeded intervals). The tempo nudges to 78bpm and a pulsing bass joins from cave 6. SFX: the chirp is a 2 to 6kHz sine sweep of 60ms. Its returning echoes are softer copies delayed in proportion to the distance hit (sampled from 6 ray distances), so the cave literally sounds its size. Also a moth crunch, a wall-bump squeak, a stalactite crack plus whoosh plus thud, a web stretch (detuned saw wobble), a pup-join trill, an owl hoot (two-tone FM), and a warm major chord at the exit.
juice: Echo returns are audible with delays that match real distances, and dots light up in sync with the sound
Eating a moth gives a gold particle burst, the bat's cheeks puff, and the energy pips count up
A falling stalactite crashes with screen shake, a dust plume and a ring of echo light from the impact
Reaching the exit floods the screen with moonlight in a radial wipe while the pups trail out behind you
A rescued pup flips upright with a little heart chirp and joins the wobbling bat conga line
games.teach: The first chirp fires automatically on spawn, so the reveal is shown before any instruction. Then a ghost hand drags (steer) while a ghost dot taps (chirp). The first tunnel is wide, and a moth sits one chirp away. Pups pulse softly in the echo with a small heart icon. The pause menu holds a 3-panel pictorial How to play.
games.scenes: art: a big chirp ring mid-expansion reveals a crystal chamber in teal and gold, the bat with spread wings in the centre-left, moths glinting, and the moonlit exit arch top-right. No HUD. shot1: cave 1 with an echo ring revealing the tunnel and two moths, the HUD sonar arcs and energy pips visible. shot2: cave 5 with an underground river in blue echoes, a stalactite mid-fall with red shimmer, and three rescued pups trailing the bat.
games.feasibility: Low to medium risk. The cave is a seeded cellular automaton on a 12px grid, smoothed and then flood-fill checked so start and exit connect (if not, regenerate with seed+1). DDA raycasts run only on chirp (120 rays), which is cheap. Echo points sit in a fixed pool (max 3000) drawn as cached glow sprites, and remembered walls are a half-resolution offscreen canvas that is only added to. The main risk is unfair darkness, mitigated by soft walls, memory lines and the bat glow. Flight feel needs tuning (damped velocity, max speed 260px/s). Test hook: window.__game = { start(seed, cave), chirp(), input(dx, dy), step(frames), drainEnergy() /* forces a loss */, state() }, with seeded RNG throughout so the Playwright bot can fly a fixed route.

games.title: Tinplate GP
games.pitch: Hold to throttle a tin slot car. Too fast into a bend and it flies off the track.
games.hook: Four lithographed tin cars buzz around a lamp-lit workbench. You hold to throttle and your car screams down the straight, the bend ahead glows amber then red, and if you hold too long your car shimmies, flips off in a clatter of tin and a little grabber arm puts it back. Instantly understood, instantly tense.
games.loop: The whole circuit fits the screen, seen from above. Four lanes, and each car is locked in its slot. You control only throttle: hold anywhere for power (it ramps over 0.3 s), release to coast and brake. Each point on each lane has a corner limit, v_max = sqrt(grip x radius). Going past it makes the car shimmy (tail wiggle, squeal, the lane glow going green to amber to red). More than 5% over the limit for 0.12 s de-slots it: the car flies off on the tangent, tumbles and sheds a wind-up key or a tyre, then a tin grabber arm re-slots it 1.6 s later. Crossover pieces let a second-thumb tap or a double-tap switch to the next lane (inside lanes are shorter but have tighter limits). Special pieces: banked turns (higher limit), loop-the-loops (need a minimum speed or the car falls), jump ramps (too slow falls short, too fast flips over) and bridges on figure-8s. Five laps against 3 AI cars that drive at their skill fraction of the limit and make seeded mistakes. A championship is 6 races scored 10/6/3/1. The run ends after race 6 (reason 'win' if you lead, else 'lose'). Score = points x 1000 + fastest-lap bonus. Two-player on one device: the left and right thumbs each hold the throttle of their own car (lane change by a quick double-tap on your own side), racing the championship against each other plus two AI cars.
games.controls: Touch: hold anywhere to throttle, release to brake, tap with a second finger (or double-tap) to change lane at a crossover. Keyboard: Space to throttle, Up/Down or Shift to change lane. Two-player: each player owns one half of the screen (or the A and L keys).
games.progression: Tracks come from 7 templates (oval, kidney, figure-8 with a bridge, hairpin, tri-oval, spiral, dog-bone) with seeded perturbation. Banks arrive in race 2, loops in race 3, jumps in race 4. AI skill goes from 0.86 to 0.98 of the limit. Later championships mix in all the pieces and add a wet 'spilled tea' patch that lowers grip. Tin cars unlock with podiums (light ones grip well but accelerate slowly, heavy ones accelerate fast but de-slot easily), plus lithograph liveries. Each track keeps a fastest-lap ghost.
games.art: A night workshop seen from directly above. A walnut workbench #6b4423 with procedural wood grain, in a warm desk-lamp pool #ffd27a that falls off to a deep brown-black vignette #1a0f08. Code-drawn props with soft offset shadows: rulers, pencils, a screwdriver, a coffee mug and its stain ring, spools of thread, nuts and bolts, an open tin box. The track is black plastic sections with glinting copper rail stripes, segment seams and lane colour dots. Cars are lithographed tin with halftone-dot shading, chrome bumpers, big race numbers, wind-up keys and drop shadows that lift during tumbles. HUD styled as printed tin badges: the lap count is a mechanical rolling-digit counter, the position is a stamped tin medallion, and a vintage plunger controller in the corner presses in as you hold. Shell theme: a lithographed tin toy-box lid with a starburst, rivets and a cream #f3e3c3, toy red #d43d2f and navy #23395b scheme.
games.audio: A ragtime swing loop at 120 bpm: toy-piano triangle melody, square upright bass, brush snare, clockwork ticks as the hi-hat. Sound effects: electric motor whine for each car (sawtooth pitched by speed, yours loudest), slot buzz, shimmy squeal, de-slot (tin clatter, spring boing, crash), grabber arm servo whirr, lap (bicycle-bell ding), lane change (click-clack), finish (toy fanfare).
juice: Your lane glows green to amber to red as you approach a corner's limit
A de-slot tumbles the car with sparks and bouncing tin parts and nudges the camera zoom toward the crash
A loop-the-loop pulses the camera as the car spins round
On a fastest lap the rolling counter flickers and the digits flash gold
An overtake flips the position medallion with a stamping sound
At the finish paper-punch confetti falls
games.teach: Race 1 is a plain oval with a ghost thumb holding 'hold'. The first bend glows red when you are too fast, and de-slotting once is harmless and teaches the limit. The crossover shows a ghost second-finger tap the first time you approach it. Track tutorial_complete after the first lap without a de-slot.
games.scenes: art: the lamp-lit workbench from above with a figure-8 track, four tin cars, one tumbling off a bend in sparks, props around, no HUD. shot1: the start grid with the rolling counter, medallion and plunger. shot2: a loop piece and a banked turn with your lane glowing red and position 1.
games.feasibility: Low risk, very testable. Lanes are offsets of a closed spline, with arc length and curvature precomputed per sample. Each car's state is just s and v. A de-slotted car is a free projectile plus a spin. Figure-8 bridges are drawn in two passes, under then over. The circuit is scaled to fit the screen, so there is no camera. Test hook ?debug exposes window.__game { start(seed, race), throttle(0..1), changeLane(), bot(skill), forceDeslot(), endRun(), state() } so Playwright can race a bot through a championship and force a loss.

games.title: Napwalk
games.pitch: Swipe and every cat steps the same way. Get each cat curled up on its cushion.
games.hook: One swipe and a little parade of cats trots in lockstep. The first to reach its cushion yawns, turns three circles and curls up purring. It is charming instantly, and you see the puzzle at once: the sleeping cat is now a wall.
games.loop: A top-down room grid of 6x8 (later 7x9) with walls and furniture (sofa, plant, bookcase, table) that block movement. It holds 2-5 cats, each with a coat (ginger, grey, black, calico, white), and the same number of cushions in matching patterns. A swipe moves every awake cat one tile in that direction at once. Moves resolve together, leading edge first: a cat blocked by a wall, furniture, a sleeping cat or a blocked cat stays put and wiggles. A cat that steps onto its own coat's cushion falls asleep and becomes a permanent obstacle; a cat on the wrong cushion just walks over it. The goal is every cat asleep. Later elements: Rugs (slippery: a cat stepping on keeps sliding until it leaves the rug or is blocked), Yarn balls (a cat entering one plays with it and skips the next swipe, and the yarn rolls one tile on), and Pet-door pairs (a cat entering one comes out of the other). Par is the optimal move count from BFS: stars at par or better, par+3, or solved. Undo and restart are unlimited and there is no fail. A hint button shows the next optimal swipe as a paw arrow, but a hinted room caps at 2 stars.
games.controls: One thumb: swipe anywhere on the room (a 24px threshold, picking the dominant axis). Felt buttons for Undo, Restart and Hint sit at the bottom within thumb reach. Keyboard: arrows or WASD, plus Z to undo and R to restart.
games.progression: Rooms 1-10: 2 cats, any cushion colour. Rooms 11-20: 3 cats with coat-matched cushions. Rooms 21-30: rugs. Rooms 31-40: yarn. Rooms 41-50: pet doors and 4 cats. Room 51 onward is endless with mixed elements and 4-5 cats. Every room is generated from seed (room*7919+attempt): furniture comes from small templates, then cats and cushions are placed. A BFS over joint states (cat positions, sleep flags and yarn timers, capped at 200k states) gives the optimal par. The room is accepted only if par falls in the band (3-5 early, rising to 14-22) and every cat must move at least twice, with solutions that repeat one direction rejected. Stars per room and a total stars count are kept. The run is saved, and progress shows 'Room 23'. Best = rooms solved.
games.art: A cosy 3/4 top-down living room in late-afternoon sun. Honey wood floor planks (#d9a066 and #c4884f) with drawn grain lines and seams. A window at the top casts a skewed sunbeam polygon composited 'lighter' at about 25% (#ffe2a8) with drifting dust motes. Wallpaper at the top carries a small botanical repeat (#e9dcc3 and #9bb28a). Furniture has soft rounded corners and fabric patterns: a striped sage sofa (#7a9e7e), terracotta pots (#c8643b) with leaves, and a bookcase with coloured spines. Rugs are woven kilim-like patterns in rose and indigo. Each furniture piece casts a soft shadow. Cats are round vector bodies with ears, sine-animated tails, blinking eyes and coat patterns: tabby stripes, calico patches, a white chest on black. A sleeping cat becomes a curled donut with a tucked tail and floating Zzz. Cushions are plump with button tufts and coat-matching piping. HUD: felt fabric tags hanging by threads from a curtain rod across the top, one each for the room number, moves and par (par as a paw-print row), with embroidered felt patch buttons. The menu shell is felt and knit. Dark mode is an evening room at #2a2030 with a warm table-lamp pool (#ffb35c radial), dimmer wallpaper and glowing cat eyes.
games.audio: Music: lo-fi jazz at 80 bpm, with soft Rhodes-like chords (sine plus tremolo with a bell partial), brushed noise hats and a walking sine bass. SFX: pitter-patter of 3 tiny filtered clicks per cat step, staggered between cats; a little 'mrrp?' when blocked (a two-sine formant glide); a yawn glide plus a purr (low noise amplitude-modulated at 25 Hz) when a cat falls asleep; a rug slide swish; a yarn bat 'boing'; and a music-box ditty when a room is solved.
juice: Cats hop with squash and stretch on each step, staggered by 30 ms so the movement reads as a parade
A blocked cat bonks with a sweat drop, a head shake and a tiny haptic
Falling asleep plays a stretch, three circles and a curl as Zzz particles float up
A solved room makes all cats purr in sync, hearts drift up, the sunbeam brightens and paw-print stars stamp in with a haptic
Undo rewinds the last move in reverse with a soft whoosh
games.teach: Room 1 has two cats and two cushions in open floor, and an animated ghost swipe arrow shows the first move, which puts one cat to sleep. Room 2 can only be solved by using a wall to hold one cat while the other moves. If the player is idle for 10 s, the useful wall pulses gently.
games.scenes: Art: the sunlit room with four cats, two asleep on cushions, one mid-hop, a rug, a yarn ball and dust motes, with no HUD. Shot1: Room 1 with felt tags and the ghost swipe arrow. Shot2: Room 34 with rugs, yarn, 4 coloured cats and the hint paw arrow.
games.feasibility: One step(state, dir) function is shared by the solver, the play and the tests, so the solver and the game cannot disagree. Global moves keep reachable states small; BFS is capped and a seed that exceeds the cap is rejected, with each attempt deterministic. The generation budget is 300 ms per room. Cat animation uses tweens plus procedural poses with no sprite sheets, and pose drawing should be kept to 3 poses: walk, sit and curl. Test hook ?debug: __game.start(room), .swipe('up'), .solution(), .state(), .forfeit() (runEnd 'restart'). Estimated 1800-2400 lines.

games.title: Long Ball Night
games.pitch: Home run derby at a seaside ballpark. Aim the bat, let go to swing, light up the boardwalk.
games.hook: The first pitch floats in slowly with a ghost circle showing where to hold your thumb; you let go, the bat cracks, and the ball sails over the wall into a boardwalk Ferris wheel whose lights chase round in a spiral. It is the perfect ten-second dopamine hit.
games.loop: Catcher's-eye view behind the batter, the whole ballpark in perspective beyond (field, outfield wall, stands, boardwalk and sea). Press and hold the lower half of the screen: a sweet-spot reticle appears about 80 px above your thumb, and moving the thumb moves it around the strike zone. Release to swing: the swing happens at the reticle's position at that instant. The pitch is a 3D point travelling toward the plate with its own path (fastball straight, curveball breaking down and in, changeup slower, slider late break sideways, knuckler wobbling). Contact quality = 3D distance between the reticle and the ball at the plate, plus timing (early pulls the ball, late pushes it the other way, too far = whiff or foul). Contact gives exit speed and launch angle, the ball flies as a 3D projectile with drag and a shadow on the field, and it lands as a home run if it clears the fence at that angle. A whiff or a foul, and any strike you take (pitch in the zone, no swing), is an out; a fair ball that stays in the park costs half an out (two of them make one out), so making contact is never punished as hard as a whiff; balls outside the zone that you let go by cost nothing. 10 outs ends the derby. Score: distance in feet for each home run x a streak multiplier (consecutive home runs), plus bonuses for hitting lit targets beyond the fence (Ferris wheel, a neon fish sign, a lighthouse lamp, a moving blimp-like kite).
games.controls: One thumb: hold to show the reticle above your thumb and move it, release to swing. Keyboard: arrow keys move the reticle, Space to swing.
games.progression: Pitchers change every 5 home runs during a run, each a seeded combination of repertoire and speed: the first throws only slow fastballs, the next adds changeups, then curves, sliders, faster fastballs and finally knucklers with a late shimmy. Golden pitch every 7th pitch: a glowing ball worth triple. Beyond-the-fence targets move or appear as the night deepens (the sky darkens from dusk to night as the derby goes on, and more boardwalk lights come on), so long runs look and feel different. Best score and longest home run are kept.
games.art: A 1960s-style seaside ballpark at dusk turning to night. Palette: dusk sky gradient from peach #F4A259 to violet #5B2A86 to night #1A1230 (shifts during a run), outfield grass #2D6A4F with mowed stripes #357A5A, infield clay #C8794A, cream #FFF3D6 chalk lines, ketchup red #D62828 and mustard #F7B32B on stands and pennants, sea #1F4E79 beyond the boardwalk. Layers: sky with drifting clouds lit from below; the sea horizon with a lighthouse sweeping a beam; the boardwalk with a Ferris wheel (spokes and gondolas drawn in code, lights chase), a roller coaster silhouette and neon signs drawn as glowing shapes (no words); stands as tiers of tiny bobbing fan dots; light towers with bloom; the field in perspective with a shadow under the ball. The batter is a stylised retro player silhouette from behind with cream jersey and red cap, bat swing in a few drawn frames with motion smear. HUD: a hand-operated manual scoreboard in the outfield (green boards with cream tiles that flip) shows outs as lit bulbs (a half-lit bulb for half an out) and the score; the batter-side bottom shows the streak as baseball stitches. Shell 'solid' with cream panels, red trim and mustard buttons, Unbounded headings in a vintage feel.
games.audio: Music: a bouncy ballpark organ shuffle at 112 BPM (square and sine organ with tremolo, walking bass, brushed snare); a rising organ 'charge' riff plays during long home run streaks. SFX: pitcher wind-up rustle, pitch whoosh (pitch matched to speed), crack of the bat (sharp noise transient plus a woody resonant ping; better contact = brighter crack), whiff (air swish), foul tick, catcher mitt pop on called strikes, crowd roar that swells with flight distance, Ferris-wheel light chase (a rising run of bell ticks), target hit (bell and neon buzz).
juice: Perfect contact: 6 frames of hit-stop, the bat flashes, a shockwave ring at the contact point and the camera tilts up to follow the ball
Home run: the distance counter races in feet as the ball flies, the Ferris wheel's lights chase round in a spiral, crowd roar
Target hit: the Ferris wheel or neon sign flares and spins, coins of light shower, '+500' in mustard type
Streak: each consecutive home run adds a stitch to the HUD and makes the organ climb a step in key
Whiff: the batter twirls, a dust puff from the plate, outs bulb flips on with a clunk
Golden pitch: the ball glows gold with a sparkle trail as it comes in
games.teach: First two pitches are slow meatballs with a ghost circle showing where to place the reticle and a ghost thumb lifting at the right moment. After the first home run on your own, the ghosts stop and tutorial_complete is tracked. One-line hint: 'Hold to aim, let go to swing'.
games.scenes: art: the ball at the top of a towering arc over the outfield wall toward the Ferris wheel mid light chase, dusk sky, batter in follow-through, no HUD. shot1: a pitch mid-flight with the reticle visible above the thumb and the manual scoreboard. shot2: a golden pitch home run hitting the neon sign at night with the streak multiplier counting up.
games.feasibility: Risks: 3D projection of the ballpark and pitch paths. Mitigation: one fixed camera and a simple pinhole projection; the field, wall and stands are drawn once to an offscreen canvas (with a second copy for night), and only the ball, its shadow, the batter and the lights animate. Pitches are parametric curves from release to plate (no physics), and hit flight is a point with gravity and linear drag. Fence distance is a function of spray angle. Test hook: start(), lose() records 10 outs, and ?debug perfectSwing() places the reticle and releases at the ideal time so test.cjs can check home runs, outs on whiffs, streaks and best-score saving; seeded pitch sequences make it deterministic.

games.title: Night Bloom
games.pitch: Burst one firework at its peak and watch the blast chain across the sky above a lakeside castle.
games.hook: Rockets whistle up over a glittering lake below a hill castle. One tap and a gold peony blooms, catches its neighbours, and the sky erupts in a climbing chain of colour and notes, all reflected in the water. The first tap pays off with a show.
games.loop: Each wave launches 10-30 shells from barges at the bottom in staggered, seeded arcs. Each shell has a visible fuse spark and fizzles harmlessly if it is never ignited. You get a few sparks per wave (usually 2, shown as matchsticks). Tap near a shell (60 px forgiving radius) to ignite it. Its burst radius expands over 0.6 s and lingers. Any shell inside a live burst ignites too, so chains propagate. Igniting a shell in its apex window (it glows white for 0.35 s at the top of its arc) makes a 'Bloom' with 1.5× radius. Each wave has a quota of shells ignited. Missing it costs one of 3 beacon braziers on the castle wall, and losing all 3 ends the show. Score per shell = 10 × chain depth, with Bloom ×2 and a wave-clear bonus for each shell over quota. Shell types: peony (round burst), willow (long-lingering drooping burst that holds the chain open), crossette (splits into 4 small offset bursts), ring (only the ring edge ignites), strobe (flickers on and off), dud smoke shell (absorbs the blast and blocks the chain), and a golden shell that returns a spark.
games.controls: One thumb: tap the sky. Keyboard play is not natural here, so it is touch or mouse only.
games.progression: Wave 1 has 8 slow peonies in a cluster and a quota of 5. New shell types arrive one per wave (willow 2, crossette 3, ring 5, smoke 6, strobe 8). Spacing widens and launch timing staggers more, so finding the chain gets harder. Wind from wave 7 drifts bursts and shells, shown by smoke trails and flags. Every 5th wave is a 'Finale': a huge volley with a rated result (bronze/silver/gold by percentage ignited) that keeps the show varied. After wave 25 a harder 'encore' show begins and mist rises off the lake, softening the reflections.
games.art: A lakeside hill castle at night, in a glass shell. Sky gradient #0B1026 → #1E2A5A, warming to a haze #3B2A4F at the horizon. A castle silhouette on a wooded hill with lit windows #FFC66B flickering in its towers, a village along the shore and moored rowing boats with small lights. The lake mirrors the sky: bursts are drawn a second time flipped, squashed, at lower alpha and broken into horizontal ripple bands. Smoke from previous bursts drifts and is lit by new bursts (tinted puffs). Burst colours: peony red #FF4D6D, chrysanthemum gold #FFD166, willow amber #F4A261 with long drooping trails, crossette cyan #4CC9F0, palm green #80ED99, strobe white. Glow comes from pre-rendered radial sprites drawn with additive blending. HUD: a row of castle pennants along the battlements that unfurl one per shell toward the quota, matchsticks for sparks at the bottom-left, three beacon braziers for lives, and the score in a frosted glass plaque with a warm rim.
games.audio: Music: a festive 120 bpm loop of warm brass-like synth stabs (detuned saws through a lowpass), glockenspiel and soft timpani, ducking under big chains. SFX: launch whistle (rising sine with vibrato), burst crack (noise burst + lowpass sweep + low boom delayed by distance), crackle (sparse granular clicks), chain notes climbing a pentatonic scale per depth, a crowd 'ooh/aah' (formant-filtered noise swell scaled by chain size), a fizzle for duds, beacon lost (a brazier hiss and a gentle descending bell).
juice: Chain notes climb the pentatonic scale per depth, so a 15-chain plays a cascading melody
The whole sky and water brighten with each burst; big chains wash the screen in coloured light
A 10+ chain triggers 0.4 s slow-mo and a crowd roar, with a floating ×depth counter that grows
Bloom ignitions flash a white starburst ring and a small camera kick
The quota pennants unfurl one by one with soft pops, and clearing a wave launches a celebratory salvo
games.teach: Wave 1's shells rise in a tight cluster and pause dramatically at the apex while a ghost finger taps the centre one, and the chain fills the quota in one go. The second wave lets the player do it. The apex glow is introduced visually on wave 1 by the ghost tapping a glowing shell.
games.scenes: art: seed 7 at a Finale, no HUD. A sky full of gold willows and cyan crossettes reflected in the lake, lit smoke drifting past the castle towers. shot1: seed 3 at 6 s with HUD, shells rising, the first burst expanding, the pennant row 4/9 unfurled and 1 match left. shot2: seed 9 at a scripted 14-chain mid-propagation with slow-mo, the ×14 counter and the crowd 'aah' moment.
games.feasibility: Low risk. Shells are parametric arcs; bursts are expanding circles; chain checks are circle contains point. Particles use the kit's pool: cap each burst at 40-60 particles (half with reduced motion), draw glow with pre-rendered sprites, and cap total live particles around 1200. The reflection redraws only the glow sprites flipped at 25% alpha, not the whole scene. Waves come from a seeded generator with a solvability rule: the quota is set from a precomputed best-chain search (try igniting each shell at its apex in simulation and take the best 2-spark result × 0.7), so every wave is fair. Test hook: lose() spends all braziers; state() exposes wave, sparks and quota. test.cjs uses the solver to play waves and asserts quotas are met and scores add up.

games.title: Riposte
games.pitch: A shadow-puppet sword duel. Swipe against each strike to parry, then cut back through the opening.
games.hook: A bandit puppet rears back with its rods shaking, and you swipe across the blow just as it lands. The screen rings with a metallic 'shing', the bandit staggers and a glowing seam opens in its armour. Two quick swipes along the seam and the paper tears with light pouring through from the lamp behind the screen. One duel teaches you to wait, read and answer.
games.loop: A front-on duel against one articulated shadow puppet on a backlit paper screen; your own sword is a silhouette puppet blade in the lower right that swings to match your swipes. Every enemy attack telegraphs with a wind-up pose (4 frames of anticipation) and a shake of its rods: a strike from the left, from the right, an overhead chop, a low sweep, a thrust, or an unblockable grab. Swipe AGAINST the strike to parry: across from the side it comes from, upward against an overhead chop, and low across the bottom third of the screen against a sweep. Tap to turn a thrust aside. Swipe down to duck a grab. A parry within 300 ms of impact blocks; a PERFECT parry within 120 ms of impact staggers the foe and opens a 1.5 s riposte window in which your swipes land cuts, and cuts along the glowing seam in the puppet's armour do double damage. Stamina is your parry budget: every parry costs a little, a swipe with nothing to parry costs more, and it refills while you hold still, so mashing exhausts you and a drained duellist cannot parry at all. Taking a hit costs one of 3 vermilion seals; losing all 3 ends the run. A foe is beaten when its paper is torn through, and it rips in two and drops off its rods. The gauntlet is 12 seeded foes built from five types and their variants: bandit (plain swings, the teacher), spearman (long reach and delayed thrusts that bait early parries), twin daggers (two-hit chains from alternating sides), ogre (slow, crushing blows and feints that stop short), and archer (arrows you bat aside with taps while it closes in). Foe 12 is the paper-dragon boss, whose body segments attack in sequence like a chain of separate duellists. Between foes choose 1 of 2 sword-guard charms, with at most 3 slots (a 4th replaces one): Crane (perfect window +40 ms), Tortoise (parries cost half stamina), Fox (riposte window +0.5 s), Koi (seam cuts deal triple), Ember (the first hit from each foe is ignored), Moth (every thrust can be parried with a tap anywhere). Score = damage dealt + perfect parries x combo + a no-hit bonus per foe.
games.controls: One thumb: swipe against an incoming strike to parry (the direction matters), tap to turn a thrust aside, swipe down to duck a grab. During a riposte window, swipe anywhere to cut, and along the glowing seam for double damage. Keyboard: arrows parry or cut in that direction, Space turns a thrust, Down ducks.
games.progression: The gauntlet runs in a fixed shape with seeded scripts: foe 1 bandit, 2 spearman, 3 twin daggers, 4 archer, 5 ogre, then six variants that remix their patterns (a masked bandit who feints, a spearman who chains thrusts into sweeps, daggers that switch sides mid-chain, an ogre who grabs), and the paper dragon at 12. Each foe's attack script is seeded per run, so foes keep their personality but never their exact rhythm. Beating the dragon starts the Night Gauntlet: the same twelve with faster wind-ups, shorter perfect windows and mixed scripts, scored on top. The run (foe number, seals, charms) is saved at the start of each foe, and progress shows 'Foe 7 of 12'. Best = foes defeated plus score.
games.art: A lamplit puppet theatre, front-on. The whole play area is a warm saffron paper screen (#f3c46b at the centre falling to #e08a2e at the edges) with visible paper fibre and a gentle flicker in the backlight, framed by a carved dark-wood proscenium (#2a160c) and deep indigo tasselled curtains (#1d2340). Puppets are crisp black silhouettes with lacy cut-out patterns in their costumes that let the light through, brass pin joints that glint, and thin rods running down to the bottom edge, held by unseen hands. Coloured gels mark special moves: vermilion (#e0442f) washes behind unblockable grabs and jade (#3fae8a) flashes on perfect parries. Where cuts land, the rice paper tears and glows white-gold from the lamp behind. The paper dragon is a long chain of jointed segments with fringed cut-paper whiskers. Silhouettes are cheap to draw beautifully, which is why this is feasible. HUD: health as 3 vermilion seal stamps top-left, stamina as a brush-stroke bar along the bottom that dries to grey as it is spent, the 12 foes as small puppet heads on a rod across the top, and charm slots as three round sword-guards beside it. Shell theme: paper theatre (rice-paper panels, carved wood frame, indigo tassels).
games.audio: Music: taiko-like drums (sine pitch drops plus noise slaps) and a shamisen-like plucked synth (Karplus-Strong with a sharp attack and a buzzing bridge), with a breathy bamboo-flute sine lead, at 96 bpm rising to 120 for the dragon. During every wind-up the music drops to a single heartbeat drum, so the tell is also heard. SFX: a metallic parry 'shing' (FM bell with fast decay), a brighter 'shing' with a gong-like tail for perfect parries, a wooden rod rattle as the tell, a paper tear (bandpassed noise rip) for each cut, a slash whoosh, a cloth rustle for ducks, a falling flute sigh when stamina runs out, a paper crumple and drum roll when a foe is torn through, and a low formant growl for the dragon.
juice: Perfect parry: 100 ms freeze, the backlight flares white, a jade gel flash and a vermilion spark at the point of contact
The seam glows and pulses through the riposte window, and each cut leaves a tear that glows white-gold from the lamp behind
A beaten foe rips in two, drops off its rods and scatters paper scraps that flutter down the screen
Taking a hit jolts the screen, ripples the paper and cracks one seal stamp
Low stamina dries the brush stroke to grey and the player's blade puppet droops
games.teach: Foe 1, the bandit, only strikes from the left at first, slowly, with a ghost swipe arrow drawn across the path of the blow. The first parry is always perfect-timed by the ghost, which opens the seam, and the ghost then swipes along it. The thrust tap is taught by the spearman and the duck by the twin daggers' first grab, each with one ghost. The only text is 'Swipe against the blade'.
games.scenes: art: the paper dragon coiling across the backlit screen with one segment torn and glowing, the player's blade puppet mid-parry with a vermilion spark, no HUD. shot1: foe 1, the bandit mid wind-up with its rods shaking, the seal and stamina HUD. shot2: the ogre staggered after a perfect parry, its seam glowing, two gold tears in its armour and two charm slots filled.
games.feasibility: Low-medium risk, about 1800-2400 lines. Each foe is a jointed rig of 6-9 rods (paths with pin joints) driven by forward-kinematic angle keyframes per pose, with the anticipation, strike and recovery poses tweened. Attacks are a seeded script of {type, direction, wind-up ms, impact time}, so every duel is deterministic. The parry test compares the swipe angle with the strike direction (within 50 degrees) and the swipe time with the impact time. Cuts are segment tests against the seam polyline. The screen and frame are pre-rendered once; tears are small additive sprites. Test hook: Arcade.test {start, lose, state}; ?debug window.__game {start(seed, foe), step(ms), parry(dir), thrust(), duck(), cut(dir, onSeam), lose(), state()} with the upcoming attack script in state(), so a perfect-parry bot clears foe 1 deterministically and a passive bot loses.

games.title: Thimblekeep
games.pitch: A mouse knight with a needle sword. Swipe to dash-strike through a castle of beasts.
games.hook: Swipe and the little mouse zips across the floorboards in a silver streak, cape snapping, slicing a beetle right as it winds up. Hit-stop, a 'shing', shell bits everywhere. It is crunchy and heroic on the very first swipe.
games.loop: Rooms are single-screen, top-down chambers inside a castle's walls, seen at mouse scale (giant floorboards, buttons, spools, crumbs, candle stubs). MOVE = DASH: a swipe sets direction and length (up to 180px). The mouse dashes along it, damaging every enemy on the path (1 damage, or 2 plus a white flash on a PERFECT hit that catches an enemy during its glinting wind-up). Dashes are invulnerable. There is a 0.25s recovery, and chained dashes build a combo that heals a sliver at 10. A short TAP does a spin-parry that hits adjacent enemies and deflects projectiles. Obstacles like spools and thimbles stop dashes. Mousetraps snap if you end a dash on them (shown armed with a glint). ENEMIES all telegraph with a red flash and a 0.6s wind-up: beetle (a straight charge), spider (drops from above with a shadow marker and shoots slowing web), wasp (circles, then dives), rat brute (armoured front, so hit from behind), centipede (only the head is vulnerable, segments follow its path), and floor bosses (cat paw slamming from the screen edge with a growing shadow and a whisker sweep, where you dash to the nose when it peeks in; a crow; a tom rat carrying a candle stub). Clearing a room swings open two doors, each showing a reward icon (cheese heal, key, bead coins, relic chest, or a shop thimble) so you choose your path. A floor is 6 rooms plus a boss. RELICS (12) change play: thread spool (dashes leave a cutting trail), button shield (blocks one hit per room), pepper seed (perfect hits burn), bell (enemies stun on room entry), and more. Health is 3 cheese wedges. The run ends at zero.
games.controls: One thumb. Swipe anywhere: direction and length set the dash. Tap to spin-parry. Keyboard: arrows/WASD dash a fixed medium distance in that direction (diagonals combine), Space spin.
games.progression: Five floors with their own palette, enemies and boss: Pantry (beetles, a crow boss), Sewing Room (spiders, pins as hazards, the cat paw), Library (centipedes, falling books, an owl), Chimney (wasps, ember floors, a soot rat) and Attic (everything, lit only by warm candle pools with dim moonlit gaps between them, then the tom rat). After the Attic, New Moon mode loops with enemy modifiers. Relic synergies and door choices make every run different. Rooms come from 12 hand-tuned layout templates with seeded props, enemy picks and mirroring. The save holds floor, room, health, relics and beads, with Arcade.progress showing 'Sewing Room 4'. The best score is floors cleared plus beads.
games.art: World: a storybook castle at mouse scale. Every actor and prop has a 2px warm-ink outline (#2a1a12) for a picture-book feel. Rooms are lit by candles with warm radial gradients and long soft shadows cast away from the light (props draw a skewed dark shape). Floors use pre-rendered wood grain, rugs and fabric. Palettes per floor: Pantry ochre #e8b04b with jars and crumbs, Sewing Room rose #d9738c with pincushions and fabric weave, Library leather green #3f6b4f with giant book spines, Chimney soot #4a3b3b with ember orange #ff7a2f drifting sparks, Attic moonlit blue #6f86b5 with warm candle pools and dust shafts (never a black mask). The mouse knight is grey-brown with pink ears, an acorn-cap helmet, a red cape that trails as a ribbon on dashes, and a needle sword with a white glint. Enemies are chunky readable silhouettes with shell sheen. HUD: an illuminated-manuscript gold-leaf band at the top, with cheese wedges for health, a bead counter and relic icons in gilt roundels, and the floor map as a vine with leaf nodes. Shell theme: illuminated manuscript, gold leaf on a deep red cloth binding.
games.audio: Music: baroque-flavoured harpsichord (square with fast decay) and a recorder lead at 120bpm, in a minor mode per floor. Boss fights move to 140bpm with timpani (pitched sine drops) and an ostinato. SFX: dash zip (noise sweep), a needle ting (high FM bell), a shell crunch, a perfect-hit 'shing' with hit-stop, a hurt squeak, a cheese munch, door creaks, a trap snap, a web thwip and a cat yowl for the boss telegraph.
juice: Hit-stop of 60 to 90ms on every hit, and perfect hits flash white with a brief slow-mo
Enemies burst into shell bits and dust that stay on the floor until the room changes
The cape trails as a ribbon behind every dash and settles with a flutter
On room clear every candle flares, the doors swing open with dust puffs and the reward icons bob
Boss defeat explodes into a confetti of buttons and beads, with a big screen shake and a fanfare
games.teach: Room 1 holds a single sleeping beetle with a ghost swipe arrow drawn through it. Room 2's beetle charges, so you see a telegraph and dodge with a dash. Room 3 introduces the door choice with icons only. The first perfect hit pops a small star icon so players notice the mechanic. tutorial_complete is tracked on the first room cleared without the ghost.
games.scenes: art: the mouse knight mid-dash with a silver streak and flowing cape, slicing through a beetle in a candle-lit pantry of giant jars, shell bits flying, a spider dangling in shadow. No HUD. shot1: Pantry room with a beetle winding up (red flash), the gold-leaf HUD with cheese wedges and relics. shot2: Sewing Room boss with the giant cat paw's shadow telegraph and the mouse dashing to the nose, beads scattered.
games.feasibility: Medium risk, about 2500 lines, and the largest Adventure build: floors 1-2 and their bosses must be polished and playtested before floors 3-5 are started. Combat uses circle colliders and capsule sweeps along the dash segment, enemies are small state machines (idle, telegraph, attack, recover), and rooms come from 12 templates (under the 30-level limit) with seeded variation. Content is bounded: 5 enemy types, 3 bosses reused with floor variants, 12 relics as small modifiers. The main risk is combat feel, so the brief prioritises hit-stop, telegraphs and i-frames. Test hook: window.__game = { start(seed, floor), dash(angle, len), spin(), step(frames), hurt(99) /* loses */, state() } exposing enemy positions so a bot can dash at them and assert room clears.

games.title: Bramble Cup
games.pitch: Race garden critters in seed-pod karts and pelt rivals with acorns, honey and bees.
games.hook: Five chunky critters in walnut-shell and seed-pod karts burst off the line through a sunny garden. You drag to steer, burst a dandelion-clock item box, the seed packet rips open on an acorn, and you bonk the rabbit ahead with a squeak and a spray of petals.
games.loop: Five racers, 3 laps on a garden circuit generated from a seeded spline, with track width and decor. The camera is a tilted 3/4 diorama view: the world does not rotate and scrolls to follow you, and tall things (sunflowers, tulips, flower pots) stand up with height offsets. Karts always accelerate. Drag from where your thumb lands to set the heading, and releasing holds the current heading. Tapping the seed-packet button uses your item. Dandelion-clock boxes give one of 4 items, weighted by race position: Acorn (thrown forward, bounces off walls twice), Honey blob (dropped behind, slows), Bumblebee (homes on the racer ahead) and Ladybug shield (blocks one hit). Two more, Spring clover (a hop that clears hazards and opens shortcuts over flower beds) and Snail glitter (last place only: a 3 s turbo leaving a slippery trail), are added only if time allows once the first four are polished. Hazards: sweeping sprinklers (telegraphed by a water arc), puddles, crossing snails. Grass off the path slows you. AI follows a racing line with lateral noise and rules for using items. A cup is 4 races scored 10/7/5/3/1. The run ends after race 4 (reason 'win' on a podium, else 'lose'). Score = cup points x 1000 + hits landed.
games.controls: Touch: drag with one thumb to steer by direction, and tap the seed-packet button (bottom right, 64 px) with the other to use an item. Keyboard: arrows to steer, Space for the item.
games.progression: Four seasonal cups of 4 seeded tracks each: Spring (blossom, gentle), Summer vegetable patch (sprinklers, narrow rows), Autumn (leaf piles that hide items and slip you sideways), Winter frost (ice patches, berry boosts). AI pace and aggression rise per cup, and a mirror mode unlocks after all four. Critters unlock with podiums, each with a small trade-off (rabbit: acceleration, badger: weight, hedgehog: shrugs off spins, fox: top speed, frog: quick hop, mouse: tight turns), as do karts (seed pod, walnut shell, pumpkin, teacup). About 20 minutes per full set of cups.
games.art: A storybook garden in soft daylight from the top-left. Spring palette: grass #7cc153 with mowing stripes, soil paths #b07a4a flecked with pebbles, flower beds in pink #ff7eb6, yellow #ffd23f and purple #9b6bd6, foliage #3f8f4a. Dappled leaf shadows from an unseen tree drift slowly across the track. Tall plants lean slightly away from the camera centre for depth. Critters are round, chunky vector characters with ears, glossy eyes and fluttering scarves, in karts with button wheels. Each season swaps the palette and decor: summer bright greens and tomato red, autumn rust and gold with leaf drifts, winter blue-white frost with red berries. HUD styled as garden labels: the position is a numeral on a wooden plant stake, laps are acorn icons, the item slot is an illustrated seed packet that rips open and spins through items like a roulette. Shell theme: seed-packet cards pegged on garden twine.
games.audio: Bouncy folk-pop at 128 bpm: ukulele-like plucks, glockenspiel melody, kick-and-tap percussion. The final lap is 8% faster. Sound effects: kart putter (low pulse), item box puff, roulette ticks, acorn thwip, hit bonk plus a squeak pitched per animal, honey splat, bee buzz (an LFO on a saw), spring boing, mushroom boost pad pop, lap (bird chirp), finish fanfare.
juice: The item roulette ticks and the seed packet bursts open with confetti seeds
A hit spins the kart with orbiting stars, a leaf burst, a squeak and a small shake
Mushroom boost pads squash and stretch as karts bounce over them
An overtake flips the position stake with a wooden clack
On the final lap petals swirl across the screen and the music speeds up
On the podium the critters hop and petal confetti falls
games.teach: In the first race a ghost thumb drags in the track direction at the start, the first item box glows with a ghost tap on the packet button, and the first rival ahead is slow and easy to hit. Track tutorial_complete after the player first hits a rival with an item.
games.scenes: art: a diorama view of a spring garden track with a hedgehog in a walnut kart throwing an acorn at a rabbit, a bee chasing a frog, sunflowers and dappled shadows, no HUD. shot1: the start grid with five critters and the stake and seed-packet HUD. shot2: an autumn track with leaf piles, the item roulette spinning and position 2.
games.feasibility: Medium risk: it has the most systems in the set. Hold scope to 4 items (2 more only if time allows), 5 racers for clear position sorting on a phone, and simple circle-and-projectile logic, one physics model (heading, speed, grip), and AI that targets a lookahead point on the racing line with item rules. Tracks are seeded splines checked for self-intersection, with seasons done as palette and decor swaps instead of new art sets. Draw sorted by y for the 3/4 look and pre-render plant and critter sprites per season. Test hook ?debug exposes window.__game { start(seed, cup, race), giveItem(type), steer(angle), bot(true), finishRace(pos), endRun(), state() } so Playwright can run bots through a cup and force a loss.

games.title: Orrery
games.pitch: Turn the rings of a brass orrery. Planets that line up lock together. Bring on the eclipse.
games.hook: You drag the outer ring and its coral planet clicks round the sun, step by step. It lands on the same ray as the jade planet next door and the two lock together with a brass 'tock'. Now they turn as one, and you can see at once that the puzzle is the order you join them in.
games.loop: A brass orrery of 3 to 5 concentric rings around a sun. Each ring has 12 step positions and carries 1-3 planets. Drag a ring to turn it one or more steps; one drag is one move. CONJUNCTION RULE: when planets on adjacent rings land on the same ray, they couple with a brass click, a spoke slides between them, and from then on their rings turn together as one group. Coupling is permanent within a level (undo reverts it), so the order of moves is the whole puzzle. The goal is to put every planet on its marked ray, shown on the outer star chart by a constellation medallion in the planet's colour. Later goals ask for a full syzygy instead: every planet on one ray, which brings on the eclipse. Later elements: a counter-turning ring (geared to its neighbour, so turning it turns the neighbour the opposite way), moons that orbit their planet one step per move (and can couple rings through their own conjunctions), and a comet that crosses one ray each move and uncouples anything it passes. There is no fail state: undo and restart are unlimited, and stars are given at par, par+2, or solved. If the current state can no longer reach the goal, the sun dims and the undo button pulses.
games.controls: One thumb: press on a ring and drag around the sun; it snaps to steps with a tick and commits on release. Undo and Restart buttons sit at the bottom within thumb reach. Keyboard: Up/Down select a ring, Left/Right turn it one step, Z undoes, R restarts.
games.progression: Charts 1-8: 3 rings, place 2-3 planets, couplings simple. Charts 9-16: 4 rings. Charts 17-24: counter-turning rings. Charts 25-32: moons. Charts 33-40: syzygy goals. Charts 41-50: comets and 5 rings. Chart 51 onward is endless with mixed elements. Every 10th chart is an eclipse chart with a syzygy goal and the full eclipse payoff. Generation: random rings, planets and targets from seed+attempt, then a BFS for the optimal par (the state is ring offsets, coupling flags, moon phases and the comet's step, at most 12^5 times the flags, under 1M reachable states with pruning). A chart is accepted when par sits in the band for its tier and a greedy move-toward-target solver fails, so the order genuinely matters. The run is saved, and progress shows 'Chart 18'. Best = charts solved, plus total stars.
games.art: No nebula at all. The whole screen is an astronomer's star chart on cream vellum (#f1e6cc) with ink hatching (#2a2a3a) and constellation lines in gold leaf (#b8892b). The orrery sits at the centre: engraved brass rings (#c9a24a with tick marks at the 12 steps), enamelled planets on brass arms (lapis #2f5aa8, coral #e0644f, jade #3f9e7c, later amber #e3a83a and plum #7a3f6e), and a gilt sun with a soft warm glow. Target rays are fine dotted ink lines running out to constellation medallions on the chart's edge. A coupling is drawn as a brass spoke bridging the two rings. Moons are small pearl beads; the comet is an ink-drawn streak with a gold head. During an eclipse the sun dims into a pale corona, the vellum tones down to sepia and the chart's stars glint gold. HUD: a brass cartouche at the top with the chart number in Unbounded, moves against par as small brass pins, and star slots as gold-leaf stars. Shell theme: astronomer's vellum with brass rule borders. Dark mode is night vellum (#2a2620) with the gold ink glowing.
games.audio: Music: a 76 bpm loop of harpsichord-like plucks and a soft music box over a low organ drone (stacked sines). SFX: a clockwork tick per step (short filtered noise clicks), a brass 'tock' on coupling followed by a pitched chime (each ring has its own note in a pentatonic chord, so a solution sounds as a chord), a reverse whirr on undo, a muffled chime when the goal becomes unreachable, and on an eclipse a swelling choir-like pad (detuned sine stacks) as every coupling chime sounds together.
juice: Rings turn with a little inertia and a ratchet click per step, settling with a slight overshoot
Coupling: the brass spoke slides in with a spark and both planets flash
A planet reaching its target ray glints and its constellation medallion lights in gold leaf
Eclipse solve: the sun shrinks to a corona, the chart darkens to sepia and fills with gold stars as the full chord rings
Undo spins the rings back with a soft reverse whirr and the spoke slides out
games.teach: Chart 1 has two rings with one planet each; one ring needs a single turn to reach its target, and a ghost hand drags it. Chart 2 teaches coupling: turning the inner ring first locks it to the outer and ruins the goal, so the ghost shows undo and then the right order. The only text is 'Drag a ring'.
games.scenes: art: a 5-ring orrery at the moment of eclipse, the sun a pale corona, enamelled planets lined up on one ray, gold-leaf constellations across the vellum, no HUD. shot1: Chart 1 with the cartouche HUD and the ghost drag. shot2: Chart 27 with moons, a counter-turning ring, two brass couplings and a planet one step from its target.
games.feasibility: Low-medium risk, about 1600-2200 lines. One step(state, ring, steps) function is shared by play, the BFS solver and the tests, so they cannot disagree. The BFS uses a packed integer state and a typed-array visited set, with a 1M-state cap and a 400 ms generation budget per chart; seeds over the cap are rejected. The 'unreachable' check reuses a capped BFS spread over frames. Rings are pre-rendered per radius and rotated with a transform; the vellum and chart are drawn once. Test hook: Arcade.test {start, lose, state}, where lose is a forfeit that calls runEnd with reason 'restart'; ?debug window.__game {start(chart), turn(ring, steps), undo(), solution(), state(), forfeit()}.

games.title: Swellrider
games.pitch: Surf a giant sunset wave. Pump for speed, launch off the lip, spin, and stay ahead of the curl.
games.hook: You drop down the face of a towering wave and feel the speed, sweep back up, and fly off the lip into the sunset, spin, and land as spray explodes; behind you the barrel crashes. One ride shows it all in ten seconds.
games.loop: Side view of a long breaking wave that fills most of the portrait screen. The world scrolls as you ride along the wave; the breaking curl chases you from the left. Your surfer has a position along the wave (x) and a height on the face (h from trough to lip). Drag the thumb up or down to set the board's target height on the face; moving down the face converts height into speed, climbing converts speed back into height ('pumping'), and the wave adds a steady push. If you reach the lip moving fast upward, you launch into the air: hold the thumb to spin (rotation speed increases while held), release to stop spinning; land with the board roughly aligned to the face to score the trick (points by rotation, x2 for a clean landing angle). A bad landing angle is a wipeout. The curl matters: riding just in front of it (inside the shaded 'pocket' zone) fills a multiplier; letting it catch you is a wipeout unless you are low and fast, which becomes a barrel ride (big bonus while it lasts). Hazards along the ride: floating driftwood and kelp near the trough (jump or avoid), a closeout section where the face goes flat (you must pump to keep speed), and gulls at the lip (bonus to fly near). 3 boards per run; each wipeout costs one; score accumulates across rides.
games.controls: One thumb: drag up or down to carve up or down the wave face, hold in the air to spin and release to stop. Keyboard: Up/Down to carve, hold Space to spin in the air.
games.progression: Each ride is a seeded wave with a set length; finishing a ride (reaching the channel as the wave fades) gives a ride bonus and the next wave arrives. Progress is by place and swell, always at sunset: the run travels from a beach break (shoulder-high, slow, forgiving curl) to a reef point (long walls, fast curls, barrel sections) to a rivermouth (shifting peaks, double-ups, driftwood), and then the swells grow (taller faces, more potential speed and airtime, faster curls and closeout sections). Trick variety keeps it fresh: 180/360/540/720 spins, barrel rides, and a combo chain if you land tricks without touching the trough. Best score and longest barrel are kept.
games.art: A tropical big-wave break at sunset. Palette: deep ocean #0A2342 to wave face teal #0E6BA8 to translucent lip #3FC1C9 (the lip glows where the low sun shines through), foam #FFFFFF, sunset sky gradient #FFD166 -> #FF5E5B -> #6A2C70, a huge low sun with a halo, palm silhouettes #1B0F26. Layers: sky with banded clouds lit from below; the location's coastline silhouette (dunes at the beach break, a palm-lined point at the reef, mangroves at the rivermouth), while the sunset palette never changes; the sun and its shimmer path on the flat sea behind; the wave itself drawn as a filled bezier profile with a vertical gradient, light streaks running down the face (scrolling lines), the curl as a pre-rendered spiral with foam particles and spray; whitewater spilling behind the curl. The surfer is a lean silhouette in dark tones with a bright board colour (#FFB703), drawn with poses for carve, crouch, air and wipeout; board leaves a spray trail. HUD: surf-wax stamp style - the score at the top in a chunky outlined type on a sticker-shaped badge, boards left as three little surfboards, the pocket multiplier as a curling wave meter, trick name replaced by a rotation icon (e.g. a 540 shown as one and a half arcs). Shell theme: surf-wax stickers with sunset-orange outlines on deep-ocean panels.
games.audio: Music: warm surf-rock-meets-chillwave loop at 108 BPM - reverby twangy pluck lead (Karplus-Strong with spring-reverb-like delay), driving tom groove, mellow bass; a breathy pad rises during barrel rides. SFX: carving spray (filtered noise that follows speed), pump (soft whoosh), lip launch (rushing air), spin whoosh per half turn, clean landing (deep splash with a bright crack), wipeout (big crash of noise and a bubbling underwater muffle), barrel (low hollow roar with resonant filter), gull cry (pitched chirps), board lost (sad descending tone).
juice: Lip launch: hit-stop 4 frames at takeoff, the camera pulls back and the sun flares behind the surfer
Clean landing: spray explodes, screen shake 3px, rotation icon and points pop on the sticker badge
Barrel ride: the screen darkens at the edges into the tube with light at the end, time slightly slows and the bonus counter climbs
Wipeout: the surfer tumbles in whitewater, the screen goes blue and bubbly for a moment, a board on the HUD floats away
Pocket multiplier: the wave meter fills with glowing foam and the surfer's spray trail turns gold when maxed
Ride complete: the surfer kicks out over the back of the wave and the next set rises on the horizon
games.teach: The first wave is small and slow; a ghost thumb shows drag down then up, and a dotted curve on the face shows the ideal pump path for the first few seconds. The first time you approach the lip fast, a ring pulses at the lip. One-line hint: 'Drag down for speed, up to fly'.
games.scenes: art: the surfer high in the air above the glowing lip mid-spin, sun behind, the curl breaking with spray, no HUD. shot1: carving down a tall face with the curl close behind, pocket meter filling and the sticker score. shot2: a barrel ride inside the tube at the reef point with the bonus counter, the sunset glowing through the lip.
games.feasibility: Risks: modelling the wave and the riding feel; the most ambitious of the set. Mitigation: the wave is not fluid simulation: its profile is a fixed parametric shape (height, steepness) scrolled in x, and the rider lives in (x, h) coordinates with a 1D energy model (speed from height loss, push from the wave, damping), plus a ballistic air phase and a rotation angle. The curl is a moving x position with a seeded speed curve. Rendering uses pre-rendered gradient strips for the face and pooled spray particles. Test hook: start() starts set 1, lose() wipes out all boards, and ?debug autopilot (follow an ideal pump curve) lets test.cjs check that a good rider completes a wave, tricks score, the curl wipes out an idle rider and best score saves.

games.title: Sunken Bell
games.pitch: Two-thumb pinball on the deck of a sunken galleon: wake the octopus, ring the ship's bell, start the multiball.
games.hook: A coin-gold ball cracks off a brass cannon slingshot, pings between coral-crusted bumpers and clangs the great ship's bell at the top of the table with a deep 'BONG' that shakes the screen. Then a tentacle uncurls from the captain's cabin and snatches your ball.
games.loop: Three balls per game on one hand-designed table that fills the portrait screen: the deck of a sunken galleon. Launch: drag down on the anchor-chain plunger and release, and hitting the lit top porthole lane gives a skill shot. Two flippers plus a small upper-right flipper. Features: three coral-crusted pop bumpers, two brass cannon slingshots, a bank of 3 treasure-chest drop targets (clear it to raise the Fathom multiplier and light the left kickback), a ship's-wheel spinner in the right orbit, top porthole rollover lanes 1-2-3 (flippers shift the lit lane; completing them adds a bonus multiplier), left and right orbit loops round the masts, the ship's bell at the top (the jackpot target: three rings light the Bell Jackpot), and the captain's cabin sinkhole where the octopus lives. Shooting the cabin once wakes the octopus. Each later shot locks a ball in a tentacle, and 3 locks start 'Ink Storm' multiball (3 balls, jackpots on the cabin and the bell). 'Plunder' is a 30 s mode lit by 10 bumper hits in which bumpers are worth x5. A ball save covers the first 8 s of each ball, and an extra ball comes at score thresholds. Draining all balls ends the game.
games.controls: Two thumbs: touching the left half flips the left flipper and the right half flips the right and upper flippers. Drag down on the lower-right plunger area to pull and release to launch (a quick tap auto-launches at medium power). Keyboard: Z and / or Left/Right Shift for the flippers, Space or Down to plunge.
games.progression: Within a game, modes stack and the score climbs through Fathom multiplier levels (x1 to x5). Completing Ink Storm and Plunder and clearing the chests twice lights 'Bell Tolls', a wizard-style 45 s mode in which the bell rings with every jackpot, every target glows and the galleon visibly lifts on the seabed. After each wizard mode the wreck settles at a new angle: the plankton lane pattern and bumper colours shift, and a hidden lane opens through a hull breach behind the left cannon. The DMD celebrates milestones with dot-matrix animations. Best score persists.
games.art: The deck of a sunken galleon at night, seen from above. Palette: deep teal-black water (#06222a), weathered oak planks (#5a3d26) with barnacle clusters and rope coils, verdigris brass (#6fa58f) on the cannons, bell and fittings, and coin gold (#ffcc4d) for the ball, treasure and jackpot glints. Coral growths in pink and orange crust the bumpers, and torn rigging and a broken mast frame the upper table. Light comes from bioluminescent plankton (drifting cyan specks that chase along the lane guides when lit) and the galleon's lantern swaying on the mizzen boom, whose warm pool moves slowly across the deck. Caustics are toned down to one faint scrolling layer near the top only. The octopus (#8e5be8) lives in the captain's cabin with glowing eyes and animated tentacles that curl around locked balls. The ball is coin-gold with a stamped-crest glint and a soft shadow. HUD: a dot-matrix display across the top, amber #FFB000 on #1A0F00, drawn as a grid of dots with a code-defined 5x7 digit and icon font (score, balls, mode icons, small animations), so no words are needed. Shell theme: pixel-style DMD.
games.audio: Music: a shanty-flavoured 116 bpm loop with a squeezebox lead (square and saw with vibrato), a round bass and creaking-timber percussion. Modes switch to their own stems: Ink Storm gets a darker, driving minor groove and Bell Tolls a triumphant full mix with the bell on the downbeats. SFX: flipper clack (short noise plus thump), bumper 'bloop' with a coral crunch, cannon sling boom (low thump plus noise), chest drop clunk with a coin jingle, wheel spinner ratchet (rapid clicks at spin rate), porthole rollover ding, cabin suck (descending glide), octopus grab (squelch), the bell (an inharmonic FM 'BONG' with a long tail), multiball start (a triple bell ring), drain (low wobble with bubbles), ball save (sparkle), jackpot fanfare.
juice: Bumpers recoil and flash, throwing coral chips and a bubble burst with a 40 ms hit-stop on big hits
Bell strike: the bell swings, a shockwave ring spreads, a short screen shake and the plankton flare across the deck
The DMD plays dot-matrix animations for jackpots, mode starts and extra balls
Octopus lock: tentacles curl around the ball, ink clouds bloom and the screen dims briefly
Drain: the ball sinks with a sand puff and a soft slow-mo, then the bonus count-up ticks on the DMD
games.teach: The first ball auto-launches after 3 s if the player does nothing, with ghost thumbs pulsing on both halves and the flippers glowing. Ball save is generous on ball 1 (15 s). The cabin, the bell and the chests blink with chasing plankton lights, so the player can see what to shoot without reading.
games.scenes: art: seed 7 in Ink Storm multiball on the galleon deck, no HUD (DMD hidden): three balls in flight, the octopus mid-grab, the bell swinging and the lantern pool sliding across the planks. shot1: seed 3 at 6 s with HUD, a ball rising off the left flipper toward the chests, the DMD showing the score and ball 1. shot2: seed 9 at a scripted Bell Tolls start, the bell mid-ring, every target lit and the DMD jackpot animation playing.
games.feasibility: Highest risk in the set; contained by scope. The table is data: polylines, circles and arcs for walls and features, defined in one array. Physics runs 120 Hz fixed steps with 4 substeps (480 Hz). Ball speed is clamped so per-substep travel stays under 40% of the ball radius, which prevents tunnelling. Flippers are rotating capsules with angular velocity, and contact impulses use the contact-point velocity (w x r) plus restitution. There are no ramps or layers, so everything is one plane. Pre-render the static table art. test.cjs runs 20k simulated steps with a random-flipping bot across seeds and asserts the ball never leaves the table polygon and never gets stuck (no position change over 3 s triggers an auto-nudge, which is also a shipped safety feature). Test hook: Arcade.test {start, lose, state}, where lose drains all balls and state exposes balls, mode and score. Deterministic: the launch power and seed fix the opening.

games.title: Cinderwing
games.pitch: Ride a dragon through a storm sky. Hold to fly, let go to breathe fire on airships.
games.hook: You swoop up beside a fat cream gas bag, lift your thumb, and the dragon rears and roars a stream of fire. Seconds later the envelope goes 'fwoomp', the whole airship lights up and sinks with tiny crew parachuting out.
games.loop: Free-flying portrait sky arena with drifting cloud layers. Hold your finger: the dragon flies toward it (offset above the thumb) with gliding momentum. Lift your finger: the dragon hovers, flapping, and breathes a flame cone in the direction it was last flying, with a gentle aim assist (up to 25 degrees toward the nearest burnable part). Breath drains a gauge that refills while flying. While breathing you are nearly still and vulnerable, so every attack is a commitment. Airships are made of 6-14 segments (gas cells, wooden hull planks, rigging, cannon decks). Each segment has heat: flame raises it, and burning segments spread fire to their neighbours over time. Gas cells explode, and an airship falls when half its lift is gone. Crew run to beat out fires (watch fires shrink), so you need to light several segments. Threats: harpoon cannons (a muzzle glint, then a straight shot), flak bursts (a growing ring marks where they pop), gyro-copters that chase. 3 scale-hearts.
games.controls: One thumb: hold and move to fly, lift to breathe fire. Keyboard: arrows fly, hold Space to breathe.
games.progression: Saved campaign of procedural sorties ('Sortie 7'). Each sortie is a seeded convoy of 3-5 waves ending with a dreadnought (several linked envelopes, cannon decks, a captain's bridge that must burn last). There are no trait cards: the dragon grows from what it burns. The airship part you set alight last in each sortie decides the growth: gas cells give a bigger breath gauge, cannon decks harden its scales, rigging lengthens the flame cone, hull planks make fire spread faster, and the bridge earns an ember trail while flying. Every growth is visible on the dragon (a new horn, a wing-membrane pattern, scale plating, a glowing throat stripe, an ember tail), so after a few sorties your dragon looks like your play style. Weather changes per sortie (storm sunset, rain that dampens fire, lightning that refills breath on a near-miss, night with searchlights). Losing ends the campaign and keeps the best sortie reached, plus a portrait of that run's grown dragon on the title screen.
games.art: Storm-sunset sky with real depth: a teal storm ceiling (#0f3b46) that breaks to a blazing tangerine sun band (#ff9f43) and soft peach highlights (#ffd6a5). Four parallax layers of pre-rendered volumetric clouds (stacked soft blobs with lit tops and shadowed bellies), distant mountain spires poking through, rain streak layers in storm sorties. Airships are cream canvas envelopes (#efe2c4) with stitched panel lines, brass gondolas (#b08d57) and red pennants; burning sections char to #3a2a20 with glowing seams. The dragon is emerald (#1e8a5a) with a gold belly, membranous wings lit from behind (translucent orange at the edges) and a throat that glows molten before each breath. Fire is additive orange-yellow particles that turn into drifting grey smoke. HUD: brass and leather. The breath gauge is a curved horn on the left edge filled with glowing embers, scale-hearts are 3 dragon scales, and the score sits on an engraved brass plaque. Shell theme: riveted brass and oiled leather straps.
games.audio: Adventurous 6/8 at 120 BPM: timpani-like toms (sine pitch sweeps), horn-like detuned saw pads, pizzicato triangle ostinato, cymbal swells on wave starts. The dreadnought adds a low brass ostinato and faster drums. SFX: a roar that opens each breath, a crackling flame loop (bandpassed noise), a big 'fwoomp' gas-cell ignition, creaking timber, cannon thumps, a harpoon whistle tell, wing-flap whooshes.
juice: Gas cell ignition: bloom flash, shock ring, burning canvas scraps flutter down
Throat glow and a 120ms anticipation rear before each breath
Sinking airships trail smoke columns and tiny parachuting crew
Dreadnought kill: slow motion, multi-stage explosions, strong shake, haptic pulse
Wing flaps squash the body; near-miss harpoons leave a whistle and a speed-line. After a sortie the dragon roars and its new growth draws on in a sweep of embers
games.teach: The first airship is a lone unarmed blimp straight ahead. A ghost hand drags toward it and then lifts with a flame icon. Fire spread is visible at once. The second ship has crew putting fires out, which shows that one spot is not enough. Harpoon tells appear on wave 2 with an exaggerated glint.
games.scenes: art: the dragon breathing a fire stream into a burning dreadnought against the tangerine storm break, no HUD. shot1: sortie 1, a blimp with two segments burning and the ember horn gauge half-full. shot2: a rain sortie with flak rings, a copter chasing, and an airship sinking in smoke.
games.feasibility: Medium risk. Fire spread is a tiny graph per ship (segments with heat and neighbour lists), cheap and deterministic. The particle cap is 400, with smoke drawn as pre-rendered soft sprites. Clouds are pre-rendered once per weather to offscreen layers and scrolled. The dragon is the highest-risk drawing, so it is drawn and reviewed first, before any content. The spec is a body spine of 8 circles following a head (snake-follow), two polygon wings driven by a flap sine, and a tail tip and head polygon drawn with gradients, plus 5 optional growth overlays (horns, membrane pattern, plating, throat stripe, ember tail). Aim assist keeps release-to-breathe fair. Debug hook: window.__game {start(seed, sortie), step(ms), hold(x,y), release(), lose(), state()}.

games.title: Hoolock
games.pitch: Swing a gibbon arm over arm up a misty jungle canopy to greet the morning sun.
