games.hook: Hold and the gibbon's long arm snaps onto the glowing branch. It swings, you let go at the top of the arc, and it flies up through a shaft of golden light to the next branch, with the whoosh rising in pitch. A satisfying, flowing grab-and-fling in the first two seconds.
games.loop: A vertical seeded jungle climb in portrait, scrolling upward through layers: forest floor and river, understory, canopy, emergent crowns, then the sunrise sky. GRAB: hold anywhere and the gibbon grabs the nearest grab point within arm reach (90px). The target branch shows a glowing ring before you press, so you always know what you will catch. SWING: while holding, the gibbon is a pendulum on the arm. Sliding your finger left or right leans (pumping energy at the bottom of the arc), with energy capped. RELEASE: let go to fly ballistically. HAND-OVER-HAND: grabbing again within 0.35s of releasing counts as a brachiation chain, which raises speed and the score multiplier, with a rising pitch ladder. Grab points include branches (solid), vines (flexible, a longer pendulum), rotten branches (crack after 1s with a cracking sound and a darker colour), temple ledges and bells (ringing one opens a stone gate in the Temple biome). COLLECT: figs and rambutans (score), and lost baby gibbons that cling to your back (each adds +1 multiplier and a little extra weight). HAZARDS are telegraphed: thorn vines (red tips), snakes on branches (head bob before a strike), hornet nests (a buzz cloud that patrols), eagle swoops (a shadow, then a dive) and waterfall spray (slippery grabs). FALLING more than 1.2 screens below your highest grip, or into the river, costs a fig-heart, and you respawn on the last safe branch. 3 hearts. Each biome ends at a giant emergent tree crown where the gibbon sings, a checkpoint and a fanfare. The run continues upward until hearts run out. Score = height + fruit × multiplier.
games.controls: One thumb. Hold anywhere to grab the highlighted branch, slide left or right to lean and pump, release to fling. Keyboard: hold Space to grab, Left/Right to lean.
games.progression: Biomes in order, each about 8 screens: Riverbank (wide gaps, no hazards), Fig Giant (vines, rotten branches), Temple Ruins (stone ledges, bells and gates, snakes), Waterfall Cliff (spray, slippery grips, hornets) and Storm Canopy (wind gusts that push mid-flight, eagles, and slow-rising floodwater below that keeps the pace up). After that the biomes repeat with denser hazards and wider gaps. The generator validates reachability between grab points with a jump envelope, so no seed is unbeatable. Families rescued are a long-term collection (each biome hides a unique one). The best height and fruit score are saved.
games.art: World: a misty layered jungle that brightens toward a sunrise. Back layers are hazy silhouettes in #2f5d50, #4f8a6e and #8cc7a1 with atmospheric fade. God-ray shafts of #ffd27a slant from above, with drifting pollen motes. Foreground giant leaves (monstera and palm shapes in #0f2b22 with rim light) pass in front for depth. Higher up the palette warms and lightens, so the top is a sunrise sky of #ffb36b to #ffe7a8 with a sun disk and bloom. Temple Ruins add mossy carved stone #9a9a7a with gold bells. The waterfall is animated white strokes with spray mist. The gibbon has dark fur #3a2b24 with a white brow ring, long arms done with 2-bone IK to the grip, and a fur sway on its body. Babies cling to its back. Fruit is glossy with highlights. HUD: a carved wooden plaque at top with the height counter in Unbounded, a climbing vine along the right edge with a leaf marker for progress to the biome top, fig-hearts and family silhouettes. Shell theme: jungle green with carved wood and leaf borders.
games.audio: Music: marimba, log drum and kalimba (plucks) in a 3-against-2 polyrhythm at 108bpm. Layers add as you climb (shaker in the canopy, a flute-like sine lead in the emergent crowns). Biome tops play a gibbon song: sliding sine 'whoop-whoop' glissandi that rise in duet. SFX: a grip slap, a whoosh whose pitch tracks flight speed, branch creak and snap, fruit pop with juice splats, a combo pitch ladder, a river splash, a hornet buzz (detuned saws), a snake hiss and an eagle cry.
juice: Releasing near the apex gives 0.15s of slow-mo with speed lines and a whoosh
Each hand-over-hand grab raises the pitch and makes the leaf marker on the vine jump
Fruit bursts into juicy droplets with a pop and a floating multiplier number
A rotten branch snaps into wood chunks with a camera nudge, and the gibbon flails briefly
At a biome summit the gibbon sings, the sun breaks through in a golden bloom and birds scatter
games.teach: You start hanging from a branch. A ghost hand shows release, then hold, with the next branch close and glowing. The first gap needs one release at almost any timing. Lean is taught on the first wider gap with a left/right ghost slide. tutorial_complete is tracked on the first 3-grab chain.
games.scenes: art: the gibbon mid-flight with arms spread through a golden god-ray, misty canopy layers below, a baby on its back, figs glinting and the sunrise above. No HUD. shot1: Riverbank with the gibbon swinging on a glowing branch, the next grab ring highlighted, the plaque HUD and the height vine. shot2: Temple Ruins with stone ledges and a gold bell, a snake on a branch bobbing its head, and a 4x chain counter.
games.feasibility: Low risk, about 1800 lines. Pendulum physics is a distance constraint with gravity, and the grab search is a nearest-point query over a spatial bucket list. The generator places grab points in rows with a reachability check (jump envelope from the swing speed range), so it is deterministic per seed. Background layers are pre-rendered tall strips. Test hook: window.__game = { start(seed), grab(bool), lean(x), step(frames), fall() /* empties hearts, loses */, state() } exposing the current and next grab points so a bot can climb.

games.title: Mare Moto
games.pitch: Ride a moon bike over craters, flip in low gravity and land clean to boost.
games.hook: The first crater rim launches you into a slow, floaty arc with Earth hanging huge in the black sky. Holding a thumb spins the bike into a backflip, a green landing arc appears under the wheels, and you touch down clean: a slow-motion puff of dust, a chime and a rocket boost past a rival.
games.loop: A side-view race over a 1.5-2 km course of seeded lunar terrain made from a segment grammar: rolling regolith, crater rims as ramps, rille gaps, boulder fields and abandoned lander ramps. Four riders. The bike always throttles. Hold the left half to lean back (wheelie on the ground, backward rotation in the air) and the right half to lean forward. Gravity is about 1/6 tuned so jumps last 1.5-3 s. Landing: within 35 degrees of the slope you land, and within 12 degrees is a clean landing. Each full rotation completed before a clean landing banks boost (1 flip = 1 s, 2 flips = 2.5 s, 3 flips = 4.5 s), fired automatically on landing. More than 35 degrees off, or the helmet touching ground, is a crash: bike and rider tumble apart in dust, then respawn at the last checkpoint flag after 1.5 s. Rival riders replay deterministic bot rides generated with the course. The run is a points tour with a time cut-off: a crash never eliminates you, it costs the 1.5 s respawn and your banked boost, and your times add up across courses. Each course awards tour points by position, and the tour has a cumulative cut-off time that tightens each course; the run ends (reason 'lose') when your total time misses the cut-off. Score = tour points + flips and clean landings; best = courses survived.
games.controls: Two thumbs: hold the left half to lean back or backflip, the right half to lean forward or frontflip. Throttle is automatic. Keyboard: Left/Right arrows or A/D.
games.progression: An endless tour of 60-90 s courses, with the cut-off clock shown between courses as a mission-time readout. Rilles get wider and need boost to clear, boulder fields get denser, and 'mascon' zones of heavier gravity (shown as a faint violet shimmer) change jump arcs. Every fourth course is an earthshine night course lit only by your headlamp and Earth. Rivals get faster and flip more. Flip totals unlock two more bikes (a light flipper that spins fast but lands harder, and a heavy hauler with forgiving landings) and suit colours. Picking between a safe ride and a greedy double flip for boost is the hook that keeps runs going.
games.art: Stark lunar landscape. Black sky #050507 with a fine starfield. A huge Earth (#3d8bd9 oceans, swirling white clouds, soft terminator) hangs in the upper third. Hard low sunlight from one side: lit ground #cfcfc8, shadow #4a4a48, and long black shadows cast by boulders and crater rims (offset polygons). Parallax layers: distant flat-grey mountains, mid crater rims with antennas and dome habitats, the foreground terrain with craterlets (ellipse pairs, a rim highlight and an inner shadow) and scattered rocks. Dust plumes rise and fall in slow ballistic arcs with no drag. The bike is a chunky white rover-moto with orange #ff7a1a panels and gold foil. The rider wears a suit with a gold #f2b33d visor that reflects a tiny Earth. HUD styled as mission placards: orange-on-grey blocks with rivets, a mechanical flip counter whose digits roll, and the boost meter as a cylindrical O2-style gauge. Shell theme: a lunar module panel with rivets, crinkled gold-foil texture (procedural) and toggle-switch buttons.
games.audio: Minimal space-funk at 110 bpm with a filtered slap bass, sparse drums and synth beeps that sound like radio chatter, muffled as if heard through a helmet. Sound effects: a low muffled square engine, landing thump (sine pitch drop), a clean-landing chime plus a radio double-beep, flip ticks rising in pitch with each rotation, crash (crunchy low-passed noise and a bump), boost (rocket hiss).
juice: A clean landing slows time for 0.15 s and bursts a ring of dust that hangs in low gravity
The flip counter ticks and rises in pitch with each full rotation
Earth glints across the visor at the top of each jump
A crash bounces the helmet, scatters bike parts in slow arcs and shakes the screen
Boost lights a rocket flame and motion streaks
An overtake pops the rival's rider number off with a beep
games.teach: Course 1 opens with a gentle ramp. During the first airtime a ghost thumb holds the left side, and a landing arc under the bike shows the safe angle in green and the clean angle brighter. Track tutorial_complete after the first clean landing with at least one flip.
games.scenes: art: the rider mid-backflip above a crater rim with Earth behind, a dust plume hanging, and a rival on the ground below, no HUD. shot1: the start gate with four riders, the placard HUD and the flip counter at 0. shot2: a double flip over a rille gap with the landing arc showing, the boost gauge filling and position 2.
games.feasibility: Low to medium risk. No rigid-body solver: the bike is a point mass plus an angle. On the ground, sample the terrain height under two wheel offsets and set the angle from the slope. In the air, motion is ballistic plus angular velocity from input, and the landing check runs on contact. Terrain is a polyline sampled every 8 px and generated in chunks from a seeded segment grammar, with chunks baked to offscreen canvases. Rivals replay bot rides simulated at course generation. Test hook ?debug exposes window.__game { start(seed, course), setInput(l, r), bot(true), crash(), finish(pos), state() } so Playwright can ride a course and force a loss.

games.title: Crease
games.pitch: Fold patterned paper along its creases until the top matches the target card.
games.hook: Swipe across a crease and the paper follows your finger: it lifts, foreshortens, shades and flips over to show its other side, with a crisp snap. Folding feels physical from the first touch.
games.loop: The sheet is a grid of squares (2x1 at first, up to 5x5), each with a front face and a back face (colour plus a block-print motif). A fold is a swipe across any crease line inside the current outline: the part on the side where the swipe started flips over onto the other side. Its cells are mirrored across the line, their stacking order reverses, and each shows its other face. The flap may overhang, so the outline becomes the union. The target card, pinned at the top right, shows the required outline and the top face of each cell. You win when the current outline and top faces match the target, normalised for position. Each folio has a fold budget equal to the generator's minimum; once it is spent no more folds are allowed, but undo and restart are unlimited, so there is no fail. Later chapters add directional motifs (waves, arrows, cranes) that mirror when folded, so the target also requires the right orientation. The data model: a dictionary keyed by cell coordinate holds a stack of cell records {id, faceUp, flipX, flipY}, and a fold reflects coordinates, reverses the moved stacks onto the destination, and toggles faceUp and the mirror flag. Generation: a random paper pattern and k random valid folds (no no-ops) give the target. A BFS over fold sequences of length below k (memoised by canonical state) rejects puzzles with a shorter solution, so the budget is tight. Any sequence that reaches the target wins.
games.controls: One thumb: press on the paper and drag across a crease; the flap follows the finger (scrubbing the fold angle) and commits past halfway, or springs back. Crease lines highlight as the finger nears them. Buttons for Undo and Restart. Keyboard: arrows choose a crease, Enter folds from the selected side.
games.progression: Folios 1-8: 2x1 to 3x3, solid two-colour sheets, 1-2 folds. Folios 9-20: 4x4 with 3 folds. Folios 21-32: two-tone front patterns. Folios 33-44: directional motifs. Folios 45-60: 5x5 with 4-5 folds. Folio 61 onward is endless with mixed rules. Every 10th folio is an 'unfold' variant: the sheet starts folded and you open it to match a flat target, using the same model in reverse. The run is saved, and progress shows 'Folio 17'. Best = folios solved.
games.art: A paper-maker's table in soft window light from the left. The background is a linen texture (#efe6d6) with pre-rendered fibres and a long soft shadow from a window frame, with a wooden ruler and a bone folder lying at the edge. Paper faces use block-print colours: vermilion #e2452f, indigo #233a6b, ochre #d99a2b, moss #6e8b3d, ink #1c1c1c and cream #f6efe2. Motifs are drawn as simple vector patterns (waves, dots, chevrons, leaves, stars), each with a subtle paper-grain overlay. The folding flap is drawn per cell as transformed quads: coordinates are scaled by cos(theta) toward the crease, a darkening gradient grows with lift angle, the back face shows when cos(theta) < 0, and a soft cast shadow falls on the base sheet. Crease lines are faint embossed lines that darken once used. HUD: red seal-style stamps for the folio number, and the fold budget shown as small paper-crane outlines that fill in as folds are used. The target card is clipped to a little wooden peg. The menu shell has torn-paper edges and string ties. Dark mode is a lamplit night table: charcoal linen (#24201c), a warm lamp pool, and paper colours slightly deepened.
games.audio: Music: a sparse 72 bpm loop of plucked-zither tones (Karplus-Strong) over a soft breathy pad (noise through a bandpass), in a pentatonic scale with long reverb-like tails made by feedback delay. SFX: a paper swish (bandpassed noise whose gain and cutoff follow scrub speed), a crease crunch on commit (a short crackle of noise clicks), a reverse swish on undo, a wood-block knock when cells match the target, and on solve a crane-wing flutter (rapid amplitude-modulated noise) plus a zither flourish.
juice: The flap follows the finger live, foreshortening, shading and flipping to its back face at 90 degrees
Committing a fold snaps with a crisp sound, a faint dust puff along the crease and a haptic tick
Matching cells flash on the target card as they come right, so progress is visible
On solve the folded packet lifts, morphs into a paper-crane silhouette that flaps away across the screen, and a seal stamps the folio
An over-budget attempt makes the crane counters wobble and the undo button pulse
games.teach: Folio 1 is a 3-second tutorial: a 2x1 strip, red on the front and blue on the back, with an all-blue single-square target. A ghost hand drags across the one crease and the fold completes the folio. Folio 2 is a 2x2 needing two folds, and its target card shows the outline clearly.
games.scenes: Art: a flap mid-fold at about 70 degrees, casting a shadow on the linen sheet, with a paper crane flying off, and no HUD. Shot1: Folio 1 with the target card on its peg, seal stamps and ghost drag. Shot2: Folio 36, a 4x4 directional-motif sheet after two folds, with crane counters and matched cells flashing on the target card.
games.feasibility: Build order: the finger-following fold scrub and the 2x1 single-fold tutorial are prototyped first, because the scrub is the hook. The fold data model is the crux and is fully specified above. It is pure grid logic and deterministic, so it is easy to unit-test in test.cjs. Fold rendering is a per-cell affine squash with shading, which is cheap for at most 25 cells and needs no 3D. The BFS shortest-solution check branches over at most (creases x 2 sides) per step, with depth 4 or less and memoisation, which is fine. Normalise both outline and faces by their bounding-box minimum before comparing. Test hook ?debug: __game.start(folio), .fold(axis, index, side), .solution(), .state(), .forfeit() (runEnd 'restart'). Estimated 1600-2300 lines.

games.title: Otterstone
games.pitch: Curling on a frozen lake with otters. Push the stone, then scrub the ice to steer it home.
games.hook: Your thumb pushes a granite stone out of the hack, it glides away, and when you rub the ice in front of it two otters in scarves sweep furiously and the stone keeps going and slides right onto the button. Rubbing the screen is tactile and funny from the very first throw.
games.loop: Portrait sheet with the house (target rings) at the top; the camera follows the stone. Throw: before the throw, tap a curl toggle (stone handle turns clockwise or counter) to choose which way it curls. Then put your thumb on the stone and push it up the ice: the stone moves with your thumb inside a delivery zone, and when you lift the thumb the release speed and direction are taken from the last 100 ms of movement. Physics: the stone decelerates by a friction constant; it curls sideways in the chosen direction, more as it slows. Sweep: while the stone is moving, rub the thumb back and forth across the ice just ahead of it; rub speed lowers friction (the stone travels farther) and slightly straightens the curl; the otter sweepers mirror your rub. Collisions: stones are equal-mass discs with elastic-ish collisions (restitution 0.85), so takeouts, raises and chips work. Match: 4 ends; each end the two teams alternate 3 stones each (6 total). Scoring as in curling: the team with the stone nearest the button scores one point per stone closer than the opponent's best. The opponent team is an AI that picks a shot type (draw, guard, takeout) by simple rules, solves the required release speed analytically from the friction model, and adds noise based on its skill. AI throws play at 2x with a tap to skip.
games.controls: One thumb: tap the curl toggle, push the stone up the ice and let go to throw, then rub the ice ahead of the stone to sweep. Keyboard: Left/Right choose line, hold Space to build speed and release to throw, tap Space rapidly to sweep.
games.progression: A bonspiel: a bracket of 8 animal teams on a lakeside map. You play the quarter-final, semi-final and final, each on a different lake along the shore, and the bracket's other results (simulated) decide who you meet. Teams: beavers, badgers, hares, foxes, owls, moose, lynxes and a polar bear crew, each with a skill level (aim noise, sweep strength) and a personality (guard-heavy, takeout-heavy, aggressive draws). Lakes change the ice: keen glassy ice (low friction, big curls), heavy snowy ice, a lake with a frozen-in log the stones bounce off, frost patches that slow stones, and a moonlit night lake with cabin windows glowing on the shore. Losing a match knocks you out of the bonspiel; winning the final starts a harder bonspiel with re-seeded teams. The bonspiel and the current match are saved between visits. Score = points from ends won, plus bonuses for takeouts, double takeouts and stones on the button. Best bonspiel score is kept. Pass-and-play 2-player: two people share the phone, alternating stones and each sweeping their own.
games.art: A frozen alpine lake in golden afternoon light. Palette: ice #CFE8F2 with cool shadow blue #6C8EAD and painted house rings in scarlet #E4572E and cobalt #2F6DB5, warm sunlight #FFD8A8 on snowbanks, birch trunks #EDE6DA with charcoal marks, a pine treeline #2F4A3A, distant peaks in lilac #A99BC8. Layers: a mountain range with a soft gradient sky; a pine forest band; snowbanks along the sheet edges with spectators (other animals) bobbing; the ice surface with scratch textures and a pre-rendered pebbled sheen that catches a moving specular highlight; long afternoon shadows from stones and otters. Otters: chunky brown #7A4E2D bodies with cream bellies, whisker strokes, red scarves #E4572E and knitted hats, animated with squash-and-stretch sweeps. Stones: granite discs with speckle texture, team handle colours (your team red, the rival's colour by team). HUD: a carved wooden scoreboard on a post at the top (end numbers burnt into wood, scores as chalk tallies) and stones remaining as little stones on a knitted mitten at the bottom-left. Shell theme: curling-club tartan with enamel team badges.
games.audio: Music: cozy folk waltz at 96 BPM in 3/4 - plucked triangle-wave 'mandolin' melody, an accordion-like square pad with slow vibrato, a soft upright bass; a calmer, sparse variant plays while the stone is sliding so sweeping sounds stand out. SFX: delivery push (grainy noise scrape), stone glide (low continuous rumble whose pitch follows speed), sweeping (rhythmic bright brush noise synced to rubs), otter squeaks when sweeping hard (short pitched chirps), stone clack (sharp hard click with resonance), takeout (two clacks and a crowd 'ooh'), end won (bell chime), match won (spectators cheering - layered noise bursts).
juice: Sweeping: the otters' brooms kick up ice dust particles, the stone's glide rumble rises in pitch and a speed shimmer appears ahead of the stone
Takeout: hit-stop 5 frames on contact, the struck stone spins away with sparks of ice, camera shake 3px
Stone stops on the button: rings pulse outward from the centre, otters do a belly slide celebration
Measuring: at the end of an end, a measuring tape animates from the button to the two closest stones, then the points tally onto the wooden board
Match win: snow flurry, spectators throw hats, and the bracket on the lakeside map draws your line through to the next round
games.teach: End 1 of the first match is against a sleepy beaver team. The first throw shows a ghost thumb pushing the stone; when the stone is moving, a ghost thumb rubs ahead of it with the hint 'Rub to sweep'. A faint target ring marks where a perfect draw would stop for the first two throws only.
games.scenes: art: low angle along the ice toward the house at golden hour, a red stone gliding with two otters sweeping in a cloud of ice dust, rival stones in the house, no HUD. shot1: mid-end aiming state with the curl toggle and a ghost of the line, wooden scoreboard visible. shot2: a double takeout at the moment of impact with sparks, then the scoreboard tallying.
games.feasibility: Risks: rubbing gesture detection, AI quality, and the slow pace. Mitigation: sweeping uses the total distance the pointer moves per 100 ms inside a sweep zone ahead of the stone, which is easy to measure and to drive from Playwright; physics is discs with a closed-form friction model, so the AI can solve the required release speed exactly and then add noise (no search needed); AI throws run at 2x speed and are skippable. Content is 8 teams x 5 ice presets by data, no levels. Test hook: Arcade.test start() begins the bonspiel quarter-final, lose() forfeits the match, and ?debug throw(speed, angle, curl) plus sweepFor(seconds) let test.cjs check draws, takeouts, scoring per end and saved progress.

games.title: Croakback
games.pitch: A bullfrog sings a rhythm. Tap it back on your lily pads before the heron gets close.
games.hook: The bog grooves from the first frame. The big frog's throat balloons and booms a 4-note riff, you tap it back on two glowing pads, and your frog booms in time with the bass. Getting it right adds a new instrument to the swamp's song, so every success sounds better.
games.loop: A backing groove (bass + shaker) loops continuously at the current tempo, so the beat is always felt. Play alternates call and response bars. CALL: the lead bullfrog at the top croaks a seeded phrase of 1-2 bars over two voices, low 'BRRUM' (left pad) and high 'rib-it' (right pad). Each note also lights a stepping-stone marker on a curved row of stones spaced by time, so it can be read visually as well as heard. RESPONSE: the same span of bars follows, and you tap the phrase back on the left and right lily pads at the bottom. Each expected note has a window relative to the response bar's beat grid: ±70 ms Great, ±140 ms OK, outside that a miss. Extra taps count as slips. Later phrases add both-pads chords and hold notes (hold until the throat sac deflates). A clean phrase scores per note × combo, adds a music layer (pad, then counter-melody, then chorus frogs, up to 4 layers) and pushes the heron back one step. A phrase with any miss moves the heron one step closer through the reeds. At the third step it strikes, your frog plops underwater and the run ends. Every 8 phrases comes a 'Chorus': the full bog sings the last phrase together with a firefly swarm, then the tempo rises.
games.controls: Two thumbs: left lily pad (low croak) and right lily pad (high croak). Both pads are large, about 40% of the width each, near the bottom. Keyboard: F and J (or Left and Right). Hold notes use a press and hold.
games.progression: Phrases come from seeded rules (density, subdivision and syncopation budgets per tier), so they never repeat in a run but are fair. Tier 1: quarter notes on one voice at 88 bpm. Then mixed voices, then eighths, rests and syncopation, then two-bar phrases, chords, triplets and holds. Tempo ramps per Chorus to 140 bpm. The night progresses visually (moonrise, fireflies multiply, then dawn mist at high tiers). Bests are tracked for score and longest clean streak.
games.art: Moonlit bog in a mossy wood shell (lily-pad green panels with bark edges). Sky #0D1B2A → #1B263B with twinkling stars, and a moon #F1E9C9 with a soft halo whose long reflection streaks shimmer on the black-green water #0A2A2E. Tree-line and reed silhouettes #081C15 sway gently; fog bands drift in two parallax layers. Lily pads #2D6A4F/#40916C have a pale rim light #95D5B2 and ripple rings when struck. The lead bullfrog is olive #6B8F3A with golden eyes #F4C430 and a translucent throat sac #E9F5DB that inflates with a glow on each note. The player frog is emerald #2EC4B6 and mirrors the inflation. Fireflies #F7F48B are additive glow dots wandering in curl-noise paths. A grey-blue heron silhouette #5C677D lurks in the reeds and steps closer with each missed phrase, its eye glinting; every step throws its long shadow across the moon's reflection on the water, so the threat is impossible to miss. HUD: the score is etched on a floating leaf at the top-left, lives are 3 fireflies in a glass jar at the top-right, and the call/response state shows only as the stepping-stone row lighting amber (call) or green (you).
games.audio: The sequencer runs the bog groove: a sine-sub bass, a noise shaker, plus up to 4 unlockable layers (warm pad, kalimba counter-melody, choir-like 'ooh' formant pad, rim clicks). Croaks are synthesised: low = a pitched-down square with formant filter and a fast pitch drop, high = a two-blip FM chirp. All notes are scheduled on the AudioContext clock with lookahead. SFX: Great (a soft sparkle on top of the croak), miss (a dull plop), heron step (reed rustle + low cello-like note), Chorus (all frogs + firefly shimmer), heron strike (whoosh + splash).
juice: The throat sac visibly inflates and glows on every croak, yours included, and ripple rings spread from the pads
Each clean phrase adds an audible new music layer and a burst of new fireflies
Great hits throw a ring of firefly sparks from the stone, and combos above 16 make the moon reflection pulse
The heron steps closer with a slow camera push-in, the reeds part and its long shadow slides across the moon's reflection, which builds tension
Chorus: every frog sings together, the camera pulls back to show the whole bog lit by a firefly swarm, and the score counts up
games.teach: The first call is two low croaks; during the response a ghost thumb taps the left pad exactly on the stones, then the second phrase waits for the player. Stones and pads share colours (amber left = low, teal right = high), so the mapping is learned visually without words. The first three phrases cannot move the heron.
games.scenes: art: seed 7, no HUD. The bullfrog mid-croak with a fully inflated glowing sac, moon reflection, fireflies swirling and the heron silhouette half-visible in the reeds. shot1: seed 3 at 6 s with HUD, a response bar in progress, 3 stones lit green, the player frog croaking. shot2: seed 9 at a scripted Chorus: all frogs singing, a firefly swarm, the score count-up and the 4-layer music state visible as glowing reeds.
games.feasibility: Medium risk: timing. Use AudioContext.currentTime as the master clock and map pointer events (performance.now) to audio time through a measured offset. Judge taps against the response grid with an adaptive latency correction: the median signed error of the last 12 Great/OK hits, clamped to ±150 ms, which absorbs Android WebView output latency. Offer a 'tap along' calibration in the pause menu as a fallback. Phrases are data (an array of {beat, voice, len}) from a seeded generator, so test.cjs can read the expected times via state() and inject perfect, late and missing taps through a debug hook to assert the scoring windows, heron steps and run end. lose() triggers the heron strike. Reduced motion: no camera push.

games.title: Ratel Rumble
games.pitch: A honey badger holds the savanna road. Tap a side to smack what comes from it.
games.hook: A jackal runs in from the left, you tap left, and it cartwheels off the screen with a thwack and a dust puff. Five seconds later both sides are coming and you are in a rhythm.
games.loop: The badger stands in the centre of a side-view road, and enemies arrive from the left and right at different speeds. Tap the left half to strike left and the right half to strike right. A strike only lands inside a fixed reach zone (a trampled grass ring on the ground). Hitting an empty zone means a 0.35 s stumble, so mashing is punished. Swipe down to burrow for 0.6 s (dodges anything overhead). Enemies: jackal (1 hit), hyena (2 hits, knocked back between them), cobra (rears in the zone; only strike when the hood is open, because striking while coiled gets you bitten), vulture (its shadow grows on the ground, then it dives; burrow or strike in the 150ms as it lands), mongoose pair (two fast hits on the same side). Taking a hit costs one of 3 honey jars. The honey badger twist: a cobra bite plays 'venom nap', 1.2 s of wobbly dizziness, then 6 s of 'Unbothered' fury (double reach, one-hit kills, saturated colours), so a bite hurts but pays back. Honeycomb falls from a tree now and then; strike it to refill a jar. Score is kills times combo, and the combo resets on a whiff or a hit.
games.controls: Tap the left or right half of the screen (two thumbs or one). Swipe down anywhere to burrow. Keyboard: Left/Right arrows strike, Down burrows.
games.progression: Pressure is continuous, from enemy speed, side switches and mixed queues; the seeded spawn script tightens every 20 s. A boss arrives every 60 s: the lion pounces (its shadow arcs overhead), you burrow, it lands past you and shows its flank, then you hammer that side. Later bosses: leopard (feints from both sides) and an elephant charge (burrow at the exact beat). Time of day moves from golden hour to dusk to moonlit night as you survive, which is both a progress marker and a visual reward. Best score and longest combo are saved.
games.art: Savanna at golden hour in flat cut-paper layers: a huge low sun disc, sky gradient #ffb347 to #ff6f3c to #7a2e4d, three parallax ridges of acacia silhouettes in deepening plum, an ochre road (#c8803a) with grass tufts and a heat-shimmer band. Characters are chunky silhouettes with one warm rim-light edge from the sun. The badger is black with a bold silver-white back stripe (#e8e4da), oversized claws and a stubborn squint. Enemies have distinct shapes: lanky jackal, hunched spotted hyena, upright banded cobra with a big hood, vulture with a shadow drawn on the ground. Night stage: indigo sky (#2b1d4a) with a big moon and drifting seed-fluff caught in the moonlight. HUD: a carved wooden signpost holding 3 honey jars, and a combo of claw-mark tally scratches that get deeper with the count. Shell theme: linocut print (ink texture, ochre rice paper, rubber-stamp numerals).
games.audio: A percussion-led groove at 112 BPM: synthesised kick, shaker noise, a marimba-like triangle with fast decay, a plucked bass. Fury mode adds a distorted lead and doubles the hats. SFX: a thwack (noise burst plus low sine) pitched up with combo, a different yelp per enemy, a cobra hiss tell before the hood opens, a wobbly detuned slide for the venom nap, a honey slurp, a dirt-scuff for burrowing.
juice: 50ms hitstop on every strike; enemies ragdoll off screen in spinning arcs
Dust puffs and grass blades on strikes and burrows
Venom nap: screen sways, hue rotates, the badger snores a 'zzz' bubble, then wakes in an orange fury glow
Combo tally scratches carve in with a crunch; every 25 a big punch-scale flash
Boss lion landing shakes the screen; its flank opening flashes white
games.teach: The first 6 enemies are jackals that alternate sides slowly, with a pulsing hand icon on the side they come from. The first cobra comes alone with its hood tell exaggerated. Vulture shadows and the burrow swipe are introduced with a down-arrow ghost the first time. No text beyond 'Tap the side'.
games.scenes: art: the badger mid-strike with a jackal flying off and a cobra rearing on the other side, giant sun behind, no HUD. shot1: early run with a hyena knocked back and the claw tally at 12. shot2: fury mode at dusk with saturated colours and the lion pouncing overhead.
games.feasibility: Low risk: play is 1D and fully deterministic from a seeded spawn script, and hit tests are distance-in-zone checks. The main risk is animation quality. Characters are built from a few shapes (ellipse body, capsule limbs, head polygon) animated by a tiny pose-tween system with 3-4 poses each (idle, strike, hurt, fly), plus squash and stretch. This rig is the quality bar for the game: every strike, the badger's and every enemy's, gets 4 frames of anticipation before it lands, and every enemy has its own silhouette (lanky jackal, hunched hyena, hooded cobra, broad-winged vulture, low twin mongooses), so the cut-paper art never reads as a template. The background is pre-rendered once per time of day to offscreen layers. Debug hook: window.__game {start(seed), step(ms), press('L'|'R'|'D'), lose(), state()} so a bot can play perfectly from the spawn queue.

games.title: Driftwork
games.pitch: Kick off walls in zero-g through a dark derelict station and turn its lights back on.
games.hook: Your astronaut grips a rail in a dark module. Drag back and release, and they sail across in a perfect straight line, turning slowly, until a gloved hand clangs onto the far rail. It feels like real weightlessness. Slotting the first fuse makes the room's lights flicker on in a wave.
games.loop: A station is a seeded graph of 4 to 9 modules (rectangular and cylindrical rooms 1 to 1.5 screens tall) linked by hatches. Unpowered modules are dark apart from your helmet lamp cone and red emergency strips. GRIP: you start holding a rail or wall. AIM: drag back from anywhere (slingshot). A dotted straight line shows your path, including the first wall bounce, and launch power has 3 tiers by drag length. FLIGHT: pure inertia, no gravity. A tap during flight fires an RCS puff that nudges velocity toward the tapped side of the astronaut. You get 3 puffs per flight, refilled on grab. CONTACT: touching any surface below the speed threshold grabs it automatically. Above the threshold you bounce, get stunned for 0.5s and lose O2. Rails and handholds glow when they are in reach. OBJECTIVE: each module has a power panel. Find fuse cells (glowing cubes drifting in that module or a neighbour), carry them by flying through them (they tether to your belt) and touch the panel to slot them. When powered, the module's lights wave on, its hatches unlock and its O2 locker opens. Restore every module and reach the escape pod (a burst of light) to finish the station. O2 drains constantly, faster after bounces and in breached rooms. HAZARDS: sparking cables (arc flicker telegraph), slow-spinning vent fans, breaches that pull you toward the hole in a visible particle stream, tumbling debris and coolant jets that push you sideways. The run ends when O2 hits zero.
games.controls: One thumb. While gripping, drag back and release to launch (a slingshot with a lifted aim line). During flight, tap to puff toward the tap side. Keyboard: arrows aim, hold Space to set power and release to launch, WASD puffs in flight.
games.progression: Station 1 has 4 modules and no hazards. Each next station adds 1 to 2 modules and introduces one hazard type (cables, then fans, then breaches, then debris, then coolant). Station themes rotate: cargo (crates as floating cover), greenhouse (water blobs that splash and slow you, plant tendrils to grab), lab (floating specimen jars and a centrifuge ring), reactor (radiation zones that double O2 drain and glow violet). Later stations need fuses carried through several modules. Score is modules restored × station, plus an O2 bonus. The save holds the station number, restored modules and O2 at the last powered module (the checkpoint).
games.art: World: a dark derelict station orbiting Earth. Windows show Earth's limb as a huge #1f6fd6 to #8fd0ff gradient arc with drifting cloud swirls and a thin atmosphere glow, which washes the interior in cold blue fill light. Interior: grey panelling with rivets, conduits and hanging cables that wobble in zero-g (bezier curves with slow sine offsets). Unpowered rooms are dim, not black: cold blue Earth-light (#1f3f6e) falls through the windows, red #ff3b4a emergency strips trace the walls, and the helmet lamp adds a soft sodium-orange #ff9d3c pool. The signature image is the restore wave: when a module powers up, warm sodium-yellow #ffd27a panels flick on one after another down its length, pushing back the cold blue until the room glows warm white #fff3d6. The astronaut is a chunky white suit with a gold visor reflecting the lamp, a backpack with puff nozzles, and simple 2-bone limbs posed for grip, fly and tumble with slow rotation. HUD: inside the helmet. A curved glass glare sweeps across the top, O2 is an amber segmented readout with a ring gauge, fuses are cell icons, and a small node-graph minimap fills in white as modules light. Shell theme: suit white and signal orange with stencilled markings.
games.audio: Music: slow synth pulse at 76bpm with a heartbeat-like low kick and a lonely sine melody. Each restored module permanently adds a layer (warm pad, then arpeggio, then soft hats), so the station literally comes back to life. SFX: launch (a muffled 'fwump'), a constant soft breathing loop (filtered noise), a rail clang (FM metal), a puff hiss, spark crackles, a fuse click-clunk, a power-up hum rising into a major chord, a breach roar, and O2 alarm beeps that speed up below 25%.
juice: Lights-on: warm sodium-yellow panels flicker on in a wave down the module, the cold blue retreats, and the light reveals floating dust
Grabbing clamps the glove onto the rail with a tiny camera nudge and a metallic clang
A hard bounce stars the visor with a crack sparkle, a short shake and a spinning tumble
Slotting a fuse sends a spark shower and an energy pulse along the conduits toward the panel
Low O2 quickens the breathing and fogs the visor edges
games.teach: You start gripping a rail in a small lit room. A ghost hand drags back, the aim line shows, and the target rail opposite pulses. The second room has a fuse drifting right on the obvious path and the panel blinking. Puffs are introduced when the first bounce would miss: an icon-only prompt says 'tap'. tutorial_complete is tracked on the first restored module.
games.scenes: art: an astronaut mid-flight across a half-lit module, one side warm white and powered, the other cold blue with red emergency strips and an orange helmet pool, Earth's blue limb filling a big window and fuse cubes glowing. No HUD. shot1: station 1 with the astronaut gripping a rail, the aim line with one bounce, and the visor HUD with O2 and fuses. shot2: reactor module with violet radiation zones, a breach pulling particle streams, the astronaut tumbling and the minimap mostly lit.
games.feasibility: Low to medium risk. Rooms are axis-aligned boxes plus circle obstacles, flight is a straight line until contact, and the aim preview is a single raycast with one reflection, so it is easy and deterministic. Lighting is a cold blue tint layer plus additive warm light sprites, with no full darkness mask (Pipistrelle owns that look); the restore wave is a timed sweep of panel sprites. Module layout is seeded tree placement on a grid with hatches. The risk is O2 pacing feeling stingy; tune generously and use lockers as checkpoints. Test hook: window.__game = { start(seed, station), launch(angle, power), puff(angle), step(frames), ventO2() /* loses */, state() }.

games.title: Aurora Pass
games.pitch: Weave night traffic up a snowy pass and reach each lodge before the clock runs out.
games.hook: The run opens at speed on a snowy mountain road under a moving green and violet aurora, with 40 seconds on a split-flap clock. Within seconds you slip past a snowplough's flashing orange lights close enough to trigger a near-miss whoosh, and the road curves into pines lit only by your headlights.
games.loop: A pseudo-3D road made of segments (classic projected-segment renderer with curves and hills, 150 segments visible). The car is always at full throttle. Dragging left or right steers. Speed drops when you run onto the snowbanks, spin on ice patches (less steering, the tail slides) or clip traffic (a 1.2 s spin-out). Traffic drives the same way at varied speeds: sedans, lorries and wide snowploughs, all signalling lane changes with blinking indicators 1 s ahead. Staying 1 s in a vehicle's slipstream pushes speed 15% past the cap. Passing within a hair of a vehicle scores a near-miss, and chains of them add to a combo. The clock starts at 40 s. Each lodge checkpoint adds 30 s, dropping 2 s per stage. After each lodge the road forks: the left branch has more curves and less traffic, the right is shorter with hills and ice. Each stage is generated from the seed, stage index and branch as a sequence of curve/hill 'phrases' with a traffic schedule. The run ends with reason 'lose' when the clock hits zero and the car coasts to a stop, or with 'win' at the eighth lodge, which then continues as an endless night road. Score = distance + near-miss combos + time left at each lodge.
games.controls: Touch: drag horizontally anywhere. The distance from where your thumb landed sets the steering, like a virtual wheel, and releasing centres it. Keyboard: Left/Right arrows or A/D.
games.progression: Eight stages with distinct phrase sets and scenery: pine forest, a frozen-lake causeway, a tunnel lit by orange sodium lamps, a village with lit windows, a windy ridge with blowing snow, a glacier, a hairpin descent and a summit observatory. Forks give 128 possible routes. Traffic density, ice coverage and lane-change frequency rise per stage while time bonuses shrink. After stage 8 an endless mode keeps raising density. Car paints unlock at distance milestones. Route choice, near-miss chains and the shrinking clock keep runs fresh.
games.art: Night in snowy mountains, strictly night and headlight-lit, the opposite of Barnstorm's daylight. Sky gradient from deep blue #0a1530 to teal #12384a at the horizon. Aurora curtains are vertical gradient strips in green #5cf2a8 and violet #b06cff, with sine-displaced edges drawn additively and slowly animated. Snow is #e8f1ff with blue shadows #9fb4d9. Three parallax layers of pine silhouettes and mountain ridges, snow-dusted road edges, orange reflector posts, and a warm headlight pool (#ffe3a3) drawn over the nearest road segments. Lorry taillights bloom red, snowploughs throw amber strobes on the snow, and falling snow streaks toward the camera with speed. The player car is a boxy rally wagon seen from behind, with roof lights and exhaust vapour. HUD styled as a frosted dashboard: a strip along the bottom with an analog speedo needle, the checkpoint clock as split-flap digits that clatter when they change, and frost that creeps in from the screen corners and turns red-tinged when under 10 s. Shell theme: frosted-glass panels with ice-crystal corners and an aurora-gradient title.
games.audio: Ambient synth at 96 bpm in a major pentatonic: bell-like plucked arpeggios, a soft pulsing bass and a pad. Under 10 s it adds a ticking hi-hat and a heartbeat kick. Sound effects: engine hum (oscillator pitched by speed), near-miss whoosh panned to the side of the vehicle, checkpoint (bell chord plus split-flap clatter), ice skid (soft crunchy noise), crash (thud plus glassy tinkle), slipstream (rising wind).
juice: At each lodge the split-flap digits roll up the added seconds with a clatter while the aurora flares brighter
A near-miss bursts snow at the screen edge on that side, plays a panned whoosh and ticks the combo counter
In the slipstream speed lines grow and the camera's field of view widens, then snaps back as you pull out
Hitting traffic spins the camera with a shake and throws a puff of snow
When time is low, frost creeps in from the corners in time with a heartbeat bass
Fork arrows light up in sequence on gantries ahead
games.teach: The game starts already moving. A ghost thumb slides left and right over a wheel icon for 3 seconds. Stage 1 has a wide road and sparse, slow traffic. The first fork shows two huge glowing arrows. Track tutorial_complete when the player reaches the first lodge.
games.scenes: art: behind-the-car view on a curving snowy road through pines, the aurora blazing overhead, a lorry ahead with taillights blooming, snow streaking, no HUD. shot1: start of a run, clock at 40, aurora and an empty road ahead, frosted dash. shot2: the frozen-lake causeway, slipstreaming a snowplough with a near-miss combo, low clock and frost in the corners.
games.feasibility: Low to medium risk. Pseudo-3D segment rendering is a well-documented technique (about 400 lines). Draw sprites far to near per segment. Pre-render trees, lorries and lodges to offscreen canvases at 3-4 scale buckets to avoid redrawing vectors every frame. Portrait needs a narrower field of view: tune camera depth so the road fills about 70% of the screen width at the bottom. Phrases and traffic are seeded and deterministic. Test hook ?debug exposes window.__game { start(seed), steer(x), bot(true), skipToCheckpoint(), forceTimeout(), state() } so Playwright can drive a run and force a loss by timeout.

games.title: Starthread
games.pitch: Drag stars until no threads cross. Untangled, each one becomes an animal.
games.hook: Grab a star and fling it: golden threads stretch like silk, crossings flare red and then fade to gold as they clear. Within seconds you feel the tangle loosen, and the reveal of a whale or fox shape is a real payoff.
games.loop: Each Night is a graph of 6-20 stars joined by threads. Any two threads that cross glow coral-red, with a spark at the crossing; threads with no crossings glow gold. The astrolabe in the HUD shows the live crossing count. Drag any star; it lifts 36px above the finger with a small lens so the thumb never hides it, and threads update live. When the count reaches 0 the night is solved: the stars glide over 1.2 s into the canonical animal figure, its watercolour silhouette blooms behind them, and the animal joins the Star Atlas. A moon-phase badge (3 tiers) is awarded by moves (star pickups) against a par from the scramble size. Later nights add Anchor stars (fixed in place, drawn with a silver ring) and Twin stars (a linked pair that moves mirrored about the screen's vertical axis). Graph generation: start from one of 16 hand-authored animal figures (each 7-16 normalised points with figure edges and an outline index list for the silhouette). Add extra edges greedily from shortest to longest, keeping only those that do not cross existing edges, until the edge-to-vertex ratio reaches the target, so the graph is planar with a known solution. Then scramble the stars to random well-spaced positions, re-rolling until the crossing count reaches the target. Any crossing-free layout wins.
games.controls: One finger drags stars, with generous 26px hit radii and the nearest star picked within 44px. Undo button. Keyboard: Tab cycles stars and arrows nudge the selected one.
games.progression: Nights 1-5: 6-9 stars, ratio 1.2, 2-6 crossings. Nights 6-15: 10-14 stars, with Anchors from night 10. Nights 16-30: 14-18 stars, ratio up to 2.0, Twins from night 20. Night 31 onward is endless at 16-20 stars with mixed elements. Figures cycle through the 16 animals (whale, fox, owl, hare, heron, turtle, stag, bear, cat, koi, butterfly, snail, seahorse, wolf, swan, bee). Each second pass is mirrored or rotated and unlocks a gold variant in the Atlas, so there is a collection goal. The run (night and atlas) is saved, and progress shows 'Night 12'. Best = nights solved.
games.art: A desert observatory at night. The sky gradient runs #0b1033 to #2b2160 to a horizon ember #c46a4a, with a Milky Way band painted as soft noisy gradients across the diagonal. Layered silhouette mesas sit in near-black purple (#1a1230 and #120c22), with a small domed observatory whose window glows warm (#ffcf7a). Wisps of drifting cloud move at low alpha. Stars are pre-rendered cross-flare sprites with a white core and a temperature-tinted halo (blue-white, gold, rose). Threads are gold (#f4c86a), drawn twice: a wide low-alpha glow and a thin bright core. Crossing threads turn coral (#ff5b6b) with spark particles. The solved silhouette is a pale aqua watercolour wash (#9ff0e6 at 25%), pre-rendered from the figure's outline points through a Catmull-Rom smooth with soft blurred edges. HUD: a silver astrolabe ring at the top centre with the crossing count in Unbounded numerals at its hub; its engraved tick ring fills as crossings drop, and the night number sits on a small silver plaque. The menu shell is a desert-night watercolour wash with silver ink (brass and vellum belong to Orrery). Light mode is blue hour: sky #a7c4ec to #f6d7b0, indigo ink threads, coral crossings and lilac mesas.
games.audio: Music: a slow 66 bpm music box of celesta (sine plus inharmonic partial) over a bowed pad in D major pentatonic. Each crossing removed plays the next note of a hidden melody, so the tune emerges as you untangle and the melody completes on solve. SFX: a soft pluck on pickup, a string hum during drags whose pitch follows the stretch of connected threads, a chime for each crossing cleared, a dull tick for each new crossing, and a harp glissando plus choir-like pad (stacked detuned sines) on solve.
juice: Threads wobble elastically after a star moves (a spring on each thread's midpoint control point)
A cleared crossing pops its red spark into gold dust that drifts upward
At zero crossings every thread pulses gold, then the stars swoop into the animal with light trails as the silhouette blooms
A shooting star crosses the sky on solve, with a soft haptic
The astrolabe ring rotates and clicks to each new count, and its ticks light in sequence
Anchor stars thunk and shimmer when you try to drag them
games.teach: Night 1 has 6 stars and only 2 crossings. A ghost hand drags one star across a red thread, the thread turns gold and the count drops; red means bad, which needs no words. tutorial_complete fires on the first self-solved night.
games.scenes: Art: a solved fox constellation glowing with its aqua watercolour silhouette over the mesas and Milky Way, with no HUD; this is the card art and the most giftable image in Puzzle. Shot1: Night 2 mid-untangle with red crossings, the astrolabe showing 3 and a ghost hand. Shot2: Night 18 with a dense 17-star tangle, anchor stars and the astrolabe at 14.
games.feasibility: Very buildable. Crossing checks are O(E^2) with E at most 45, about 1000 segment tests per drag frame, which is cheap. The 16 animal figures are small coordinate arrays (the only authored content), and each includes an outline index list so no hull computation is needed. Generation is planar by construction, so it can never be unsolvable. Twins need care but are simple mirroring. Test hook ?debug: __game.start(night), .crossings(), .moveStar(i, x, y), .solve() (snaps stars to canonical positions), .forfeit() (runEnd 'restart'). There is no fail state by design: the run ends only by solve, restart or quit. Estimated 1500-2000 lines.

games.title: Clean Sheet
games.pitch: Be the keeper in the rain. Read each striker and swipe to dive before the ball beats you.
games.hook: A striker sprints at you under floodlights; you swipe, your keeper flies across the goal, fingertips the ball onto the post and the rain explodes off your gloves. The first save takes three seconds and feels heroic.
games.loop: View from just behind and above the keeper, looking out at the pitch; the goal frame fills the lower screen and the striker runs up in the middle distance. Each shot: the striker runs up (telegraph phase, 0.6-1.2 s) with honest tells: plant-foot direction, hip and shoulder angle, and for early strikers a faint aim glint at the target corner. The ball then travels toward a target point on the goal plane along a path (straight drive, curler with a bezier bend, chip with a high slow arc, knuckleball that shimmies once with a seam flicker shown just before). The player swipes from the keeper in any direction: the keeper dives along that vector (swipe length = dive reach), with a 0.22 s travel to full stretch; a tap keeps the keeper set and catches anything central. At the moment the ball reaches the goal plane, the keeper's glove capsules are tested against the ball: centre of glove = Catch (bonus, keeps combo), edge = Parry (ball spills and may create a rebound shot from a second striker that must be saved too), miss = Goal. Diving early commits you: chips over a keeper who has already dived are goals. Three goals conceded ends the run. Points: save 100 x combo, catch +50, double save (rebound) +200, penalty save +300.
games.controls: One thumb: swipe from anywhere in the direction you want to dive (any angle, length = reach); tap to stay big and catch central shots. Keyboard: arrow keys or WASD give 8 dive directions, Space to set and catch.
games.progression: The run is a gauntlet of matches against seeded rival clubs (generated names avoided; clubs are shown by crest shape and kit colour). Each club sends 6 attacks; between clubs the 'pressure' level rises. Pressure adds: shot types (drives, then curlers at 2, chips at 3, knuckleballs at 4, crossed headers from a winger at 5, deliberate stutter run-ups at 6), shorter flight time (0.95 s down to a floor of 0.45 s), fewer glints, and rain intensity (wet ball: parries spill more often). Every 3rd club ends with a sudden-death penalty round: 3 penalties, each worth 300. One conceded goal is wiped every time you clear a club with zero goals (a clean sheet), which gives the title meaning and a reason to play perfectly.
games.art: A rain-soaked floodlit stadium at night. Palette: deep bottle green #0B2A1F for shadow, striped turf #1E5A3A / #236B44 that glistens with a moving specular sheen, floodlight white-cyan #E8F6FF, sodium spill #FFB46B at the stands, rival kits in crimson #D7263D or other seeded colours, keeper gloves lime #C6FF3D. Layers: black sky with 4 floodlight towers whose lights bloom (pre-rendered radial gradients) and cast cones through rain; stands as stacked silhouettes with flickering phone-light dots and flags; advertising-board band with abstract glowing shapes (no text); the pitch with perspective stripes and puddle reflections of the floodlights; rain as 2 layers of slanted streaks plus splash rings on the turf; mist that thickens near the far end. Keeper: a big-shouldered silhouette from behind with lime gloves and a number-free shirt, articulated for set, dive, stretch and land poses (drawn shapes, tweened). Striker: athletic silhouette with kit colour and a readable plant foot. HUD: stadium LED dot-matrix in floodlight white-cyan #CFF4FF on black (amber dot-matrix belongs to Sunken Bell) - top centre shows saves count and combo as dots; conceded goals as three red cards along the crossbar. Shell theme: floodlit rain, dark green panels with white-cyan LED headings and rain-streaked glass, Figtree body.
games.audio: Music: tense, driving stadium electronica at 128 BPM - a pulsing saw bass on eighths, a four-on-the-floor kick muffled as if heard from the pitch, and a crowd-chant-like pad (vowel formant synth) that swells at pressure 4+. SFX: whistle (sine with vibrato) before each shot, run-up footsteps on wet turf, strike (punchy noise burst with low thump), glove save (crisp slap plus wet splash noise), catch (deep thud), post ping, net ripple (soft noise swish), crowd roar on saves (layered filtered noise rising), crowd groan on goals.
juice: Fingertip save: 8 frames of slow motion as the glove touches the ball, rain droplets freeze and then burst outward, the crowd roar rises
Catch: the keeper pulls the ball into the chest, screen shake 3px, '+150' rises in white-cyan dot-matrix
Goal: the net bulges (mesh of springs), red flash on the crossbar card, camera nudges back
Parry onto the post: a ringing post ping, the ball spins away and a second striker charges in for the rebound
Clean sheet: floodlights pulse in sequence, phone lights sweep across the stand, a conceded card flips back to white

Penalty round: the crowd goes silent, the music drops to just a heartbeat kick. Great saves get a 1.5 s slow-motion replay from a side angle (the camera swings to the post and the dive plays again), skippable with a tap: it is the share moment
games.teach: The first three shots are slow straight drives with the aim glint showing and a ghost hand swiping toward the glint. After the first save on your own, track tutorial_complete. The first chip arrives with a one-shot 'Wait for it' ghost (hand holds still) the first time it appears.
games.scenes: art: full-stretch diving save to the top corner mid-slow-motion, rain droplets frozen, floodlight bloom, no HUD. shot1: striker mid run-up with plant foot visible, keeper set, dot-matrix HUD and three cards. shot2: the side-angle slow-motion replay of a fingertip save to the top corner, rain droplets frozen, with the combo count-up.
games.feasibility: Risks: fairness (a reaction game can feel like guessing) and making the 2.5D shot paths readable. Mitigation: every shot has a seeded target and type chosen before the run-up, and the tells are drawn from that target, so a bot can read them; flight times have a hard floor; glove hitboxes are generous capsules (bigger than drawn). Ball path is a parametric curve on the goal plane plus depth, not physics. Keeper is a small rig of tweened shapes with 5 poses. Test hook: start(), lose() concedes 3 goals, and a ?debug autoKeeper flag that dives at the true target so test.cjs can check that perfect play saves, no input concedes, combos and the clean-sheet refund work. The save replay re-renders the stored ball path and keeper pose track from a second fixed camera. Rain pooled particles; floodlight and stand layers pre-rendered.

games.title: Beakful
games.pitch: Flap over the waves, dive under them: a puffin fishing with a beak full of dangling fish.
games.hook: The first tap makes the puffin flap. Stop tapping and it drops into the sea with a big splash, the music goes muffled underwater, and now tapping swims it deeper. That air-to-water flip is surprising and delightful in the first 5 seconds, and the fish hanging from its beak make you greedy right away.
games.loop: Side-scrolling flight in a portrait frame, with the waterline at about 55% of the height. One rule drives everything: every tap pushes the puffin away from the water surface. In air, gravity pulls it down toward the water and a tap flaps upward. Underwater, buoyancy pulls it up toward the surface and a tap strokes downward. Momentum carries through the waterline, so a fast fall becomes a deep dive and a fast rise launches the puffin out of the water in an arc. Underwater you catch sandeel schools and fish (each adds a fish to the beak, max 10, drawn dangling). Fish only score when banked: every ~700 m a cliff with a burrow ledge appears, and flying into the burrow mouth (a wide target in the air) banks the beak. Banking pays triangular points (1,3,6,10,15...), so carrying more is riskier but worth far more. Hazards: overhanging cliff ledges and gulls (sine flyers, squawk telegraph) in the air; floating driftwood on the surface; rocks, jellyfish (pulsing size) and seals underwater. Seals lunge after a bubble-trail warning. One hit ends the run, and hitboxes are 70% of the drawn size.
games.controls: One thumb: tap anywhere. Keyboard: Space or Up. There is no hold, drag or second gesture.
games.progression: The first 300 m have no hazards and a fish school sits directly in the dive path. Scroll speed rises slowly, and hazard density follows a seeded chunk generator with difficulty tiers. Biomes change by place and weather every 2 burrows, not by time of day: Cliff Colony, then Sea Stacks (arches to dive under), then the Squall, the star of the run, where the swell makes the waterline itself rise and fall, so the very boundary you flip across moves and dive timing changes, then Kelp Shallows (kelp forests that hide fish and slow you), then Plankton Fog (a grey sea fog where the water glows with plankton that light the puffin's wake, and glowing fish are worth double). Rarer catches appear deeper (herring 1, mackerel 2, golden capelin 5). Milestone bests unlock cosmetic scarf colours shown on the title puffin.
games.art: North Atlantic dawn, painterly. Sky gradient peach #F7C9A9 → #9EC3D9 → #5B7FA6 with a low sun #FFE3B0 and soft glare. Three cliff silhouette layers (#46566E, #31405A, #22304A) with tiny nesting birds that flicker, and mid-ground sea stacks with grassy caps #6E8F4E. The water surface is a multi-sine animated line with a foam edge #F4F7F2 and sparkle dashes. Underwater fades #1E6C80 → #0B2D45, with soft diagonal light bands that sway, kelp silhouettes and rising bubbles. The puffin is drawn in code: #1A1A22 back, white face disc, a striped orange-red beak #F26A2E with yellow bands, orange feet, and two-pose wings that become flippers underwater with a bubble trail. Squalls darken everything with rain streaks and a heaving waterline; the plankton fog washes the sky grey and lights the water with plankton glow #7CF5D2. HUD in a weathered driftwood shell (cream #F2EBDD, ink #1F2A3A, puffin-orange accents): the banked score is branded on a weathered plank in the top-left, and the carried fish hang on a string under it.
games.audio: Music: a lilting 6/8 sea jig at 96 bpm with a squeeze-box lead (square + saw with vibrato), a plucked bass and a soft frame-drum kick. While submerged the whole music bus goes through a lowpass (cutoff ~600 Hz), which is a signature detail. SFX: flap (short noise whoosh), splash in and out (noise with downward and upward sweeps), bubbles (sine blips), fish gulp (pitch rises with beak count), gull squawk (FM chirp), seal bark, bank (cascading pentatonic chime per fish), hit (thud + feather flutter).
juice: Entering the water throws a splash crown of particles, a radial screen ripple and the music lowpass sweep
The fish gulp pitch climbs with every fish, and the beak bundle visibly sags as it fills
Banking: fish fly one by one into the burrow, three chick heads pop out, and the score counts up with chimes
Near-miss slow-mo (0.15 s) when the puffin passes within 6 px of a seal or ledge
Hit: feather burst, 80 ms hit-stop, screen shake, the puffin tumbles into the water and floats belly-up comically
games.teach: Before the first tap the puffin hovers on the title with a ghost hand tapping. The first 300 m have one fish school just under the surface, so the player naturally stops tapping and drops in, then a tap shows that it pushes down underwater. The first burrow has a pulsing arrow glyph. No text is needed beyond the one-line hint 'Tap pushes away from the surface'.
games.scenes: art: seed 7 at the Cliff Colony burrow, no HUD. The puffin bursts out of the water with 6 fish dangling from its beak, spray behind, chicks peeking from the burrow, soft light bands below. shot1: seed 3 at 6 s with HUD, the puffin underwater beside a sandeel school, 3 fish carried, a gull visible above. shot2: seed 9 in the Squall, the waterline heaving mid-swell, the puffin banking 10 fish with the count-up mid-way and rain streaks.
games.feasibility: Low risk. The physics is a single point with a sign flip at a waterline function y(x,t) (sum of sines, with a squall amplitude). Obstacles come from seeded chunks (a list of templates with difficulty weights) so every run is reproducible. Collisions are circle vs circle or rect. Pre-render the cliffs and sky per biome to offscreen canvases with parallax. The music lowpass uses one BiquadFilter on the kit's music bus, guarded in case the kit routes music differently. Test hook: lose() triggers a hit; state() exposes depth, beak and banked. A debug autopilot (tap when y is below target) can drive test.cjs to assert that banking adds triangular points and the best score persists.

games.title: Hivewarden
games.pitch: Lead a swarm of bees and mob the hornets raiding your hive, bee by bee.
games.hook: You drag, and a cloud of buzzing bees pours after your finger. You sweep them over a hornet, they clamp on into a glowing ball that heats up and pops it. Your swarm got the kill, not a gun.
games.loop: Top-down meadow with the hive at the bottom centre. You steer the lead bee and the worker swarm (starting at 12) flows after it in a loose flock. Raiders fly toward the hive. When the swarm overlaps a raider, bees latch on one by one and form a heat ball. A raider dies when enough bees are latched: wasp 3, hornet 6, giant hornet 12, shown as a ring of pips around it that fill as bees latch. Unballed raiders sting a bee every second they touch the swarm, and a kill costs 1 bee (the rest rejoin), so attacking with too few is costly. Bees are replaced by gathering: sweep the swarm through flowers to collect pollen (bees glow gold), then fly to the hive to deposit it, which hatches new bees. A raider that reaches the hive steals larvae (hive comb health). Bee-eater birds swoop across with a shadow tell and eat bees in their path, so you have to dodge. Every moment is a choice: gather now or defend, split attention, how big is big enough.
games.controls: One thumb: drag anywhere and the lead bee follows (offset so the swarm stays visible). Tap the hive to recall the swarm. Keyboard: arrows steer, Space recalls.
games.progression: Days of 90 s with a seeded flower layout and raid schedule, and a short honey-count recap between days. New raider types roll in (wasps on day 1, hornets day 2, bee-eaters day 3, giant hornet scouts that mark the hive and call a big raid on day 4). There is no fixed boss rhythm: a hornet nest hangs at the meadow's edge and visibly swells with every raider that escapes alive, and when it is full the giant hornet queen leads a raid with her scouts, so a clean defence delays her. Seasons shift the palette every 5 days (spring, summer, autumn, first frost), with fewer flowers later. The hive grows comb tiers you can see as score rises. Best days survived and best honey are saved.
games.art: A macro meadow at warm midday, like a close-up lens: large out-of-focus flowers and stems in the foreground and background as soft bokeh blobs (pre-rendered blurred shapes), with a crisp middle layer where play happens. Palette: honey gold #f6b93b, leaf green #6ab04c, poppy red #e84a3c, lavender #a689d9, cream #fff3d6, deep shade #2f3b1c. The hive is a carved log with glowing comb inside. Bees are tiny but readable (amber and black striped ovals, flickering translucent wings, a slight bob). Hornets are bigger and orange-black with mandibles and a menacing slow wingbeat. The heat ball glows orange to red with heat shimmer. Sunbeams angle across and pollen motes drift. Seasons recolour grass and flowers (autumn is rust and ochre). HUD: no hexagons anywhere. Swarm count sits on a round wax seal top-left, and hive health is 7 larva cradles on a curved strip of wax that fills with honey. Shell theme: warm amber wax with pressed-flower corners.
games.audio: Pastoral folk at 100 BPM: plucked triangle melody, accordion-like square pad, soft brushed noise snare. Raids shift to minor with tom rolls. The swarm buzz is a chorus of filtered saws whose volume and brightness follow swarm size, so you hear your strength. SFX: a 'tik' per latch rising in pitch, a sizzling heat-ball crescendo, a satisfying pop on kill, a hatch chime per new bee, a sparkle for pollen deposit, a bird call tell before a bee-eater dive.
juice: Heat ball: bees pile on with ticks, the ball pulses red with shimmer, then bursts and bees fan back out
Pollen sweep puffs golden dust and makes the bees glow
New bees pop out of the comb with a tiny bounce and chime
Swarm buzz swells with size; a bee-eater swoop leaves feathers and a gap in the swarm
Giant hornet kill: hitstop, shake, honey splash across the hive
games.teach: It opens with a ghost hand dragging the swarm through a flower cluster and then to the hive (a bee hatches). Then a single slow wasp drifts in with its 3 empty pips, and the hand drags the swarm onto it. No text beyond 'Drag to lead your swarm'. Pips are self-explanatory once you see them fill.
games.scenes: art: a large swarm forming a glowing heat ball around a giant hornet above the log hive, bokeh flowers in the foreground, no HUD. shot1: day 1, the swarm sweeping through flowers with pollen glow and the comb HUD. shot2: an autumn raid with two hornets, one half-balled, and a bee-eater shadow crossing.
games.feasibility: Medium-low risk. Bees use a simplified follow: each bee springs to a jittered slot around a trailing point plus noise, which is O(n) for up to 90 bees and readable, not true boids. Latching parents the bee to the raider at an orbit angle. Bokeh and flowers are pre-rendered offscreen. Bees are drawn as 2 ellipses plus a wing flicker, batched, about 100 per frame on a mid phone. Raid schedules are seeded per day. Debug hook: window.__game {start(seed, day), step(ms), lead(x,y), lose(), state()}, deterministic under step().

games.title: Shutterfin
games.pitch: Dive a living reef with a camera. Snap shy sea creatures before your air runs low.
games.hook: A school of striped fish swirls right into your viewfinder. Tap, and the screen flashes white, freezes, and a polaroid drops into the corner with a two-star stamp. Then you notice a turtle drifting below and your air gauge ticking, and you instantly want to go deeper.
games.loop: Each dive is a seeded vertical reef column about 1 screen wide and 200m deep, scrolling as you descend from the boat at the surface. SWIM: drag works as a relative stick and the diver turns to face the direction of travel. A VIEWFINDER reticle floats about 140px ahead of the diver. SNAP is a tap from a second finger or the shutter button (bottom-right, 64px). The photo score adds up subject inside the reticle (circle overlap), fill ratio (closer is better, too close crops), sharpness (diver speed low), a BEHAVIOUR MOMENT bonus (puffer inflated, octopus colour-flash, manta mid-bank, jelly mid-pulse, eel lunging), and rarity. CREATURES: 25 species (5 per site) built from 8 body archetypes with palette and feature variants. Their behaviours: boid schools that scatter if you rush, shy wrasse that flee fast swimmers, curious turtles and seals that approach if you hover still, octopuses camouflaged until close and then inking, morays in holes, drifting jellies (touch = sting = air loss), lionfish (avoid), patrolling reef sharks (bump if you swim fast near them), and deep anglerfish that you find by their lure in the dark. AIR drains, faster below 60m. Bubble vents refill some. DEPTH darkens the water, so your torch cone becomes the light source. You must SURFACE (reach the boat or a buoy line) to bank your photos. If air hits zero the run ends and unbanked photos are lost. The JOURNAL keeps the best photo of each species (1 to 3 stars) between dives.
games.controls: One or two thumbs. Drag anywhere with the first finger to swim. Tap with a second finger, or tap the shutter button, to snap. A single-thumb player can lift and tap (a tap under 180ms with no move snaps). Keyboard: arrows/WASD to swim, Space to snap.
games.progression: Five dive sites unlock by journal progress: Sunlit Shoal (0 to 40m, bright, tangs, turtles), Kelp Hall (swaying kelp occludes photos, seals), Wreck (rooms, eels, an octopus), Twilight Wall (dim, torch matters, mantas, sharks) and Midnight Vent (black, bioluminescence, anglerfish, a vent that refills air but hides a rare species). The first build ships 5 sites with 5 species each; a 6th species per site is added only if time allows. Banked points buy small upgrades: tank size, fin speed, torch width and a faster shutter. Journal goals (silhouettes with star slots) give a clear 20-plus-minute chase. The best single-dive score is saved. The journal and upgrades persist via Arcade.store.
games.art: World: a sunlit reef that sinks into the abyss. The water gradient runs by depth: #7fe7e0, #1aa2b8, #0b5a8a, #08264d, #030914. Near the surface, swaying god-ray quads (additive, skewed) and a pre-rendered caustics tile scroll on the sand and on the diver. Marine snow drifts at every depth. Three parallax reef silhouette layers fade to blue haze. Coral is drawn with bezier branches: coral #ff7a6b, sea fans #b25cff, sponges #ffb84d and anemones with waving tentacles. Creatures are stylised vector shapes with gradient bodies, stripe and spot masks, and rim light from the torch, and deep species glow (bioluminescent cyan #5ff7ff and magenta #ff5ad1 spots). The diver wears a yellow #ffd23f wetsuit and flippers with a kick animation, plus a bubble trail. HUD: a camera viewfinder, not panels. Corner brackets frame the screen, a film-counter dial sits top-right, air is a round brass gauge with a needle bottom-left, and depth is a tick ruler along the left edge. Banked photos stack as tilted polaroids. Shell theme: brass and sea glass with a porthole title.
games.audio: Music is muffled and underwater: a lowpassed (900Hz) marimba arpeggio at 90bpm. The regulator's inhale and exhale (filtered noise envelopes) is the percussion on beats 1 and 3. Deeper water slows the tempo, drops the key and adds a dark pad, and the midnight site uses glassy bell tones. SFX: a shutter click plus film whir, a flash ping, a photo-quality chime ladder (one rising note per star), bubbles (sine blips with pitch drift), a jelly sting zap, a shark bump thud, and a low-air heartbeat beep that speeds up. Surfacing is a splash and seagull-like sine chirps.
juice: A snap freezes the frame for 120ms with a white flash, and a polaroid drops and swings into the corner
3-star photos earn a gold border with sparkles and a little fanfare
Schools burst apart in a boid scatter when you rush them, then re-form
Low air tightens the vignette, fogs the gauge glass and brings in a heartbeat
Surfacing fans the dive's polaroids across the screen as the points count up
games.teach: Dive 1 starts with a slow school of tangs already inside the reticle. A ghost finger taps the shutter, and the first photo always rates at least 2 stars. As you descend the air gauge pulses once with an up-arrow toward the boat. A journal silhouette appears with a tick when the first species is captured, and tutorial_complete is tracked when the first photos are banked.
games.scenes: art: an open dive journal in close-up: a fresh polaroid of a manta mid-bank in sun shafts over a coral wall, the flash glare still fading on the print, clipped to a page of hand-drawn species silhouettes with star slots. No HUD. shot1: Sunlit Shoal with the viewfinder brackets on a turtle and a polaroid dropping into the corner with the flash. shot2: Midnight Vent in deep blue with the torch cone revealing a glowing anglerfish, the low-air vignette and the brass gauge in red.
games.feasibility: Medium risk, mostly in content volume. The design limits it to 8 parametric body archetypes (fusiform fish, disc, eel, jelly, cephalopod, turtle, ray, seal), each a draw function with palette, pattern and fin parameters, so the 25 species are data, not art. Boids are capped at 60 agents. Depth is shown by water colour and haze, with a warm torch cone that lifts colour and contrast where it points; there is no black mask (Pipistrelle owns that look). Photo scoring is pure geometry, so it is deterministic and unit-testable. Test hook: window.__game = { start(seed, site), swim(dx, dy), snap(), step(frames), setAir(0) /* loses */, journal(), state() }.

games.title: Silverleap
games.pitch: Tap left and right to swim a salmon upstream, leap the falls and dodge the bears.
games.hook: Your thumbs alternate left, right, left and the salmon wiggles forward against the current, with splashes on each side. A white waterfall roars ahead, you hold to charge and release, and the fish arcs over the lip in slow motion as a bear's paw whiffs past.
games.loop: A top-down river scrolling upward, built on a seeded spline with varying width. The current comes from a flow field: fastest at the centre, slow by the banks, and gentle reverse eddies behind rocks. A tap on the left half is a tail stroke that pushes and noses left, and a tap on the right half does the same to the right. Alternating within the rhythm window (0.25-0.45 s apart) builds a multiplier of x1 to x1.6, shown by glowing gills. Tapping faster than the window gives weak, splashy strokes. Doing nothing drifts you downstream. Strokes cost stamina, which refills when you rest in eddies or eat glowing shrimp. A waterfall every ~25 s has 2-3 notches of different heights. Swim into the foam pool at the base, hold to fill a power ring and release: enough power clears the lip, too little tumbles you back with a 1.5 s loss.
