Riding the spline with an offset avoids free-flight control problems and soft-locks. The course frame comes from the spline tangent with a fixed world up, which avoids roll flips. Keep fewer than 150 visible objects and pre-render clouds and islands. Knife-edge is a roll angle tied to corridor width, and the elimination check is a few lines over the points table. Test hook: Arcade.test {start, lose, state}; ?debug exposes window.__game { start(seed, course), stick(x, y), autopilot(true), forceFinish(pos), endRun(), state() } so Playwright can fly a course and force a mathematical elimination.

games.title: Roost
games.pitch: Place one owl in every row, column and orchard grove. Owls are territorial: no two may touch.
games.hook: Tap a cell and an owl glides in and settles on a branch with a blink of its lamp-yellow eyes. Its row, column and neighbours softly dim, so the logic clicks instantly, and every forced cell you spot feels like a small win. Put two owls side by side and they fluff up and hoot at each other.
games.loop: An NxN grid (5 to 10) of orchard tree crowns divided into N groves, each a tinted canopy region. Rules: exactly one owl per row, per column and per grove, and no two owls touch, even diagonally, because owls are territorial. Tapping a cell cycles empty, then a leaf mark, then owl, then empty. Dragging across cells paints marks. An auto-dim setting (on by default, toggled in the menu) dims every cell excluded by placed owls. Rule breaks glow red and the owls involved fluff up and hoot at each other. Every puzzle has a unique solution. Two modes: Orchard (endless, saved) and the Daily Roost (seeded by the date, with a streak). The score is time, shown as the moon crossing the sky; there is no fail. A hint reveals one forced deduction, found by the logic solver, by highlighting the line or grove and the cell to place, and adds 30 s. Generation: a random valid placement (a permutation with |p[i]-p[i+1]| > 1), then N groves grown by randomised balanced flood fill from each owl. A backtracking solver checks uniqueness; if it is not unique, a boundary cell is reassigned to kill the alternative solution, or the puzzle is regenerated (seed+attempt). A 3-tier logic grader rates difficulty: tier 1 singles, tier 2 a grove confined to one line, tier 3 n groves within n lines.
games.controls: One thumb: tap to cycle a cell, drag to paint marks. Cells are at least 32px at 10x10 on a 320px screen, with a long-press magnifier showing the grove for precision. Keyboard: arrows move, Space places an owl, X marks, Backspace clears.
games.progression: Orchard 1-10: 5x5 and 6x6, tier 1. Orchard 11-30: 7x7 and 8x8, tier 2. Orchard 31-60: 9x9, tier 2-3. Orchard 61 onward: 10x10, tier 3, endless. The Daily Roost is an 8x8 tier-2 puzzle with a streak count. The run (orchard level and the in-progress board) is saved, and progress shows 'Orchard 14'. Best = orchards solved; the daily best time is stored separately.
games.art: An autumn orchard at dusk. The sky runs from plum (#3b2340) overhead to amber (#d98b4a) at the horizon behind silhouetted hills, and the last light rakes across the trees. The grid is the orchard seen from above at a slight tilt: each cell is a tree crown, and each grove is a tinted canopy region with its own fruit and a pictogram for colour-blind play: apple red #c8423b, pear gold #d9b44a, plum violet #7a4a8c, quince yellow #e6c35a, crab-apple rose #e07a8a, medlar brown #8a5a35, damson indigo #3d3f7a, cherry crimson #a3203a, walnut green #5f7a3a, elder black #2a2430. Grove borders are thick dark branches (#2a1a12). Owls are round feathered silhouettes in warm browns and greys (#7a5a42, #b49a7a) with ear tufts, soft feather scallops and lamp-yellow eyes (#ffd45a) that blink at random. HUD: carved fruit-crate labels for the level, the moon timer and hints, and a basket that fills with fruit as rows complete. Tiny pictograms show the rules: one per row, column and grove, and no touching. The menu shell is owl feather and orchard-crate wood. Dark mode is full night (#1a1424) with the groves in deeper tones and the owls' eyes glowing.
games.audio: Music: a gentle 92 bpm loop of plucked harp-like tones and a low woodwind sine with vibrato in D minor pentatonic, over a soft wind-in-branches noise bed. SFX: placing an owl is a wing whoosh and a soft landing thump with a 'hoo'. A mark is a leaf rustle. A conflict is a pair of indignant hoots. A completed row, column or grove plays a wooden chime that climbs with each completion, and a solve gives a chorus of owl hoots in harmony and a rising harp run.
juice: Owls glide in on a curved path from the edge of the screen, flare their wings and settle with a light haptic
Excluded cells dim with a single falling leaf
Completing a row, column or grove ripples a wave of rustling leaves along it and drops its fruit into the basket
Conflicting owls puff up to twice their size, glare and hoot in red
On solve every owl blinks in sequence, then they all turn their heads to the rising moon
games.teach: Orchard 1 is a 5x5 with 3 owls already placed, so the remaining two are forced. A highlighted row has only one open cell, and a ghost hand taps it. The four rule pictograms in the HUD animate once at the start. tutorial_complete fires when the player places the final owl on their own.
games.scenes: Art: an 8x8 orchard board half solved at dusk, owls mid-glide and settled, groves heavy with different fruit, with no HUD. Shot1: Orchard 1 with the crate-label HUD, rule pictograms and ghost hand. Shot2: a 9x9 Daily Roost with marks, dimmed cells and two neighbouring owls fluffed up in red.
games.feasibility: The uniqueness solver for N up to 10 is a few dozen lines and fast (under 20 ms). Grove repair for uniqueness can loop, so attempts are capped and fall back to regeneration. The logic grader is limited to 3 simple tiers to stay buildable. Rendering is static plus small animations; the board layer is pre-rendered and only overlays animate. Test hook: Arcade.test {start, lose, state}, where lose is a forfeit; ?debug __game.start(level | 'daily'), .place(r, c), .mark(r, c), .solution(), .state(), .forfeit() (runEnd 'restart'). Estimated 1600-2200 lines.

games.title: Little Orbits
games.pitch: Mini golf between tiny paper planets. Roll round their curves, dodge the moon-dust bunkers and bend your putt into the cup.
games.hook: You pull back, see the first half-second of a dotted path curving round a coral moon, let go, and the ball curls around the planet, rolls along its surface past a moon-dust bunker and drops into a glowing crater. A hole-in-one in the first ten seconds is possible, and it feels like magic.
games.loop: Top-down view of a small star system that fits the screen. The ball rests on a tee pad on one planetoid. Drag anywhere and pull back: the aim arrow points opposite the drag, the power is the drag length (capped), and a dotted preview shows only the first 0.6 s of flight (gravity is included, so the bend is visible but the finish is yours to judge). Release to putt. Each planetoid pulls the ball with softened inverse-square gravity. When the ball touches a surface it rolls along it with rolling friction and loses speed, so a putt can run round a planet's curve like a green; it can bounce off at high speed (restitution 0.4). Surfaces are golf terrain: grass (normal), moon-dust bunkers (high friction, the ball digs in and stops) and ice rings (almost no friction, the ball slides on). Each tour has one signature obstacle, mini-golf style: a rotating space-station spoke that sweeps across the hole like a windmill's blades, an airlock gate that opens and closes, or a bouncing satellite. The cup is a glowing crater on the target planet; the ball drops in when it passes over it below a capture speed (with a gentle magnetic pull on the last few pixels). Leaving the system's boundary ring or falling into a black hole costs +1 stroke and resets the ball to its last rest point. Each hole has a par of 2-4; picking up happens at par+3. A run is a 'tour' of 9 holes. Score: hole-in-one 500, eagle 300, birdie 200, par 100, bogey 40, worse 0, with a streak bonus for consecutive under-par holes.
games.controls: One thumb: drag anywhere and pull back to aim and set power, release to putt; drag back to the start point to cancel. Keyboard: Left/Right rotate aim, Up/Down power, Space to putt.
games.progression: Each tour is a seeded star system type, generated from hand-tuned rules, and tours unlock in sequence: 1 Pebble Belt (2-3 still planetoids, grass and bunkers, the rotating station spoke), 2 Moon Dance (moons orbit on rails at fixed periods, so timing matters; the airlock gate), 3 Event Horizon (a black hole hazard with a visible spiral and a slingshot ring that boosts speed; the bouncing satellite), 4 Ice Rings (low-friction ice bands where the ball slides on), 5 Binary (two planets orbit each other), then endless 'Deep Tours' mixing all rules with more bodies. Hole generator: place tee and cup planets by rule, then search a launch grid (angle x power) with the real fixed-step sim; accept only holes with at least a handful of 1-2 stroke solutions, and set par from how many solutions exist and how many strokes the best ones take. The tour and hole are saved between visits (progress pct = hole / 9). A best tour score is kept per tour type.
games.art: Flat pastel paper-cut space, like a picture book, with no nebula blobs: the background is layered paper sheets in lavender (#c9b8e8), peach (#f6c8a8) and mint (#bfe8d6) with soft drop shadows between the layers and a sprinkle of cut-out paper stars. Planetoids are paper discs with layered rings of colour: coral #FF8C69 with a darker paper shadow #C2504A, sea-green ice worlds #7FD8BE and sand moons #F2D49B. Grass is a scalloped green edge, bunkers are speckled cream dust patches, ice rings are glossy pale-blue bands. Orbits and gravity contours are chalk-dotted lines (white dots on the pastel). A black hole is a deep plum paper hole with a swirl of cut-paper strips. The ball is a pearl #FFF7E8 with a mint #7DFFC4 dotted trail. Each planet has tiny paper details: craters, a flag on the cup crater, a little tee tower, and the tour's obstacle (the station spoke is a paper cross that turns like windmill blades). HUD: a paper scorecard strip, with stroke pips and par as punched holes, the hole number on a paper planet tab and the score in Unbounded. Shell theme: pastel paper-cut with deckled edges.
games.audio: Music: dreamy space bossa at 92 BPM: soft sine-plucked chords, a gentle brushed-noise shaker, a round triangle bass, and a slow-attack pad; it gets one extra sparkle layer on the last hole of a tour. SFX: aim tick (pitch rises with power), putt (soft wooden tock), gravity whoosh (filtered noise that brightens with speed), surface roll (low rumble), bounce (rubbery blip), cup sink (descending chime arpeggio), hole-in-one (choir-like formant chord), black hole gulp (pitch-down drop), boundary reset (reverse swoosh).
juice: Hole-in-one: time slows as the ball drops, the crater erupts with a ring of star particles, camera zooms 10% then eases back, a constellation draws itself spelling the score as dots
Slingshot: when the ball passes close to a planet at high speed, its trail brightens and stretches and the planet's rim light flares
Sink: the flag pops up out of the crater with a spring tween and the stroke pips count into the score
Black hole: the ball spirals in with a shrinking trail and a short screen warp (canvas scale wobble)
Tour complete: the 9 hole planets line up as a mini solar system while the score counts up
games.teach: Hole 1 of the first tour is a straight putt between two planets with a ghost hand pulling back; the dotted preview is long on hole 1 only. Hole 2 bends around a planet so the player discovers gravity by seeing the preview curve. One-line hint: 'Pull back and let go'.
games.scenes: art: the ball rolling round a coral paper planet past a dust bunker, its mint trail curving toward the flagged crater on a second planet while the station spoke sweeps, layered pastel paper behind, no HUD. shot1: aiming on tour 2 with the dotted preview and chalk gravity contours visible, moons on their rails, the scorecard HUD. shot2: a hole-in-one star burst on the Event Horizon tour with the black hole spiral in frame.
games.feasibility: Risks: procedural holes that are unsolvable or trivial, and rolling on curved surfaces. Mitigation: the sim is a fixed-step deterministic integrator (dt 1/120) used by both play and the generator, so verified solutions really work; the solution search runs over a coarse grid (about 90 angles x 12 powers, early-out on boundary exit) spread across frames during the hole transition animation. Surface rolling is handled by projecting the ball onto the planet circle and keeping only tangential velocity, which is simple for circles. All bodies are circles (no polygons); surface type is an angular range on each planet, so bunkers and ice are a friction lookup, and tour obstacles are rotating or toggling line segments. Test hook: start() starts tour 1 hole 1, lose() ends the run, and ?debug exposes putt(angle,power) plus the generator's best solution for the current hole so test.cjs can sink holes and check scoring, stroke penalties and the saved run.

games.title: Fair Halves
games.pitch: Slice tossed market treats into perfectly even halves for two hungry bear cubs.
games.hook: A watermelon arcs up, you swipe, and it splits along your exact line. Each half tumbles to a bear cub waiting below. Cut it dead even and both cubs cheer with a 'PERFECT' ding. Cut it lopsided and one cub pouts. Slicing is satisfying from the first swipe, and fairness gives every cut a skill target.
games.loop: Treats are tossed up from below in seeded waves along arcs, spinning slowly. Swipe to cut: a cut counts when the swipe segment fully crosses an item's convex polygon. The item splits into two polygons along the line, and the halves fly apart and fall to the left and right cubs, who catch and munch them. After every cut, a ghost line of the true area-bisecting cut at the same angle flashes for half a second, so players learn where the even line sits (especially on wedges). Evenness e = smaller area / larger area: ≥0.95 Perfect ×3, ≥0.85 Great ×2, otherwise ×1, with base points per item. A seesaw fairness meter tilts toward the cub who got more on each cut. Perfects re-centre it, and if it tips fully the cubs squabble and you lose one of 3 honey jars, then it resets. An item that falls uncut also costs a jar. Wasp nests must not be cut (that releases wasps and costs a jar). Golden pears must be cut twice into quarters. One swipe through several items is a combo bonus. Every 10 waves a 'Picnic' round tosses one giant cake slowly: one cut, and the score is the evenness × 1000.
games.controls: One thumb: swipe across items. The cut line is drawn with a blade trail; the pointer path is sampled every frame and the trail sits slightly ahead of the finger. Mouse drag works too. There is no keyboard play.
games.progression: Waves 1-3: big round items (watermelon, pie) tossed one at a time, slowly. Then long items (baguette, cucumber), where only a mid-cut across the length or a careful lengthwise cut is even. Then wedges (cheese, cake slice), where the even line is not through the obvious middle and learning that is a real skill. Then faster spins, simultaneous tosses, wasp nests from wave 6 and golden pears from wave 9. Item speed and count rise per wave up to a cap. The market moves stall by stall rather than through the day: the fruit row, the bakery, the cheese cellar and the picnic meadow, each with its own awning colours, and the cubs gain little hats at best-score milestones.
games.art: A sunny open-air market. A striped awning frames the top (#E94F37/#F6F1E9) with scalloped edges. Background stall layers are soft-focus, with fruit crates, bunting triangles fluttering, and dappled sunlight patches drifting. The foreground is a wooden counter #A0673E with grain lines where the cubs sit: two honey-brown #8B5A2B bear cubs with cream muzzles, bibs and big expressive eyes, animated to open mouths, catch, chew, cheer and pout. Items are rich vector art pre-rendered to offscreen canvases: a watermelon with rind stripes and a seeded red interior, a cheese wedge with holes, a crusty baguette with score marks, a lattice pie, a layer cake, a pumpkin, honeycomb. Cut faces show interiors (flesh, crumb, layers), drawn by clipping the interior art to each half. The wasp nest is papery #C9A227 striped with buzzing dots. Each stall row brings its own awning stripes and crates. HUD in a solid shell styled as a chalk price board (#2F3B35 board, chalk white #EDEDE4, chalky Figtree): the score as chalk numerals, honey jars for lives, and the fairness seesaw as a wooden plank on a pivot at the bottom centre between the cubs.
games.audio: Music: a sunny 118 bpm accordion-and-ukulele-style loop (pluck synth + reedy square) with a walking bass and claps. The picnic-meadow variant is mellower. SFX: swipe whoosh (filtered noise by swipe speed), cut (crisp slice: a high noise click + juicy squelch per item type), Perfect ding (bright two-note bell), Great chime, munch (cub chewing blips), cheer (a pair of happy yips), pout (low 'hmph'), wasp buzz (detuned saw tremolo), jar break (glass clink), Picnic fanfare.
juice: The cut freezes for 40 ms with the line glowing before the halves part, then juice droplets spray in the item's colour
PERFECT stamps in chalk-style letters with a ding, and both cubs bounce and cheer in sync
The fairness seesaw tips and wobbles with spring physics, and the cubs glare at each other as it nears the edge
Multi-item swipes chain a rising slice pitch and pop a ×N combo label
Picnic round: slow-mo on the giant cake, a drum roll, and the evenness percentage counts up to the result
games.teach: The first wave tosses one watermelon that hangs at its apex while a ghost hand swipes straight down through the centre; the halves drop to each cub and PERFECT appears. A faint dashed 'ideal line' glows on the first three items only and then disappears. The hint reads 'Cut it fair'.
games.scenes: art: seed 7, no HUD. A watermelon mid-split with juice spray, a cheese wedge and baguette airborne, both cubs reaching up with open mouths, awning and sunlight. shot1: seed 3 at 6 s with HUD, a blade trail through a pie, the seesaw nearly level, 3 jars. shot2: seed 9 at a scripted Picnic round, the giant cake split nearly perfectly, both cubs cheering and the 98% count-up.
games.feasibility: Low-medium risk. Items are convex polygons (8-24 vertices) in local space with position, rotation and velocity. A cut is a line-polygon split (Sutherland-Hodgman against two half-planes) with areas from the shoelace formula. Each half is drawn by clipping the pre-rendered item canvas with its polygon path (ctx.clip), plus an interior cut-face fill along the cut edge, so no per-item art for halves is needed. Halves fall with simple gravity and a target arc toward their cub. Swipe detection tests the per-frame segment against each polygon's edges with a minimum swipe speed so slow drags don't cut. Waves come from a seeded schedule. Test hook: lose() spends all jars; state() exposes items and their centroids, so test.cjs can inject an ideal cut through the area-bisecting line (found by binary search) and assert Perfect scoring, the seesaw rules, wasp penalties and best persistence.

games.title: Moonglaive
games.pitch: On a rust-red moon under a swollen red sun, hurl a crescent glaive that curves out and sweeps back through the swarm.
games.hook: Your first swipe sends a silver crescent singing out in a wide arc. It cuts three crawlers going out, then swings back and cuts two more as it returns to your hand with a bright 'ting'.
games.loop: Top-down crater arena on the dusty surface of a rust-red moon. The left thumb moves the knight with a floating joystick (low-gravity drift). The right thumb swipes to throw the glaive: the swipe direction sets the heading and the swipe length sets the range (120-340px). It flies a curved loop that bends toward the side your swipe bent (a straight swipe curves toward the arena centre), then homes back to wherever you are, hitting on both legs. While it is out you are unarmed. Tap the right side to recall it early: it turns sharply back and sweeps a new path. Catching it while moving toward it is a 'perfect catch', which charges the next throw (pierces armour, wider blade, brighter trail). Enemies: crawlers (swarm, 1 hit), shellbacks (armoured front, so hit them from behind on the return leg), spitters (lob slow orbs; the glaive cuts orbs), burrowers (dust ring tell, then erupt), splitters (split into 3 small ones). Dust devils drift across the arena: a glaive passing through one is bent along its spin, which can curve a throw round cover or ruin it. 3 suit integrity pips.
games.controls: Two thumbs: left half floating joystick to move, right half swipe to throw, tap to recall. One-thumb fallback: tap-and-hold to walk toward your finger, flick to throw. Keyboard: WASD move, arrows throw in 8 directions, Space recalls.
games.progression: Waves from seed in a crater that subtly rotates its terrain each wave (seeded rocks act as cover the glaive must curve around). After every wave, pick 1 of 3 icon cards: twin glaives, longer arc, burning trail, magnetic return (faster), ricochet off rocks, a slow-time perfect catch. The cards are the heart of the game, so builds differ run to run. Every 5th wave is an eclipse, not a boss: a moon slides across the red sun, the arena goes dark except for the glaive's glowing trail and the crawlers' lime spots, and the Mother Crawler hunts by sound, homing on footsteps and the glaive's hum, so you stand still to hide and throw to lure it. You sever its segments with arcs. Later eclipses last longer and add a hovering Lens that reflects straight throws, so only curves hit. The red giant's sunspot turns a little more each wave, which marks progress. Best score and best wave are saved.
games.art: A rust-red moon of a dying red giant, warm and alien: ochre and oxblood dust (#c4643a lit, #7a2e1f shadowed) with fine ripple dunes, and craters lit low from the side by a huge crimson sun (#e2402f core, #ff8a5c limb) that sits on the horizon, fills a third of the sky and carries a slowly turning dark sunspot. Shadows are long and teal-black (#0f2a2c), the cool counterweight to all the red. The sky above the sun is deep maroon fading to #1a0b14 with few stars. Dust devils are translucent spinning cones of ochre particles. The knight wears a bone-white suit with an oxidised-copper visor (#3fb6a8) and leaves footprints that fill with drifting dust. The glaive is a polished silver crescent with a pale cyan ribbon trail (#bff6ff) that becomes the only light during eclipses. Enemies are glossy obsidian-green chitin (#1f3b2c) with bioluminescent lime spots (#b6ff3b), so they pop against the red. Eclipse: the sun becomes a black disc in a crimson ring, the ground drops to near-black maroon, and only trails and spots glow. HUD: a visor overlay with thin curved arcs at the screen edges (suit integrity as three segments of an arc, wave number as a small orbit dial) and score in a slim instrument-readout block top-centre. Shell theme: rust-red expedition kit (oxidised iron plates with ochre stencils and copper rivets).
games.audio: Spacious ambient-pulse at 84 BPM in Lydian: a low drone, glassy triangle arpeggios, soft half-time kick, airy noise swells. Eclipse waves drop the music to a heartbeat drone with a pulsing saw bass, so the Mother Crawler's footsteps can be heard. SFX: a continuous glaive hum whose pitch follows its speed (it sings), a 'shink' on hits that rises within one throw, a bright 'ting' on catch, a chord for a perfect catch, muffled crunches (low-passed for the airless feel), a hiss of escaping air when hurt.
juice: Glaive ribbon trail and singing hum pitch-tracked to speed
Multi-hit in one throw counts up in tiny numbers along the path
Enemies burst into lime goo and ochre dust that falls in slow low-gravity arcs
Perfect catch: radial flash ring, 70ms hitstop, the knight's visor glints
Eclipse segment severed: shake, the segment tumbles away and a sliver of crimson sunlight flares round the moon's edge
games.teach: Wave 0 is a line of 5 crawlers marching slowly toward you, and a ghost hand swipes from the right side. One throw kills them on the out and back legs, which teaches the curve. Movement is shown by a faded left-thumb ring. Shellbacks first come facing you with a curved-arrow tell on their backs.
games.scenes: art: the knight mid-throw with the glaive arcing around a crawler swarm, the huge crimson sun on the horizon, long teal-black shadows and a dust devil, no HUD. shot1: wave 2, the curved trail visible cutting through crawlers and the visor HUD arcs. shot2: an eclipse wave, the dark arena lit only by the glowing glaive trail curving round the Mother Crawler, with the twin-glaive upgrade active.
games.feasibility: Medium-low risk. The glaive path is a parametric curve: out along a quadratic Bezier, then a homing return with steering. Hit tests are swept circle against circle each frame. Twin-thumb input splits pointers by screen half, and the contract asks for 44px targets, which is fine because the halves are huge. The upgrade cards are icon-first with 1-2 word labels. Eclipse hunting is a sound-radius check (moving, or a glaive in flight, makes noise within a radius), so it stays deterministic. The two-thumb control and the one-thumb fallback are both playtested, and test.cjs runs a bot through waves 1-3 with each. Debug hook: window.__game {start(seed), step(ms), throw(dx,dy,bend), recall(), lose(), pick(i), state()}.

games.title: Russet
games.pitch: Lead a fox cub through four seasons. Listen for mice under the snow and pounce.
games.hook: The cub trots along a paper-cut meadow and the grass ahead twitches with a rustle. Press there and the cub crouches and wiggles its rear. Release and it arcs head-first into the grass, then pops up with a vole and a happy yip. It is adorable and readable in five seconds.
games.loop: A side-on journey through a seeded landscape built from ground segments (tall grass, reeds, leaf piles, snow drifts, open ground, streams, logs). The cub trots right automatically at a gentle pace. PREY (voles, mice, frogs, crickets) hide under cover and move between hidden slots in short hops. They give CUES: grass tips twitch, a leaf lifts, snow sparkles and cracks, a breath puff rises in winter, plus a rustle sound panned to their position. POUNCE: press and hold on the ground ahead of the cub (valid range 80 to 260px is shown as a soft arc). The cub stops and crouches, and a landing marker appears 60px ABOVE your finger so your thumb never hides it. Slide to adjust, then release to pounce in a parabola that takes 0.45s. If the prey is within 22px of the landing point when you land, you catch it. Prey hop after the first rustle, so reading timing is the skill. HUNGER drains steadily and catches refill it. Consecutive catches without a miss build a combo multiplier. HAZARDS are telegraphed. A hawk announces itself with a screech and a growing shadow from the left; tap the cub to flatten, and it is only safe inside tall cover, so you hustle into cover first. Streams must be pounced across. Badger burrows rumble before a badger pops out. Thin winter ice cracks and needs a quick pounce off. Falling apples in autumn knock you over. The mother fox waits at a den at the end of each season leg (about 2.5 minutes). Delivering your caught food there banks the score, and the cub visibly grows a size. The run ends when hunger empties or after the third hawk catch (3 lives shown as tail-tip icons).
games.controls: One thumb. Press and hold on the ground ahead to crouch and aim, slide to adjust, release to pounce. Tap the cub to hide. Keyboard: hold Space to crouch-aim, Left/Right to adjust distance, release Space to pounce, Down to hide.
games.progression: Spring: frogs leap out of reeds (moving targets) and there are streams. Summer: crickets jump unpredictably in tall grass and the hawk arrives. Autumn: leaf piles also rustle from WIND (decoys; real prey show a tail tip) and apples fall. Winter: snow hides almost everything, so cues are sound and breath puffs only, plus thin ice and deep drifts that slow trotting. After Winter, Year 2 starts: the same seasons with denser hazards, faster prey, subtler cues and a dusk segment lit by fireflies. Each leg is generated from (seed, year, season). The save holds year, season, hunger and lives at each den, so you resume at the last den. The best score is food delivered.
games.art: World: a cut-paper diorama. Five parallax layers, each a flat-colour silhouette with a soft drop shadow onto the layer behind (shadowBlur on offscreen pre-renders), give a handmade paper-craft depth. Every season gets its own palette: spring #cfe8a9 / #8cc084 / blossom #f7c6d0; summer #f4d06f / #e09f3e / #6a994e; autumn #c8553d / #f28f3b / #588b8b; winter #e8f1f8 / #a9c6de / #5b7c99 with layered snowfall. A slow sun or moon arc sets the sky gradient. A subtle paper-fibre noise texture is overlaid once. The cub is built from paper shapes: russet #d9622b body, cream chest, dark socks, a huge tail with a white tip, and triangular ears that swivel toward rustles. It squashes and stretches on crouch and landing. Prey are tiny paper cut-outs. HUD: torn-paper tags pinned with a stitch. Hunger is a crescent belly-moon that fills, the season wheel at top centre shows a cub marker moving around four quadrants, and lives are tail tips. Shell theme: kraft paper with stitched borders, a leaf-stamp title, warm and cosy.
games.audio: Music: gentle folk. Karplus-Strong plucked guitar, a soft recorder (sine with vibrato) and a frame-drum heartbeat, with a different key and tempo per season: spring 100bpm major, summer 110bpm lydian, autumn 88bpm dorian, winter 72bpm with sleigh-bell sparkle and sparse notes. SFX: rustles (bandpassed noise bursts, stereo-panned to the prey), the crouch wiggle (soft grass swish), a pounce whoosh, a snow/leaf/grass impact (each a different filtered noise), a mouse squeak, a happy yip (pitch rising with combo), a hawk screech (FM sweep), ice cracks and a den reunion chord.
juice: The crouch wiggles the cub's rear and twitches the tail tip before the pounce
The pounce dives the cub into the snow up to its hind legs, which stick out kicking for a beat before it pops up
A catch gives a yip that rises in pitch with the combo, a paper-confetti burst, and the hunger moon counting up
When the hawk passes the screen darkens under its shadow, leaves blow sideways and the cub's ears flatten
Season changes play a page-turn transition with the palette cross-fading layer by layer
games.teach: The first rustle happens right in front of the cub, a ghost finger presses on it, and that vole waits still for the first catch. The second prey hops once to show timing. The first hawk arrives at 35s with a pulsing tap-the-cub icon and a big patch of tall grass right there. tutorial_complete is tracked on the first unassisted catch.
games.scenes: art: winter at dusk, the cub mid-pounce in a perfect arc above a snow drift sparkling with a hidden mouse, layered paper hills in blue, falling snow and the moon rising. No HUD. shot1: spring meadow with the cub crouched, the landing marker over twitching grass, and the season wheel and hunger moon. shot2: autumn with the hawk's shadow sweeping over leaf piles and the cub flattened in tall grass, apples on the ground.
games.feasibility: Low risk. It is a side-scroller with no free player movement (auto-trot), parabolic pounces and simple prey state machines. The paper look is cheap: each season's 5 layers are pre-rendered once into wide offscreen strips and scrolled. Ground segments are seeded from a small table. The main risk is the thumb hiding the target, solved by the lifted marker. Test hook: window.__game = { start(seed, year, season), pounceAt(x), hide(bool), step(frames), setHunger(0) /* loses */, state() } exposing prey positions so a bot can pounce on them and assert catches.

games.title: Mirage
games.pitch: Tune your gears, launch on the green and shift in the glow to out-drag rivals across the shimmering salt flats.
games.hook: Two dragsters sit on blinding white salt with heat shimmer on the mountains. You hold to rev, the lights drop amber, amber, green, and you launch with a wheelie and tyre smoke. The tach needle sweeps into a glowing band, you tap, and an exhaust flame and a camera kick reward a perfect shift. Ten seconds, totally clear.
games.loop: Each duel is a quarter or half mile, 8-12 s, against one rival. Staging: hold to rev, and the needle must sit in the green launch band when the tree turns green. Releasing early or launching before green is a foul and loses the duel. Run: tap to shift. Each gear's tach shows a narrow glowing 'perfect' band and a wider 'good' band near redline. A perfect shift gives a power kick, an early shift bogs, and a late one bounces off the limiter. 4-6 gears depending on the gearbox. Nitro is one swipe up per run (best saved for top gear). GARAGE: between duels there is a 30-second tune on a gear-ratio dial for each gear, and the dial physically moves that gear's shift bands on the tach (shorter ratios pull harder but bring the perfect band earlier and make it narrower), so what you set in the garage is exactly what you have to hit on the strip. From league 2, bracket racing is a core mode: you dial in a target time and must finish as close as possible without going under it, which turns the skill on its head. From league 3, crosswind gusts drift the car: drag sideways to correct, and crossing the lane line is a disqualification. Rivals have seeded reaction times, shift quality, car power and gear setups. Each result prints on a timeslip (reaction, 60 ft, ET, trap speed). The career ladder is 5 leagues x 6 rivals, and three losses in a league end the run (reason 'lose'). A rival who beats you becomes a grudge rival: they come back later in the league with a car tuned against your last setup, and beating them pays double. Score = career wins x 1000 + best-ET bonus.
games.controls: One thumb: hold to rev at staging, tap to shift, swipe up for nitro. In later leagues drag sideways to correct crosswind. Keyboard: hold Space to rev, Space to shift, Up for nitro, Left/Right to correct.
games.progression: Leagues change the time of day and the conditions: morning dew (lower grip at launch), noon heat shimmer, golden sunset, night under floodlights, and a moonlit final league. Wins earn in-game cash (no real money, no purchases) for upgrades that change how the game plays: engine (more power, but the perfect band moves), gearbox (an extra gear with narrower bands), tyres (a wider launch band), nitro (longer). Rivals have personalities (a fast starter, a late shifter, one who always saves nitro for last). Bracket events and crosswinds keep later duels from becoming rote. The best ET is kept separately.
games.art: Blazing salt flats seen from a low camera behind the cars. Salt is white #f4f1ea with a hexagonal crust-crack pattern (a seeded Voronoi texture pre-rendered and drawn in perspective strips), black lane stripes, staging lights and a timing tower. The sky runs from #7fb8e6 to pale #e9f3fb. Distant mountains are violet-blue #8a8fb8 with heat shimmer (horizontal sine offset of image strips). The palette moves to amber and rose at sunset and to floodlit blue-black at night. Cars are seventies-style dragsters and muscle cars drawn from the rear three-quarters with chrome, wrinkling slick tyres, wheelie bars and exhaust flame. The upper 55% of the screen is the scene and the lower 45% the dashboard: a huge analog tach (cream face #f2e6c8, orange #ff6b1a redline, a needle that casts a shadow), a row of shift-light bulbs, the gear numeral and a mini progress strip. HUD style is seventies motorsport with brown, orange and cream stripes. Shell theme: a timeslip paper ticket with dot-matrix digits and perforated edges.
games.audio: A funk-rock loop at 104 bpm (sawtooth slap bass, clavinet-like plucks, drum machine) ducked under the engine. Sound effects: engine (layered saw and square pitched by rpm through a bandpass), shift clunk plus an exhaust pop, limiter stutter, launch tyre squeal, nitro roar plus whoosh, tree beeps, foul buzzer, win (crowd-like noise swell plus bell), timeslip print (dot-matrix chatter).
juice: Launching lifts a wheelie, wrinkles the tyres into smoke and jolts the camera
A perfect shift flashes the needle, lights an exhaust flame and gives a small camera kick with speed lines
Nitro lights a blue flame, stretches the field of view and adds a slight colour fringe
A close finish freezes into a photo-finish frame with the gap marked
The timeslip prints line by line with dot-matrix chatter
A foul start flashes the red tree light and darkens the screen
games.teach: The first duel has very wide bands and a slow rival. A ghost thumb holds at staging, and a pulsing tap prompt appears exactly as the needle enters the green band on each gear. Nitro is introduced in duel 3 with a ghost swipe. Track tutorial_complete after the first win.
games.scenes: art: two dragsters launching side by side in tyre smoke on white salt with heat-shimmering mountains, no HUD. shot1: staging with the tree lit amber and the tach dashboard showing the launch band. shot2: nitro in top gear at sunset with a perfect-shift flash and the photo-finish split.
games.feasibility: Low risk and the smallest scope, so the extra effort can go into polish. The scene is a straight perspective ground with two car sprites, and the physics is 1D (rpm, gear, speed). The main risk is thinness, which the garage tune (ratios that move the shift bands), bracket racing from league 2, grudge rivals, crosswind and upgrades address. Test hook: Arcade.test {start, lose, state}; ?debug exposes window.__game { start(seed, league, rival), tune(gear, ratio), rev(bool), shiftNow(), nitro(), bot('perfect'|'sloppy'), forceFoul(), endRun(), state() } so Playwright can run duels and force a loss.

games.title: Philtre
games.pitch: Brew the customers' layered potions: pour between flasks, in the right order, into the right flask.
games.hook: A customer's bell rings and a recipe card drops: green, then gold, then violet on top. You tap a flask, then another, and a glowing ribbon pours across; layer by layer the order builds in the flask under that customer's bell until it matches, corks itself with a pop and slides up to the customer for a coin. It is pouring, but every pour is a plan.
games.loop: Shelves of glass flasks, each holding up to 4 layers of coloured liquid. Tap a source flask, then a target: the source's top run of same-coloured layers pours into the target if the target is empty or its top matches, moving as many layers as fit. ORDERS: each level shows 1-3 customer recipe cards hanging from brass bells above the shelf, each a layered order from bottom to top (for example green, then gold, then violet on top). An order must be built in the specific flask under that customer's bell. Every other flask only has to end tidy: a single colour or empty. Because layer order now matters, sorting becomes planning: you have to lay the bottom colour first and keep the order flask clean while you dig for the next. A finished order corks itself and the customer takes it. You win when every order is served and everything else is tidy. Moves are counted against a par from the generator's solver, and stars are given at par, par+4, or solved. Undo is unlimited. Once per level, a spare vial (capacity 2) can be added if you are stuck, but it caps stars at 2. When no legal pours remain, the flasks shudder and the undo button pulses. Twists introduced over levels: Cloudy layers (a layer's colour is hidden behind frosted glass until the layers above it are poured off), Catalyst (silver liquid: pouring silver onto a flask flips that flask's layer order and then dissolves, so an order can be built upside down and flipped), Tall flasks (capacity 5-6), and Sealed flasks (wax-sealed and unusable until N orders are served).
games.controls: One thumb: tap the source flask, then the target; tapping anywhere in a flask's column counts as hitting it. You can also drag one flask onto another. Keyboard: number keys pick flasks, U undoes and R restarts.
games.progression: Level 1 has one customer, 2 colours and 3 flasks. Colours rise to 10 by level 60, laid out on 1-3 shelves (at most 7 flasks per row), and customers rise from 1 to 3 with longer orders. Cloudy layers arrive at level 15, Catalyst at 30, Tall flasks at 40 and Sealed flasks at 50; level 61 onward is endless with mixed twists. Generation: choose the orders and the tidy colours, build the solved end state, then scramble it from seed+attempt, rejecting any start where an order is already served. A DFS with a visited set on a canonical state (non-order flasks sorted as strings, order flasks kept in place), capped at 200k nodes, finds a solution, which sets par and is stored for hints. The move set is the same as plain sorting; only the goal check differs. The run is saved, and progress shows 'Shelf 27'. Best = levels solved.
games.art: A candlelit apothecary at night. Dark walnut shelves (#2b1a12) have grain and bevelled front edges, set against a shadowy brick wall (#3a2420 with mortar lines) and hanging dried-herb silhouettes. Warm candle-glow pools (#ffb45a radial) flicker softly, and there is a brass-scale silhouette at the side. Flask silhouettes vary (round-bottom, conical, slim vial, tall cylinder). The glass is rendered with an edge highlight, an inner refraction gradient and a rim ellipse. Liquid layers glow (a 'lighter' inner gradient) with a meniscus line and rising bubbles. Colours: ruby #ff4f6d, jade #35e0a1, sapphire #4d8bff, amber #ffd23f, violet #b26bff, ember #ff8a3d, frost #7ff0ff, moonmilk #f2efe6, lime #8bd450, rose #ff6fd8, ink #3b3b5b, tea #c47b3f, plus the silver catalyst #d8dde6 with a moving mirror sheen. Each colour also carries its own inner glyph pattern (bubbles, stars, swirls, flecks) for colour-blind players. Customers' recipe cards hang from small brass bells above the shelf, each showing its order as stacked coloured bands with the colour glyphs. HUD: a red wax-seal medallion for the level and a parchment tag tied with string for moves and par. The menu shell is leather and parchment. Light mode is a daylit apothecary: whitewashed lime plaster, oak shelves, sunlight through a mullioned window, and liquids drawn with deeper saturation instead of glow.
games.audio: Music: an 84 bpm minor-key loop with a harpsichord-like line (fast-decay square waves), plucked lute arpeggios (Karplus-Strong) and a low drone. SFX: selecting makes a glass clink (2.4 kHz sine plus a harmonic). A pour is a filtered-noise gurgle that rises in pitch as the target fills. A cork pop is a noise burst with a quick sine drop, followed by a smoke fizz. A served order rings its customer's bell. Clearing a level plays an ascending arpeggio of glass clinks. A deadlock is a dull wooden knock.
juice: The selected flask lifts and tilts with its liquid surface sloshing on a damped spring
A pour is a curved bezier ribbon with droplets; the target's surface wobbles and bubbles rise
Serving an order: the flask corks with a pop and a burst of coloured smoke, the bell rings, the flask slides up to the customer's card and the card flips to show a coin, and the nearest candle flares
Level complete clinks each flask in sequence as the whole shelf glows, with stars stamped in wax
A catalyst pour makes the layers swirl and settle in reverse order with a glassy shimmer; a deadlock makes the flasks shudder as the undo button pulses
games.teach: Level 1 has one customer whose order is two layers. A ghost hand taps the flask holding the bottom colour, then the order flask under the bell, then does the same for the top colour, and the order corks. Level 2 makes the player clear a wrong colour out of the order flask first. Nothing needs reading.
games.scenes: Art: a shelf of 8 glowing flasks mid-pour with a ribbon, two recipe cards hanging from brass bells, cork smoke and candle glow, with no HUD. Shot1: Level 1 with the wax-seal HUD, one recipe card and the ghost hand. Shot2: Level 34 with three shelves, cloudy frosted layers, a silver catalyst mid-pour flipping a flask, and one order just served.
games.feasibility: Very buildable, and the rules are tiny; orders change only the goal check, not the move set, so the solver stays simple. The solver is DFS with memoisation, and hidden layers are known to the solver. Layout: 7 flasks per row at 320px means 40px-wide flasks, so the hit zone must be the full column height to stay at least 44px tall and wide in effect. The pour animation is a 2D rotation of the source about its lip, positioned over the target. Test hook ?debug: __game.start(level), .pour(a, b), .solution(), .state(), .forfeit() (runEnd 'restart'). Estimated 1500-2000 lines.

games.title: Telemark
games.pitch: A penguin ski jump at polar sunrise. Hit the lip, balance in the wind, land a clean telemark.
games.hook: A penguin rockets down an icy ramp, you tap at the lip, and it launches into a rose-gold sunrise; holding the thumb tilts it into a long glide while the distance counter spins, then it drops into a perfect telemark, one foot forward and flippers out. One jump is ten seconds of pure tension.
games.loop: Side view of a ski jump hill (inrun ramp, take-off table, steep landing slope, outrun), camera follows the penguin. Inrun: the penguin slides automatically; hold the thumb to tuck (less drag, more speed). Take-off: tap (or release the tuck) at the lip; the lip light goes from amber to green to red, and timing sets jump power (perfect window 80 ms). Flight: the penguin is a 2D body with speed and a pitch angle; lift and drag depend on the angle of attack (simple lookup curve). Hold the thumb to lean forward, release to lean back; gusts push the angle around, so you balance it inside the best-glide band (shown as a faint arc at the penguin). Too far forward = nose-dive, too far back = stall. Landing: just before touchdown, swipe down (or tap) to open into the telemark pose; landing angle close to the slope and on time gives top style; otherwise a comic tumble and belly slide (style 0). Floating herring rings in the flight path give bonus points and a tiny lift if you fly through. Points per jump = distance points (relative to the hill's K-point) + style (0-20) + herring bonus + wind compensation.
games.controls: One thumb: hold to tuck on the inrun, tap at the lip to jump, hold to lean forward and release to lean back in flight, swipe down (or tap) to land. Keyboard: Space for all of the above, Down for the landing.
games.progression: A run is a tour of 5 hills of increasing size, each from a seeded profile: Snowball (K40), Seal Ridge (K70), Glacier (K95), Iceberg (K125) and the Sunrise Flying Hill (K185). Each hill gives 2 jumps; your best jump must pass the qualifying distance (about 85% of K) to move on, otherwise the run ends. After hill 5 the tour loops with stronger, gustier wind and bigger herring patterns. Weather varies per hill by seed: calm, headwind (more lift), tailwind (shorter flights), crosswind gusts shown by snow streaks and flags at the hill side. Keeps a best tour score plus a record distance per hill shown as a fish flag on the slope.
games.art: Polar sunrise: apricot and rose light raking across the snow (#f6b48c, #f7d6e0), long periwinkle shadows (#7f8fd6), a low pink sun just above the sea-ice horizon, and the frozen sea below the hill glittering with sparkle points. The sky runs from pale gold at the horizon to soft blue-violet (#a9b4e8) overhead. Layers: a few last stars fading; distant ice mountains in 2 parallax silhouettes catching pink on their faces; a fishing village of igloos with warm window glow #FFB86B; the ski jump tower built of ice blocks with lights running down the inrun (they chase as the penguin passes); spectator penguins on the outrun waving tiny flags. Penguin: black #14161C back, white belly, orange beak and feet #FF9F1C, goggles that glint pink in the sun, a little striped scarf that streams in flight; poses drawn with shapes for tuck, flight (flippers out like a V), telemark and tumble. Snow spray on landing catches the sunrise. HUD: etched-ice style: the distance counter as large icy numerals with frosted edges at the top, a vertical wind arrow widget like an icicle, and the style score as five little judge penguins holding up cards with dots (no words) after landing. Shell theme: waxed ski and pine (honey-pine panels with a waxed sheen and red binding straps).
games.audio: Music: airy, slow synth-pop at 100 BPM with a glassy bell lead, soft sidechained pad and sparse sub bass; during the inrun the music thins to a heartbeat kick and a rising filter, and it opens fully on take-off. SFX: inrun slide (filtered noise rising with speed), lip click on tap, take-off whoosh, wind in flight (noise whose brightness follows speed and gusts), herring ring pickup (bright pling with pitch rising per ring in a row), telemark landing (crunchy snow thump), tumble (comic bonks and a squeak), crowd of penguins cheering (high chirps).
juice: Perfect take-off: a green flash on the lip, 4 frames of hit-stop, the camera swings out wide and the music bursts open
Long flight: the distance counter ticks up, passing the K-point line flashes the line and the crowd squeaks
Herring rings: each ring pops into sparkles and adds a rising note; a full set gives a gold fish trail
Telemark landing: snow spray burst, screen shake 2px, judge penguins hold up their cards one by one
Tumble: the penguin bounces into a belly slide with snow puffs and a little dazed star particle loop - funny, not frustrating
New hill record: a fish flag is planted on the slope and a flock of terns wheels over the igloos
games.teach: The first jump shows three ghost prompts in sequence at the right moments: a ghost thumb holding on the inrun, a pulse on the lip light ('tap now' as a ring), and a hand holding then lifting in flight. The first hill is small and forgiving so every first-time player lands something.
games.scenes: art: the penguin at the top of its flight arc, flippers in a V and scarf streaming, the low pink sun behind and long periwinkle shadows on the hill, the lit ice tower and igloos below, no HUD. shot1: mid-flight on Glacier hill with the distance counter, wind widget and herring rings ahead. shot2: a telemark landing with snow spray and the judge penguins holding cards, a record fish flag nearby.
games.feasibility: Risks: tuning the flight model so it feels skilful and not floaty. Mitigation: flight is a 2D point with pitch, lift = k * v^2 * L(alpha) from a 7-point hand-tuned table, drag similar; integrator at fixed 120 Hz. Hill profiles are generated from a few parameters (inrun angle, table length, landing slope curve) scaled by K, so 5 hills are data. All deterministic with the seeded RNG for gusts. Test hook: start() begins hill 1, lose() fails qualification, and ?debug autopilot (perfect take-off and a scripted lean) lets test.cjs assert a long jump scores more than a late take-off and that failing to qualify ends the run. Sky gradient and mountains pre-rendered.

games.title: Lanternspire
games.pitch: Drop swinging pagoda floors and stack them true while the tower sways in the wind.
games.hook: A lacquered floor swings on a rope above misty mountains. Tap, it drops with a heavy thunk, and the camera lifts. Land it dead centre and a bronze bell rings with a gold flash. Within five drops you are chasing the perfect bell and feeling the tower start to lean.
games.loop: A pagoda floor hangs from a rope that swings as a pendulum (amplitude, period and rope length vary per floor). Tap to release: the floor falls as a projectile with the horizontal velocity it had at release and lands on the tower top. The landing offset dx from the top floor's centre is graded: |dx| < 6 px Perfect (bell, combo +1, sway reduced), up to 50% of the floor width Placed (the overhang stays and shifts the tower's centre of mass), and past 50% the floor topples with a tumble animation and costs one of 3 roof-tile lives. Tower sway: the tower top oscillates sideways with an amplitude that comes from the accumulated centre-of-mass offset and wind, so the landing target moves and timing has to read both the swing and the sway. Wind gusts are telegraphed 2 s ahead by prayer flags snapping in their direction, and they push the hanging floor's swing. Every 10th floor is a roof tier: a sweeping eave roof with lanterns that light up for a big bonus, and then sway resets partly. Score = 10 per floor × (1 + combo/5), plus 50 per Perfect and roof bonuses.
games.controls: One thumb: tap anywhere to release. Keyboard: Space or Enter.
games.progression: Floors 1-5 swing slowly with no sway and no wind. The swing speeds up gently per floor and rope length varies from floor 8 (changing the rhythm). Wind starts at 12. Special floors come from a seeded deck: a wide hall (easy), a narrow bell floor (hard, double points), a heavy stone floor (dampens sway), a garden terrace (bonus). Altitude bands change the world every 10 floors by place, not by clock: the misty valley → pine cliffs with waterfalls → monasteries hanging on the crags → the sea of clouds → thin blue high air with the first stars → the lantern sea, where thousands of sky lanterns drift up past the spire, the band the title promises. The title shows your tallest spire as a silhouette.
games.art: Misty mountains in a black-lacquer-and-gold shell. Layered peak silhouettes #5E7F86, #3C5A66 and #24404D with mist bands #9FC2C0 drifting between them in parallax; swallows and drifting pine needles as ambient motion (no blossom petals). Floors are vermilion lacquer #C8372D walls with gold trim #E8B04B, dark slate roof tiles #2F3640 with upturned eave tips, latticed windows that glow warm #FFB84D at dusk and night, and paper lanterns that sway. The crane is a wooden beam reaching in from the top with a creaking rope and a bronze hook. The sky shifts with altitude: valley haze #F9D9B8, clear cliff air #BFE3F2, warm crag light #F28F6B → #6B3E75, a sea of clouds lit from below, high blue #1E2A5A with the first stars, then the lantern sea: deep indigo #10162B filled with warm floating sky lanterns #FFB84D. Prayer-flag strings in five colours show the wind. HUD: a vertical bamboo height gauge on the right edge with floor tick marks and the score painted in gold on black lacquer at the top-left. Lives are 3 small roof tiles.
games.audio: Music: a calm 80 bpm pentatonic loop with plucked koto-like voices (pluck synth with fast decay), a breathy flute (sine + filtered noise) and a soft taiko pulse that grows with height; layers thin out above the clouds for an airy feel. SFX: rope creak (filtered noise), release swish, landing thunk (pitch drops as the tower gets heavier), Perfect bell (inharmonic FM gong, pitch rising per combo), topple (wood clatter + tumble whoosh), wind gust (noise swell), lanterns lighting (soft chimes).
juice: Landing squash on the floor plus a dust puff from both eaves, and a camera dip and recover
Perfect: a gold ring shockwave, the bell pitch climbs with the combo, and window lights flicker on floor by floor down the tower
Topple: the floor tumbles and rotates with debris, screen shake, 70 ms hit-stop, and a roof tile crumbles in the HUD
Roof tier: lanterns light in a cascade, a flock of swallows bursts out, and the camera pulls back to show the whole spire
Altitude band change: the sky crossfades, birds scatter, and the bamboo gauge glows at the milestone
games.teach: The first floor swings slowly over a wide base while a ghost hand taps at the centre. A dashed plumb line from the hook to the tower shows when they line up for the first three floors, then fades. The hint reads 'Tap to drop'.
games.scenes: art: seed 7 at a 50-floor spire in the lantern sea, no HUD. Roof lanterns lit, a gentle lean, a floor swinging above, sky lanterns rising around the top and mist layers far below. shot1: seed 3 at floor 6 with HUD, the floor mid-swing, the plumb line, the bamboo gauge and 3 tiles. shot2: seed 9 at a scripted Perfect on a roof tier above the clouds, with the gold ring, the lantern cascade and a combo of 7.
games.feasibility: Low risk. There is no rigid-body engine: the pendulum is analytic, the drop is a projectile, and landing and toppling are scripted by thresholds, with the topple a canned rotation animation. Tower sway is a damped oscillator driven by the centre-of-mass sum and wind impulses. Floors are pre-rendered per type to offscreen canvases, and only the top 12 floors are drawn individually (lower ones are baked into a cached strip). Seeded floor deck and wind schedule. Test hook: lose() spends all lives; state() exposes floors, combo and swingPhase. test.cjs runs a bot that taps at the computed optimal phase and asserts that Perfects score, that toppling over 50% costs a life, and that the best score persists.

games.title: Swordtide
games.pitch: Swipe to lunge a swordfish through schools of fish. Breach the surface to cash them in.
games.hook: One swipe and the swordfish rockets through a shimmering school, and three sardines are stacked on its bill with a rising 'shk-shk-shk'. You flick upward, burst through the waves, and they fan out into a shower of points.
games.loop: Side-view open ocean in portrait, far from any reef: a mirror-like surface near the top, bottomless cobalt below, and the camera drifting gently to follow the fish. Swipe anywhere: the swordfish lunges that way, and lunge distance scales with swipe length (max 280px). Fish in the lunge path are skewered and stack visibly on the bill. Each stacked fish makes lunges about 8% shorter, and every stacked fish wriggles free after 6 s, so you have to bank. Lunge through the surface line to breach: the fish leaps, the stack flies off, a shoal of flying fish scatters above the waves, and you score sum times stack size (a 6-fish kebab is worth far more than six singles). The thermocline is a darker band about two-thirds of the way down where lanternfish schools glow: they are slow and worth triple, so it is the safe, rich zone, but it is the furthest point from the surface, and the 6 s wriggle clock makes every deep stack a race back up. Sargassum rafts drift on the surface: fish hide under them, lunging through one halves your lunge length, and a breach through a raft scatters golden weed for a small bonus. Hazards: jellyfish (skewering one stings you, costs a heart and drops the stack), pufferfish (safe when small; inflated ones bounce you and pop the stack), sharks (patrol, then arch and charge with a telegraph; lunge into their side to beat them for a big bonus, head-on hurts you) and fishing nets lowered from passing boats (stuck for 1 s, stack lost). 3 hearts. Tap without swiping for a short dart.
games.controls: One thumb: swipe anywhere (direction and length set the lunge), tap for a short dart. Keyboard: arrows aim, Space lunges (hold to lengthen).
games.progression: Endless tides from seed, travelling through open-ocean zones rather than times of day: the blue (sardine and mackerel schools), the sargassum line (rafts, flying fish, hidden fish), the thermocline drop (lanternfish, with sharks patrolling the band's edge) and the squall swell (the surface heaves, so the breach line moves). School size and value grow over time, jellyfish blooms drift in, and the shark count rises every 45 s. A 'feeding frenzy' every 2 minutes packs golden fish into the water for 12 s. Rare species (a striped marlin pal, a sunfish) are worth big bank bonuses. Best catch (biggest single kebab) and best score are saved separately, which gives two ways to play.
games.art: Open ocean, deep and clean, with no floor and no reef: the water runs from bright cobalt #1f5fd1 near the surface to #0b2a7a and a near-black thermocline band #06143d with drifting marine snow. Sunlight shafts appear only in the top fifth, fanning down from a mirror-like surface whose underside shows a wobbling inverted copy of the sky. Above the surface: a wide sky with a warm sunset band on the horizon (#ffb36b to #ff7b8a) under high blue, a fishing boat silhouette far off, and arcs of flying fish when you breach. Sargassum rafts are golden-olive (#b89b3a) clumps with little floats. The swordfish is steel-blue (#2f5d8a) with a silver belly, a tall sail fin and a long bill; its eye follows targets. Schools are silver sardines that flash as they turn and tiger-striped mackerel; lanternfish carry rows of cyan photophores (#7ff6ff). Jellyfish are translucent violet with glowing tendrils. HUD: hearts as air bubbles wobbling in the top-left; score painted on a red-white fishing float bobbing at the surface line; the current stack shown as a fish-count fan beside the float. Shell theme: sun-bleached sail canvas with brass grommets and rope lashing.
games.audio: Dub-flavoured groove at 90 BPM with feedback-delay echoes, plucked marimba, warm filtered pad, deep round bass. Frenzy adds steel-drum-like square plucks. SFX: a bubbly whoosh lunge, a 'shk' skewer that rises in pitch with each stacked fish, a big splash and wind on breach, a cascading coin-like arpeggio on banking, a squishy zap for jellyfish, a puffer boing, a shark growl tell.
juice: Skewer pitch ladder and the bill visibly bending with weight
Breach: 0.35 s slow motion, fish fan out spinning in the air with a scatter of flying fish, spray droplets, then score count-up
Lunge streak with bubble trail; lunging through sargassum throws golden weed fronds
Shark defeat: hitstop, the shark spins away, a burst of bubbles, a shake
Camera zooms out slightly when the stack is 5 or more to build anticipation
games.teach: It opens on a slow school right in front of the fish, with a ghost hand swiping through it. After the first skewer, the surface glints and an up-arrow ghost shows the breach. The first jellyfish arrives alone and drifts slowly, pulsing violet. The only text: 'Swipe to lunge' and 'Breach to bank'.
games.scenes: art: the swordfish breaching mid-air with five fish fanning off its bill, flying fish scattering, the sunset band and the boat silhouette behind, no HUD. shot1: underwater near the surface, a lunge streak through a silver school with three fish stacked under the sun shafts. shot2: the thermocline band with lanternfish glowing, a shark arching to charge from the band's edge, and the float HUD showing the stack.
games.feasibility: Low-to-medium risk. Lunge collision is segment against circle. Schools use cheap boids (at most 60 fish, grid-free O(n²) is fine) or seeded formations. The sun shafts and the surface band are pre-rendered and only scrolled or crossfaded; there is no caustic floor. Swipe parsing: pointerdown/up vector with a 12px minimum length, otherwise it is a dart. Physics is simple kinematics with drag, and there are no fluids. Debug hook: window.__game {start(seed), step(ms), lunge(dx,dy), lose(), state()}.

games.title: Puddleway
games.pitch: Lead ducklings across a rainy town to the pond. Rush, and they fall behind.
games.hook: Drag and a mother duck waddles off with a line of yellow ducklings pattering behind, each peeping on its own pitch. Find a lost one under a bench and it hops into line with a heart. Rush, and the tail ducklings stretch out and start peeping in worry, so the challenge is clear in seconds.
games.loop: Top-down, scrolling upward in portrait through a seeded town district, from the nest to the pond about 10 screens away. Districts are built from tile chunks: park path, crosswalk, bike lane, market stalls, fountain plaza, storm drains and puddle fields. LEAD: the mother duck walks toward a point 70px above your finger (lifted so the thumb never hides her), at walk or hurry speed depending on how far you drag ahead. FOLLOW: ducklings follow the mother's path history at fixed spacing, each with a max speed lower than hurry. If the gap to the duckling ahead grows past a threshold, that duckling STOPS and sits peeping with a ripple icon. Everything behind it stops too, so the line splits. Go back and QUACK (tap) near the stopped one to re-link it. The core tension is moving fast enough to beat hazards without stretching the line. HAZARDS, all telegraphed: bikes on painted lanes (a bell ring and a headlight streak 1s before), skateboarders, crosswalks with car traffic on light cycles (cars shown as passing roofs and shadows, lights clearly coloured), open storm drains (a duckling that walks over one plops in, so route around them; they are clearly drawn), a stalking cat that crouches and wiggles near the tail before a pounce (quack within its window to scare it), and pigeons that scatter into the line. Ducklings that are hit are startled away (they flee back to a random hiding spot nearby, rather than shown harmed, which keeps the tone gentle). PUDDLES: ducklings love them, so the line slows but you earn splash points. COLLECT: lost ducklings hidden under benches, umbrellas and planters (line max 12), and breadcrumbs. Reach the pond to score ducklings × district bonus plus crumbs. You lose the district if the mother is hit, or if the line is empty with nobody left to find.
games.controls: One thumb. Drag to lead (the mother follows a point lifted above your finger, and further ahead means faster). Tap to quack. Keyboard: arrows/WASD to walk (Shift to hurry), Space to quack.
games.progression: Districts in order: Park (puddles, a bike lane), Market Street (stalls, pigeons, crosswalks), Riverside (drains, a cat, a narrow quay edge), Railway Yard (a level crossing with trains telegraphed by lights and bells), Lamplit Lanes (evening, warm streetlamp pools on wet cobbles with softer light between them, so ducklings are a little harder to spot but never hidden by a black mask) and Flower Market (rows of flower carts and crowds of umbrellas moving as obstacles). After that, districts recombine with heavier rain and more hazards. The ducklings you arrive with carry to the next district as your lives, so protecting the line matters over the whole run. The save holds the district and line size, with Arcade.progress showing 'Riverside, 7 ducklings'. The best score is the run total.
games.art: World: a rainy watercolour town from above. Wet asphalt #5d6b7a with mirror reflections (vertically smeared copies of lamps and signs), cobbles in #8a8172, park grass #7fbf7f with fallen petals, pond #4fa3a5 with lily pads. Rain streaks fall diagonally across everything, and every puddle spawns ripple rings. Passersby are colourful umbrellas seen from above (#ff6f61, #ffd166, #06d6a0, #118ab2) gliding along paths and dripping. A paper-grain watercolour bloom texture is pre-rendered per chunk. Lighting is soft, overcast and cool, with warm shop-window glows spilling onto the wet ground. The mother mallard is speckled brown #8b6b4a with an orange bill and a waddling body. Ducklings are fuzzy yellow #ffd84d balls with dark eye dots and soft outlines, bobbing with offset phases and shaking off water after puddles. HUD: rounded stickers with white outlines. Ducklings in line are a row of tiny duckling stickers (stopped ones flash), and district progress is a dotted path from a nest sticker to a pond sticker across the top. Shell theme: rain-blue watercolour paper with sunny yellow accents and raindrop dots.
games.audio: Music: a jaunty march at 104bpm. Pizzicato strings (plucks), a tuba-like bass (lowpassed square) and a light snare, over a bed of soft rain noise. Crossings add a tick-tock. SFX: peeps (short sine chirps, each duckling with its own pitch), a quack (sawtooth with a formant-like bandpass blip), splashes, a bike bell ding, skateboard rumble, a cat hiss, a drain plop, a level-crossing bell, and at the pond a chorus of peeps rising in pitch one by one.
juice: A rescued duckling hops into line with a heart puff and a peep that harmonises with the others
The line splashes through puddles in a cascade of ripple rings and water droplets, ducklings shaking off afterwards
The cat's pounce triggers a brief slow-mo while the quack window is open, and a successful quack bristles it into a startled leap
Arrival: the line marches into the pond, each duckling splashing in turn as the score counts up with rising pitch
Stretching the line too far makes the tail ducklings wobble and peep faster before they stop
games.teach: District 1 opens at the nest with a ghost finger dragging along a dotted path, and the line follows. A lost duckling waits 2 screens ahead under a bench with a glint. The first stretch-stop happens on a gentle slope with a quack icon on it. The first bike lane has a painted bike symbol and an early bell. tutorial_complete is tracked when the first district is finished.
games.scenes: art: a mother duck leading eight ducklings across a rain-slicked zebra crossing toward a park, umbrellas around them, reflections of shop lights on wet asphalt and ripples in puddles. No HUD. shot1: Park with the line following a curving path through puddles, a lost duckling under a bench, and the sticker HUD. shot2: Riverside with a stalking cat crouched near the tail, an open storm drain, and one duckling stopped and peeping with the line split.
games.feasibility: Low to medium risk. Following uses a ring buffer of the mother's positions sampled by distance, and ducklings are indexed into it with a per-duckling speed clamp and gap check (simple and deterministic). Districts come from seeded rows of about 8 chunk types. Hazards are lane-based movers with timers. Rain and reflections are cheap (pre-rendered reflection layer per chunk, a pooled particle system with a 300 cap). The main risk is a crowd of actors, capped by limiting umbrellas and cars per screen. Test hook: window.__game = { start(seed, district), leadTo(x, y), quack(), step(frames), hitMother() /* loses */, state() } exposing line state so a bot can walk a path and assert splits and rescues.

games.title: Rooftop Swifts
games.pitch: Dive and swoop a swift through old-town rooftops to beat the flock to the bell tower.
games.hook: The swift drops off a terracotta ridge into the low gold sun. You hold and it tucks into a screaming dive between two houses, release and it whips up through a gap in the washing lines with a whoosh, faster than the rival swifts screaming around you.
games.loop: Side view scrolling right, using portrait's height for sky, rooftops and alleys. The bird always flies forward. Holding tucks the wings: pitch goes down (up to 70 degrees) and gravity adds speed. Releasing spreads the wings: pitch rises with lift proportional to speed squared, and speed bleeds while climbing. Warm thermals (shimmering columns over sunlit roofs) lift you for free. Glowing gnat swarms each give one flap charge, and a double-tap spends it for an instant climb. Chimneys, spires, antennas, roosting pigeons and washing lines (flagged by bright laundry) are obstacles. Scraping a roof costs 30% speed and a 0.4 s tumble, and hitting a wall stuns you for 1 s. There is no death, it is a race. Arches and alley gaps reward a 'thread' bonus and a speed burst. Five rival swifts replay seeded bot flights. Each evening is a 70-90 s course to the bell-tower nest. Top 3 continues to the next evening, and fourth or worse ends the run (reason 'lose'). Score = placement points + threads + gnats.
games.controls: One thumb: hold to dive, release to swoop up, double-tap to flap when you have a charge. Keyboard: hold Space to dive, Up to flap.
games.progression: Endless evenings that build on each other: rooftops get denser, washing lines and antennas get more common, wind gusts (visible streaks) push the bird from evening 3, a rain-shower evening has darker light and lower lift, a storm-front evening (5) rolls a bruise-violet thunderhead over the town, with gusty downdrafts and lightning that throws the roofs into silhouette, and from evening 6 a hawk chases you through stretches where you must keep your speed up. Rival flight bots get greedier lines. Plumage variants unlock (pale-bellied alpine swift, a dusky swift) along with trail colours. The best evening reached and the best score are kept.
games.art: A Mediterranean hill town in late-afternoon sun. The sky runs from clear cobalt #5f9bd6 to warm gold #ffd27a near a low sun, and the storm-front evening darkens it to bruise violet #4a3a63 with lightning silhouettes. Stucco walls are ochre #e3a857, roofs are terracotta #c8643b with repeated tile-arc ridges, shutters are blue #3e6fa8, plus balcony plants, domes and bell towers. Four parallax layers: far hills with cypress silhouettes, the mid town, the near rooftops, and foreground chimney and plant silhouettes rushing past. Warm rim light on the sun-facing edges and long violet shadows. Lamps and windows switch on one by one near the end of each course. The swift is a dark #2a2433 sickle silhouette that morphs between a tucked dart and a spread crescent. Rivals wear tiny coloured leg bands. HUD styled as painted ceramic tiles: swift silhouettes perched on a wire along the top show positions, a gap timer beside your position shows the seconds to the swift ahead and behind, flap charges are small tile pips, and course progress is a ribbon. Shell theme: weathered wooden shutters and a patterned tile border.
games.audio: A waltz-like 3/4 at 132 bpm: mandolin-like plucks, an accordion-ish square pad with vibrato, light tambourine. Sound effects: rival swift screams (high FM chirps, louder as they get close), dive wind (rising noise), pull-up whoosh, flap (feather flutter noise bursts), gnat gulp (pop), roof scrape (tile clatter), arch thread (bright swish), finish (bell tower bong).
juice: Diving draws wind lines and tilts the camera slightly into the dive
Pulling up at top speed pulses the zoom with a whoosh
Threading an arch flashes the screen and scatters a few feathers
A near miss on a washing line makes the laundry flap and spin
Close rivals start a chorus of screams
At the finish the flock circles the bell tower as the bell rings
games.teach: The course opens with the bird on a roof edge above a deep gap. A ghost thumb holds to dive into it, then lifts to swoop up through a pulsing gnat swarm. The first course has wide gaps and no washing lines. Track tutorial_complete after the player's first dive-and-swoop that gains speed above cruising speed.
games.scenes: art: a swift in a tucked dive between terracotta roofs against a gold late-afternoon sky, rivals swirling, washing lines and a dome behind, no HUD. shot1: the start on a roof edge with the flock, swift icons on the wire HUD. shot2: the storm-front evening with a lightning silhouette, the player threading an arch in 2nd place with the gap timer at -0.4 s.
games.feasibility: Low to medium risk. The flight model is 2D: speed, pitch, gravity and lift. Collision samples the bird's nose and belly points against a roof-profile heightfield plus a short list of boxes and lines. The town comes from a seeded block grammar (building width, height, roof type, gaps, arches) and is baked per chunk offscreen. Rivals are deterministic bot replays. Test hook ?debug exposes window.__game { start(seed, evening), hold(bool), flap(), bot(true), forceLose(), state() } so Playwright can fly an evening and force a loss.

games.title: Cogwright
games.pitch: Drop gears on a blueprint. Link the motor to every dial, the right way round.
games.hook: Drop the first gear on a peg and it bites into the motor and starts turning with a satisfying tick, and the chalk drawing lights up. You play with it before you think about it, and then the dials demand direction and speed.
games.loop: A triangular (hex) lattice of pegs, about 7x10, on a blueprint. A fixed motor gear turns clockwise. Target dials are fixed gears marked with a required direction (cw or ccw arrow) and speed (slow, even or fast notch). A tray holds a limited number of small, medium and large gears (radius 0.5, 1 and 1.5 lattice units). Drag a gear onto an empty peg: placement is refused, with a red outline, if it would overlap another gear (centre distance below the sum of radii), and it meshes with any gear exactly that distance away. Rotation propagates by BFS from the motor: direction alternates at each mesh, and speed = parent speed x parent radius / own radius. If any gear would receive two different directions or speeds (an odd cycle or conflicting paths), the whole train jams: it shudders red and nothing turns. A level is won when every dial turns with the right direction and speed and nothing is jammed. Using fewer gears than par earns more stars, and unused tray gears are fine. Later elements: bolts (pegs that cannot be used), compound gears (a small and a large on one peg turning together, for ratio changes) and a second motor turning anticlockwise. Generation builds the solution first: from the motor, random-walk gear chains across lattice pegs to each dial using valid mesh vectors. The dial requirements are recorded from that, then the gears are moved to the tray with 0-2 decoys, and bolts are scattered on unused pegs to prune trivial routes. The solution is validated by the same propagate function, and any valid machine wins.
games.controls: One thumb: drag gears from the wooden ruler tray at the bottom onto pegs. The dragged gear floats 48px above the finger, with ghost mesh lines to any gear it would bite. Drag a placed gear back to the tray to remove it. A double tap clears the board. Touch or mouse only.
games.progression: Sheets 1-8: one dial, direction only. Sheets 9-16: two dials with conflicting directions. Sheets 17-24: speed ratios. Sheets 25-32: bolts and tight trays. Sheets 33-40: compound gears. Sheets 41-50: two motors. Sheet 51 onward is endless procedural, with up to 4 dials, longer distances and fewer spare gears. The run is saved, and progress shows 'Sheet 12'. Best = sheets solved.
games.art: An engineer's blueprint. Prussian-blue paper (#1d4e89) with subtle fibre noise, a fine grid (#3f74b5), decorative white construction circles and dimension arrows in the margins, a coffee-ring stain and a pencil lying at the edge. Pegs are small white circles. Unpowered gears are white line drawings in chalk style; powered gears glow in bright cyan chalk as they turn, and only when the sheet is solved does the whole machine sweep from chalk into brass (#d4a64a) and copper (#b8693d), with shaded teeth, a bevel highlight and a centre bolt. Brass is the reward here, never the default look (Orrery owns brass as a material). Teeth count is proportional to radius, so all gears share a tooth pitch, and each gear's phase is set so the teeth visibly interleave. The motor is a red-enamel housing (#c8423b) with rivets. Dials have ink needles with a target wedge. A desk-lamp light pool from the top left adds a vignette. HUD: an engineering title block in the bottom-right corner (ruled boxes holding the sheet number, gears used and par in Unbounded numerals), and the tray is a wooden drafting ruler with tick marks. The menu shell is drafting paper and ruler. Light mode is a whiteprint: cream paper (#f4efe2) with blue linework (#2a5ca8), and gears still turn brass on solve. Dark mode is a night blueprint (#0f2747) with cyan chalk glow.
games.audio: Music: a playful 110 bpm clockwork loop, with clock ticks as hats, a square-wave bass line, a music-box arpeggio and a woodblock on the off-beats.
