SFX: picking up a gear makes a metal scrape. Placing one makes a snap click with a ring. Meshing makes a ratchet burst. Spinning ticks repeat at a rate set by the gear's speed (rate-limited). A jam is a grinding noise followed by a clunk. A solve gives a chime cascade and a short steam whistle (noise through a resonant bandpass).
juice: A placed gear drops in with an overshoot, its teeth snap into phase with its neighbour, and its chalk lines brighten to glowing cyan as it turns
Dials snap green with a little flag pop and haptic when their requirement is met
A jam makes the train shudder, red stress lines flash, sparks fly from the conflicting mesh and the screen shakes slightly
On solve the whole machine sweeps from chalk into brass and accelerates, an approval stamp (a check-mark seal) thumps onto the sheet and paper cogs flutter down as confetti
Gears rotate continuously and smoothly at their true ratios, so the machine feels alive
games.teach: Sheet 1 has the motor and one dial with a single empty peg between them, and one small gear in the tray. A ghost hand drags the gear onto the peg and the dial spins. Sheet 2 needs two gears, so the dial turns the right way, teaching that each gear reverses the direction.
games.scenes: Art: a big running machine of brass gears and spinning dials on the blueprint under lamp light, with no HUD. Shot1: Sheet 1 with the title block, ruler tray and ghost drag. Shot2: Sheet 20 with speed dials, compound gears and a jammed train flashing red.
games.feasibility: Peg geometry on the triangular lattice uses axial coordinates. Meshes and overlaps are tested numerically with a tolerance of 0.05. Propagation is a BFS over the mesh graph. Tooth phase alignment: give every gear the same pitch (teeth = round(16 x radius)) and set phase_b = -phase_a x (r_a / r_b) + pi/teeth_b + angle-to-neighbour corrections. Make this visual phase test the first task of the build, because it carries most of the polish. Generation builds forward from a solution, so a valid level is guaranteed. Gear sprites are pre-rendered per size and material, and rotated at draw time. Test hook ?debug: __game.start(sheet), .place(size, pegIndex), .remove(pegIndex), .solution(), .state(), .forfeit() (runEnd 'restart'). Estimated 1800-2500 lines.

games.title: Mistbow
games.pitch: Archery across misty mountain terraces. Read the silk streamers and thread arrows through the wind.
games.hook: You draw the bow with one thumb, the view zooms down the valley, silk streamers flutter at three distances, you aim a little left, let go, and the camera rides the arrow as it drifts and thunks into a painted ring target in a burst of red ink.
games.loop: Behind-the-archer view looking up a valley of terraces, with targets at different distances. Press anywhere and drag down to draw (draw length = arrow speed; full draw locks with a creak). While holding, move the thumb to aim: the reticle moves with the thumb (relative, at reduced sensitivity for precision). The archer's breath makes the reticle sway; sway is small for the first 1.5 s after full draw and then grows, so waiting too long costs you. Release to shoot. The arrow flies as a 3D projectile with gravity and is pushed by wind, which is layered: up to 3 bands at different distances each have their own wind, shown by silk streamers, prayer-flag-like strips and drifting petals in that band (no numbers in the world, one small wind arrow per band in the HUD). The camera follows the arrow in flight (a quick zoom along its path). Targets: ring targets scored 10 to 1, swinging hanging gongs, paper parasols that burst open, a kite target that drifts, and a 'thread' bonus: pass the arrow through a hanging ring before it hits the target for x2.
games.controls: One thumb: press and drag down to draw, move to aim, release to shoot. Keyboard: hold Space to draw, arrows to aim, release Space to shoot.
games.progression: A run is a walk up the mountain through stations. Each station gives 5 arrows and a target score to pass (rising each station); not reaching it ends the run, but extra points carry over. Station 1 is completely still air, so the first breeze at station 2 is its own teachable moment. Station rules are generated from hand-tuned rules by station number: distance increases, more wind bands appear (1, then 2, then 3), gusts that change between arrows, moving targets (swinging gongs at station 3+, drifting kites at 5+), and thread rings at 4+. The light changes as you climb, always daylight in mist: pale dawn on the valley floor, bright morning haze on the terraces, a silver noon in the cloud forest and a golden late afternoon at the summit, so the scene keeps changing. Best score and highest station are kept.
games.art: Misty mountain terraces in an ink-wash painting style made with layered gradients. Palette: pale jade #A8C5B5 hills, mist #EEF2EC, ink #22303C silhouettes, vermilion #E63946 targets and streamers, gold #E9C46A sunlight, a warm dawn sky #FBD9B4 fading to #9CC3D5. Layers: 5-6 receding ridges, each a soft-edged silhouette with lighter tone and more mist with distance (pre-rendered); drifting mist bands that scroll at different speeds; pine trees on rocky outcrops; terraced fields with thin ink lines; a hill shrine's roofline; birds flocking now and then. Targets are painted wood rings on stands, paper parasols in vermilion and cream, bronze gongs that swing. The archer's bow arm and string are in the foreground lower-left as a strong ink silhouette with a red sleeve; the bow bends with draw. Streamers are animated ribbons (a chain of points blown by the band's wind). HUD: brush strokes - the score in a red seal stamp at the top-right, arrows left as brush-stroke arrows, station marker as a small painted mountain with a dot climbing it, wind arrows as quick brush flicks. Shell theme: rice paper with an ink-wash texture, ink-black headings and a vermilion accent.
games.audio: Music: a calm, spacious loop at 72 BPM - plucked koto-like tones (Karplus-Strong style pluck synth), a breathy flute-like sine with vibrato, deep frame-drum hits every bar, and wind noise underneath; a fuller arrangement after passing a station. SFX: bow draw creak (filtered noise with rising pitch), full-draw lock tick, breath (soft noise in and out with the sway), release twang (plucked string), arrow whistle in flight (sine with Doppler), target thunk (woody), bullseye (deep bell), gong hit (inharmonic metallic synth with long decay), parasol burst (a paper pop plus a chime), thread ring (high chime).
juice: Bullseye: 10 frames of slow motion before impact, the target shudders, a ring of gold ink splashes outward and a seal stamp '10' presses onto the screen
Arrow cam: the camera rides behind the arrow with motion streaks and the streamers it passes flick in the wind
Gong: the gong swings and ripples with visible sound rings while the long tone rings out
Thread bonus: the hanging ring flashes gold and the arrow trail becomes a golden thread
Station passed: the painted mountain HUD stamps a new dot and the view pans up the valley to the next station
Full draw: the bow creaks, the screen edges darken slightly to focus
games.teach: Station 1 has one close target in completely still air; a ghost thumb shows press, drag down and release, then the first arrow always lands somewhere on the target. The first windy station shows a streamer blowing hard with a ghost arrow drifting in a dotted arc for the first shot only. One-line hint: 'Pull down, aim, let go'.
games.scenes: art: the arrow mid-flight over the misty valley with streamers flaring, a parasol target ahead and a hill shrine's roofline in the mist, no HUD. shot1: full draw at station 3 with the sway reticle, streamers in 2 bands and the brush HUD. shot2, the hero shot: the arrow cam riding behind an arrow as it threads a hanging ring toward a swinging gong, streamers flicking past and the golden thread trail.
games.feasibility: Risks: 3D projection and arrow camera. Mitigation: a single pinhole camera; targets and ridges are placed at fixed depths, so each is a scaled sprite (pre-rendered); the arrow cam only interpolates the camera's z along the arrow's path with the same projection. Wind is a function of depth band, deterministic per seed. Sway is a deterministic Lissajous curve whose amplitude grows after a delay. Test hook: start() starts station 1, lose() fails the station, and ?debug shoot(aimX, aimY, draw) plus a solver that compensates for wind let test.cjs check scoring, station pass/fail and that a perfect solver beats the threshold.

games.title: Clearance
games.pitch: Draw flight paths for incoming ships into the right docking bays. Two ships touch and the station goes dark.
games.hook: A shuttle slides in from the edge behind an orange chevron. You draw a curve from it to the matching bay, it follows your line and docks with a clunk as the bay light flips green. Then a slow freighter and a tug appear on crossing courses, and you are an orbital traffic controller.
games.loop: A slowly rotating ring station sits in the lower middle of the screen, with 4-6 colour-coded docking bays round its rim. Ships drift in from the edges, each announced by a chevron 2 s before arrival: shuttles (small, fast, any bay of their colour), freighters (slow, and they need a long bay marked with a double chevron), tugs towing a cargo pod (two bodies, wide turns, so drawn paths are rounded to their minimum turn radius), and escape pods (must reach the medical bay within 10 s). Drag from a ship to draw its path; the path is smoothed and resampled, the ship follows it at its own speed, and the end of the path snaps to a bay and tracks it as the station turns. You can redraw a path at any time, and tapping a ship puts it in a slow holding circle. Ships with no path drift on their heading for 3 s, then hold. Ships closer than the warning radius flash a proximity ring and sound an alarm; ships that touch end the run at once. Debris drifts through, and a ship that clips debris limps home and costs one of 3 station status lights, as does an escape pod that misses its deadline; losing all 3 also ends the run. Score = dockings x a chain for consecutive dockings without a proximity warning, plus bonuses for freighters, tugs and pods.
games.controls: One thumb: drag from a ship to draw its path, drag again to redraw, tap a ship to hold it. Mouse works the same. No keyboard play.
games.progression: Endless from a seeded arrival schedule. The arrival rate rises, the station's rotation speeds up, and a new ship type joins every few minutes (shuttles first, then freighters, tugs and pods). Solar flares arrive from minute 3: the gas giant's limb brightens as a telegraph, then a white sweep blanks every drawn path for 2 s so ships coast on their headings. At about minute 5 a second, outer station ring opens with its own bays, turning the other way. Best score and longest chain are saved.
games.art: An orbital dawn: a copper-gold gas giant fills the bottom of the screen as a vast terminator crescent (#c27a3a lit, #f0b56a at the limb, banded with soft storms), the sun rising over its edge, all against deep space #0a0f1e with sparse crisp stars. No nebula washes. The station is white enamel with panel lines and long shadows from the low sun, with signal-orange bay lights that flip green when a ship docks. Bays are colour-coded with painted stripes (teal, amber, violet, rose) and the medical bay carries a green heart-pulse glyph. Ships are small clean silhouettes in their bay colour with tiny engine glows; paths are thin dashed lines in the same colour that fade behind the ship. Debris is charcoal shards catching the dawn light. HUD: wayfinding signage: the score and chain on a navy sign with copper numerals, the 3 status lights as round lamps on a panel, and the next arrivals as small chevrons at the screen edges. Shell theme: station wayfinding signage (navy enamel panels, copper pictograms, white rule lines).
games.audio: Music: calm ambient pads at 70 bpm (slow sine pads, a soft pulse bass, airy noise) that never get busy. An alarm layer fades in with proximity: two-tone sine beeps whose rate follows the distance of the closest pair. SFX: a soft pencil-scratch while drawing, a docking clunk and a chime pitched up the chain, a hold-pattern blip, a rising whine as a flare is telegraphed and a white-noise sweep when it hits, pod beacon pips that speed up near the deadline, a debris scrape, and at run end a power-down sweep as the station's lights go dark ring by ring.
juice: Docking: the clamp arms close with a clunk, the bay light flips from orange to green and the chain number pops
Proximity: both ships flash red rings, the screen edge pulses and the camera leans gently toward the pair
The drawing pen has a glowing tip, and the path fades out behind the ship as it is flown
Solar flare: a white sweep across the screen and every path flickers out for 2 s
Run end: the two ships spark, then the station's lights go dark ring by ring in silence
games.teach: The first ship is one shuttle with one open bay, and a ghost finger draws the path. The second ship arrives only after the first docks. The first crossing pair arrives slowly, and a ghost path shows one of them curving round the other. The only text is 'Draw a path to the bay'.
games.scenes: art: dawn over the copper gas giant, the white ring station with five ships converging on dashed paths, one docking with its clamps closing, no HUD. shot1: 6 s in, a shuttle following a fresh path to a teal bay, with the signage HUD. shot2: late game with the outer ring open, a tug towing a pod on a wide arc and two freighters flashing proximity rings during a flare.
games.feasibility: Low risk, about 1500-2000 lines. Paths are polylines (Chaikin-smoothed, resampled every 8 px) followed at constant speed by arc length; tug paths get a minimum-radius rounding pass. A path's last point is stored in station-local coordinates, so it rotates with the bay. Collisions are circle tests with a broad grid, and arrivals come from a seeded schedule, so every run replays exactly. Test hook: Arcade.test {start, lose, state}; ?debug window.__game {start(seed), route(shipId, points), hold(shipId), step(ms), lose(), state()}. A bot that routes each ship along a precomputed safe arc should survive 3 minutes, and a bot that does nothing should lose.

games.title: Tuskfloe
games.pitch: A walrus on a cracking ice floe. Bump rivals into the sea without sliding in after them.
games.hook: You push and the walrus starts sliding on slick ice. It bowls three penguins off the edge with a plop-plop-plop and splash plumes, and you nearly slide off yourself.
games.loop: Top-down (slightly tilted) ice floe in an arctic sea. A floating joystick sets your acceleration, and the ice has very low friction, so momentum is everything. Collisions are mass-based circle bumps: knockback equals your impact speed times your mass against theirs. Anything whose centre crosses the floe edge falls in, you included (costs one of 3 lives, respawn at the centre after 1.5 s with brief invulnerability). Quick-tap anywhere to tusk-brake: a hard stop with an ice-spray scrape and 1 s cooldown, the key skill for not following enemies into the water. Enemies: penguins (the comic minions: light, waddling in groups, worth bowling, never the real threat), seals (wiggle tell, then dash at you), rival walruses (heavy shoving matches), narwhals (a ripple at the edge, then a tusk jab onto the ice), orcas (breach at the edge and grab anything near it). The floe cracks: big impacts and time advance cracks along a seeded fracture plan, and broken chunks drift off with anyone on them, so the arena shrinks. Score: ring-outs with multi-ring-out bowling bonuses.
games.controls: One thumb: drag anywhere for a floating joystick; a quick tap for tusk-brake. Keyboard: arrows move, Space brakes.
games.progression: Floes in sets of 3 waves. After each set the walrus belly-slides onto a fresh floe (a short hop transition) with a new seeded shape and conditions: pack ice under a steel sky, blizzard (reduced visibility, gusts that push everyone), sea smoke (fog rolling over the floe, with a foghorn tell for orcas) and spring melt (meltwater pools and slush patches with more friction). New enemies arrive every two waves; seals, rival walruses and the narwhal are the stars of the cast. Bosses close each set: a polar bear (heavy, swipes with a telegraph, must be baited to charge past you near the edge), then the old Walrus King. Best score and best ring-out combo are saved.
games.art: A bright, cold Arctic noon under a steel sky, not pastel: sky #8fa7b3 to #c9d6dc, a slate-teal sea (#234a57) with animated sparkle glints and soft swell lines. Ice: white (#f4fbff) with blue shadows (#9fd3e6), crisp bevelled edges with a darker waterline, cracks as dark-blue jagged lines with frosty halos. The cast's warm colours carry the screen. Characters are drawn 3/4 top-down with soft shadows: the walrus is chunky brown-pink (#a5735b) with ivory tusks, whiskers and a dopey determined face; seals are sleek grey with dark spots; rival walruses wear scars and different tusk shapes; the narwhal is mottled grey with a spiral tusk; penguins are tiny comic extras with a waddle; the polar bear is cream and massive. Sea smoke is soft white drifting bands; spring melt adds turquoise meltwater pools. HUD: weathered whalebone plaques lashed with rope; lives as three little fish; score in chunky stencilled Unbounded numerals; a combo bubble when bowling. Shell theme: weathered whalebone and rope with stencilled Unbounded numerals.
games.audio: Playful oompah-folk at 104 BPM: tuba-ish square bass with soft attack, staccato glockenspiel triangles, accordion pad; the blizzard stage switches to minor with wind noise. SFX: a deep 'bonk' bump (sine pitch drop, scaled by impact), penguin squeaks, splash (noise burst plus bubbly pitch rise), ice crack (sharp click plus low groan), tusk-brake scrape (filtered noise), orca whoosh tell, a triumphant toot on multi ring-out.
juice: Splash plumes with expanding ripple rings and droplets
Impact hitstop and squash on both bodies, with snow puffs
Cracks draw in along the fracture line with shards, then the chunk bobs as it drifts away
Triple ring-out: 0.3 s slow motion and a bowling-pin style toot
Tusk-brake: ice-spray fan and screen nudge
games.teach: It starts on a big floe with 3 penguins in a row near the edge. A ghost thumb pushes the walrus into them (instant bowling). Then a seal nudges you toward the edge with a pulsing tap icon for the brake. Only text: 'Push them off. Tap to brake.'
games.scenes: art: the walrus bowling penguins off a cracking floe with splash plumes, a rival walrus and a seal mid-dash, slate sea and steel sky, no HUD. shot1: set 1, a shoving match with a rival walrus near a crack line and the whalebone HUD. shot2: a sea-smoke floe shrunk to a few chunks with the polar bear charging and an orca breaching at the edge.
games.feasibility: Medium-low risk. Physics is 2D circle-circle impulses with mass (no rotation), cheap for under 25 bodies. The floe is a set of precomputed seeded polygon cells (Voronoi from seed, or a simpler jittered grid). On-floe tests are point-in-polygon over attached cells, and cracks detach a cell group, which then drifts. The fracture plan is deterministic. Debug hook: window.__game {start(seed, set), step(ms), stick(dx,dy), brake(), lose(), state()}.

games.title: Ballast
games.pitch: Fly the balloon post over a patchwork valley. Rise and sink to catch the wind that carries the mail.
games.hook: Hold anywhere and the burner roars, the envelope glows from inside and the balloon lifts. Chimney smoke below drifts one way and the kites above tug the other, so rising into a higher band visibly whisks you toward the village where the postmaster is waving a flag. You learn a whole navigation system from one thumb in about ten seconds.
games.loop: A seeded horizontal stretch of countryside about 12 screens wide: a patchwork of fields, a winding river valley, stone villages, a hilltop abbey, a lighthouse at the estuary and a mountain hut up the ridge, with the camera following the balloon. WIND LAYERS: 5 to 7 altitude bands, each with its own direction and speed, shown by cues at that height: windmill sails and chimney smoke near the ground, kites and bird flocks in the middle, cloud wisps high up. The bands slowly shift as the day passes. INPUT: hold to fire the burner and release to cool. Buoyancy follows envelope temperature with real thermal lag (about 0.8s), so you must anticipate. A quick double-tap vents for a fast drop. Horizontal motion comes ONLY from wind. POST: mail sacks wait at sorting posts, marked with a stamp pictogram and a coloured flag. Pass slowly within 40px above a sack and it hooks onto your rope (a 6-point verlet rope that swings with momentum). Deliver it by lowering it onto the village green or rooftop flying the matching flag, where a postmaster waves you in. FUEL: the burner uses propane. Land gently on a fuel meadow (vertical speed under a threshold) to refill. HAZARDS: storm clouds (lightning telegraphed by internal flicker, a strike tears a patch), church spires and the abbey's bell tower, flocks of geese crossing in a V (a honk telegraph), and downdrafts in the lee of hills. PATCHES: 3; the run ends when all are torn, or when you run out of fuel and come down in a field far from any post. Each in-game day lasts about 3 minutes, with deliveries paying coins.
games.controls: One thumb. Hold anywhere for the burner, release to cool, double-tap to vent. Keyboard: hold Space for the burner, Down to vent.
games.progression: Day 1: calm winds, near villages. Day 2: storms. Day 3: hills with lee downdrafts and the abbey. Day 4: geese. Day 5: night (lanterns glow in cottage windows to mark the landing greens, and the wind is read from chimney smoke lit by the windows and cloud edges against the moon). Day 6: thunderheads that drift. After that, days remix with tighter fuel. Between days a tiny post-office scene (icon buttons) buys a bigger envelope (more lift), a larger tank, a longer rope or tougher patches, plus cosmetic envelope patterns unlocked by milestones. Routes chain: delivering to one village reveals its outgoing sack. Each day is seeded from (runSeed, day). The save holds day, coins, upgrades and patches.
games.art: World: a rolling patchwork countryside seen from the air, changing with the time of day. From altitude the fields are a quilt of greens and ochres (#7fb069, #a7c957, #d4a259, #e9c46a) stitched together by hedgerows, with a river (#5fa8c7) winding through the valley, stone villages with red roofs, windmills, a hilltop abbey, a lighthouse at the estuary and a hut on the ridge. Sky gradients: dawn #ffd6c2 to #9fb8ff, noon #8fd3ff to #e9f7ff, dusk #ff9a8b to #6b4c9a, night #1b1f4b with stars. Soft cumulus are clusters of circles pre-rendered with top light and underside shade, in three parallax depths, and their shadows slide over the fields. The balloon has a patchwork striped envelope with gradient shading, glows warm from inside when the burner fires, sits over a wicker basket with a tiny pilot in a postal cap, and casts a shadow on the land below. Wind cues are drawn per band and tinted by direction (warm when going right, cool when going left), which makes the layers readable. HUD: a brass altimeter dial on the left edge whose scale carries a little wind arrow for each band (the key navigation aid), a fuel gauge drawn on the basket, the mail tag hanging from the rope, and patches as cloth swatches. Shell theme: cream and bunting stripes, stitched like a balloon envelope, with postage-stamp corners.
games.audio: Music: a gentle waltz in 3/4 at 96bpm. An accordion-like pad, music-box bells and pizzicato bass. The night swaps in celesta and slows to 84bpm, and storms add low tremolo strings. SFX: the burner roar (noise plus a low sine whose filter opens while held), the venting hiss, basket creaks, the mail-sack hook clink, a post-horn toot and a delivery bell with little cheering chirps, wind gust whooshes, thunder rumble, goose honks and a cloth rip when a patch tears.
juice: The burner flame lights the envelope from inside and a heat shimmer ripples above the basket
A delivery launches bunting confetti from the village green, the postmaster waves both flags, and coins arc up into the mail tag
Lightning flashes white with the balloon silhouetted against the storm, and a patch flaps loose
A soft landing squashes the basket, puffs dust and flattens the grass in a ring
Day transitions sweep the sun or moon across the sky as the wind arrows on the altimeter re-shuffle
games.teach: You start low beside a sorting post in a calm band. A ghost hand holds, the balloon rises, and the altimeter shows that the band just above blows toward the first village (whose flag waves). The first sack hooks automatically as you pass. Vent is introduced on day 2 with a double-tap icon. tutorial_complete is tracked on the first delivery.
games.scenes: art: dusk sky, the striped balloon glowing mid-burn above a patchwork valley with a river and a stone village, chimney smoke and kites showing two wind directions, the abbey on its hill. No HUD. shot1: day 1 noon with a mail sack swinging on the rope, the altimeter's wind arrows and the postmaster's flag in view. shot2: day 5 night over cottages with lit windows, a storm cell flickering and chimney smoke tracing the low band.
games.feasibility: Low risk. The control is one-dimensional, the wind field is a pure function f(altitude, time, seed), the rope is a 6-point verlet chain and clouds are pre-rendered sprites. Deterministic fixed-step physics. The main design risk is drifting aimlessly, mitigated by the altimeter wind key, short routes and visible flags. Test hook: window.__game = { start(seed, day), burner(bool), vent(), step(frames), pop() /* tears all patches, loses */, state() }.

games.title: Swingby
games.pitch: A grapple race between two bright suns. Tether to anchors, fling off, and steal the line from your rivals.
games.hook: Your ship streaks toward a coral-lit moon whose grab ring pulses. You press: a taut glowing cord snaps on first, the rival behind is locked out and swerves wide, and your ship whips round the anchor with a rising hum. Let go on the tangent and you shoot past them both. One gesture, and the race is already personal.
games.loop: A vertical course (portrait) up through a seeded binary-star system of 10-14 anchors (small moons and beacon buoys, radius 30-90 px, each with a visible grab ring at 1.6-2.2 times its radius), plus hazards and the finish beacon at the top. Ships fly in straight lines at their current speed; there is no gravity anywhere, only grapples, so it is readable. Holding anywhere fires a tether to the nearest free anchor whose grab ring you are inside, highlighted in advance. The ship then moves on a circle at its grab radius, building speed at 8% per second up to a cap. Releasing sends it off on the tangent. A small 'perfect' arc on each orbit marks the release angle that points at the next anchor, and releasing inside it adds a 25% speed burst. RIVALS GET IN YOUR WAY: each anchor holds one tether at a time, so grabbing first locks rivals out and forces them onto a worse line (and they do it to you; a taken anchor shows a red clamp). Staying on for a second orbit keeps building speed, but it is a gamble: a rival crossing your tether cord at speed clips it, flinging you off at a random angle with a 30% speed loss, and you can clip theirs the same way. Hazards: drifting asteroid streams (collision = tumble and lose 40% speed) and stellar flares telegraphed by a glowing arc 1 s ahead. Drifting past the course edges triggers an auto-recall to the last anchor with a 2 s penalty. Three rivals are flown by a live lookahead planner with personalities (a blocker who takes the anchors you need, a clipper who hunts tethers, a clean racer). HEATS: each system is a heat. You carry 3 hull chevrons through the run: finishing last in a heat costs one, winning a heat restores one, and the run ends (reason 'lose') when the last is gone. Your finishing position also sets your start slot in the next heat. Score = heats survived x 1000 + perfect releases + lockouts and clips landed.
games.controls: One thumb: hold anywhere to tether, release to fling. Keyboard: Space.
games.progression: Systems are endless and generated from the seed and system number. Early systems have wide grab rings and few hazards. Then come tight anchor pairs where lockouts decide everything (system 3), asteroid streams (5), twin-sun systems whose stars sweep flare arcs across the course (7), anchors moving on rails (9), and pulsar anchors (12) that spin your tether twice as fast for a huge release but sweep a beam that cuts tethers on a timer. The palette shifts between binary pairs (coral and cyan, gold and violet, rose and mint). Rival planners get greedier and clip more often each system. Ship hulls and cord colours unlock at system milestones. Best system is shown on the shell. Runs take 1-4 minutes and the hazards build up steadily.
games.art: A bright binary-star system in light, not dark: the background is a near-white haze (#f4f1ec to #e6eef2) warmed by a coral sun (#ff6f61) at one side and an electric-cyan sun (#22d3ee) at the other, with soft light gradients between them. There is no nebula, no black void and no ringed planet. Anchors are small matte moons and white beacon buoys, each lit coral on one side and cyan on the other, which gives every object a two-tone rim. Grab rings are thin dashed circles. Tethers are taut glowing cords drawn as a bright core with a soft halo in each racer's colour, with a twang ripple when they snap on. Ships are sleek darts in saturated liveries (yours navy #1e2a55 with a coral stripe) with clean exhaust streaks rather than comet trails, so they read on the light ground. Asteroids are charcoal (#3a3d46) with crisp shadows. HUD: race-timing overlays in navy: a vertical progress ladder on the right edge with a dot for each racer, the hull as three small chevrons, and the position as a big italic numeral. Shell theme: a race pit-board (white enamel with coral and cyan timing strips).
games.audio: Bright electro-pop at 112 bpm: sine sub bass, plucked FM arpeggios, claps and shaker, plus an extra percussion layer in later systems. Sound effects: tether snap (a bright twang), a hum while tethered whose pitch rises with angular speed, release zing, perfect release (harmonic chime), lockout (a clamp clank as a rival's anchor closes to you), tether clip (a snapped-string twang with a pitch drop), heat finish (whoosh plus a chord from stacked delays), asteroid hit (crunch with static), overtake blip.
juice: The cord snaps on with a quick camera zoom-in and a twang ripple running along it
While orbiting, the hum climbs in pitch and speed lines thicken
A perfect release slows time for 0.2 s, flashes a ring burst and stretches the exhaust streak
Lockout: the anchor's clamp flashes your colour and the locked-out rival swerves with a puff of thruster
Clipping a rival's cord: hitstop, the cord whips loose and the rival spins off with a pitch-dropping twang
An asteroid hit shakes the screen and scatters rock fragments
games.teach: System 1 starts with the ship drifting straight into a big moon's pulsing grab ring and a ghost finger pressing 'hold'. After 90 degrees of orbit the next anchor and the perfect arc flash, and the ghost finger lifts. In system 2 a slow rival reaches an anchor first, and its red clamp shows the lockout. Track tutorial_complete after the player's first swing from one anchor to the next on their own.
games.scenes: art: the ship mid-swing round a two-tone moon on a taut glowing cord, a rival locked out and swerving wide, coral and cyan suns lighting the haze, no HUD. shot1: the start line with four ships below the first moon and its pulsing grab ring, the HUD ladder and hull chevrons. shot2: a twin-sun flare system with an asteroid stream, the player clipping a rival's cord in 2nd place.
games.feasibility: Low risk. Motion is straight lines or circles, collisions are circle tests, and tether clips are segment-versus-moving-circle tests. Anchor ownership is a single field per anchor. Rival 'AI' is a lookahead planner: at each anchor it tries release angles in 2 degree steps, scores the line into the next free grab ring, and adds a personality term (block, clip, clean) plus seeded skill noise. Because the player affects rivals it runs live rather than as a replay, but it is deterministic under the seed and the fixed step. The background is a few baked gradients. Auto-recall prevents soft-locks. Test hook: Arcade.test {start, lose, state}; ?debug exposes window.__game { start(seed, system), hold(bool), autopilot(true), forceLose(), state() } so Playwright can fly a system with the planner and force a loss.

games.title: Logjam
games.pitch: Slide logs on an autumn millpond until they jam, and float the beaver family's raft out through the weir.
games.hook: Flick a log and it glides across the water with a soft whoosh, then knocks into another with a hollow 'tok' and a ring of ripples. A few flicks later the beavers' raft drifts out through the gap in the weir while the kits slap their tails.
games.loop: A 6x6 pond grid (7x7 later) walled by the banks, with a weir gap on the right edge. Logs are 1x2 or 1x3, lying horizontal or vertical, and move only along their length. The twist: a flicked log always slides until something stops it (another log, a boulder or the bank) and never stops midway, so every log has at most 2 possible moves. The beaver raft (1x2, horizontal, with the family aboard) must slide out through the weir. Later pieces: river otters (1x1, can slide in any of 4 directions, still until blocked), mossy boulders (fixed), and from pond 41 two rafts and two weirs. Par is the BFS optimum, and stars are given at par, par+3, or solved. Undo and restart are unlimited and there is no fail. Generation: random placement under constraints from seed+attempt, then BFS (tiny state space) for the optimum. A pond is accepted if par falls in the band and at least k distinct logs must move.
games.controls: One thumb: swipe on a log along its length; a short swipe is enough and the direction decides the move. For otters, swipe in any direction. Undo and Restart buttons. Keyboard: Tab or click to select a log, then arrows.
games.progression: Ponds 1-10: logs only, par 2-6. Ponds 11-25: mossy boulders. Ponds 26-40: otters. Ponds 41-55: 7x7 with two rafts and two weirs. Pond 56 onward is endless, with par bands rising to 14-20 and varied piece mixes. The run is saved, and progress shows 'Pond 19'. Best = ponds solved.
games.art: An autumn millpond in morning mist, seen from above. Tea-brown water (#4a3a24 in the deeps to #7a5a2e in the shallows) with soft reflections of the birch trunks on the banks and copper and maple leaves (#c4622d, #e0a03a) that drift and bob in the wakes. Mist bands cross at low alpha and burn off a little as you solve. Logs are bark-brown cylinders from above with ring-cut ends (#8a5a35 bark, #e2c08a end grain), moss patches and a soft shadow on the water. The beaver raft is lashed sticks with the family aboard: two adults and their kits, round brown bodies with flat tails that slap. Otters are sleek dark brown (#4b3526) with pale chins and whiskers; mossy boulders are grey-green with fern tufts. The weir is a low timber-and-stone dam with a bright gap where the water spills. HUD: a top bar of birch-bark strips with the pond number carved in and the move count beside leaf-shaped par markers. The menu shell is birch bark (white bark with dark lenticel marks and a peeled-curl edge). Dark mode is a moonlit pond: deep umber water (#1f1810), silver birches, leaves catching the moon.
games.audio: Music: a gentle 96 bpm loop of plucked guitar-like Karplus-Strong, a soft clarinet-like sine lead and a light woodblock, in a major key. SFX: a flick is a water swish whose length follows slide distance. A collision is a hollow wooden 'tok' (low sine plus noise) pitched by log size, otters chirp, and the kits squeak and slap their tails. A raft exit plays a splash over the weir, a short fanfare and a chorus of tail slaps in rhythm.
juice: Logs ease in, glide and ease out with a V-shaped wake that rocks the floating leaves
Impacts make both logs shudder and throw ripple rings and droplets, with a haptic and a small shake for 1x3 hits
The beavers lean against the motion and grip the raft
On exit the raft tips over the weir in a splash as the family cheers, leaves swirl and leaf-shaped stars stamp in
Undo glides the log back in reverse with a soft swish
games.teach: Pond 1: the raft is blocked by one vertical log. A ghost swipe flicks that log down, then a second ghost swipe sends the raft out. Pond 2 is solved alone. The 'slides until it hits' rule is learned on the first flick.
games.scenes: Art: the misty millpond with the beaver raft tipping out through the weir, otters in the water, logs jammed and leaves drifting, with no HUD. Shot1: Pond 1 with the birch-bark HUD and the ghost swipe. Shot2: Pond 33 with otters, boulders and a log mid-slide with its wake.
games.feasibility: Very low risk. The state space is tiny because pieces slide until blocked, so BFS and generation take milliseconds. Animation is just tweens. One shared move function serves both the solver and the play. Test hook: Arcade.test {start, lose, state}, where lose is a forfeit; ?debug __game.start(pond), .move(pieceId, dir), .solution(), .state(), .forfeit() (runEnd 'restart'). Estimated 1500-1900 lines.

games.title: Highcourt
games.pitch: Flick basketballs across city rooftops at blue hour. Bank off chimneys, beat the shot clock, swish to catch fire.
games.hook: The first ball sits under your thumb with a ghost flick over it. One upward swipe sends a spinning ball into a lit-up rooftop hoop, the net snaps, the string lights flicker and the score stamps onto the wall. You make a basket within three seconds and instantly want a cleaner one.
games.loop: Behind-the-shooter view, portrait. The ball rests at the bottom centre. Swipe up: the swipe's angle sets left/right aim, its length and speed set power (arc height and depth). The ball is a 3D point with gravity, projected by a fixed perspective camera. Rim = a circle in 3D; each fixed step, find the nearest point on the rim circle to the ball centre and, if closer than ball radius, reflect velocity along that normal (restitution 0.55). Backboard = a plane rectangle with the same treatment. Scoring when the ball crosses the rim plane going down inside the rim: Swish (no rim or board contact) 3, Rim-in 2, Bank 2 + 1 bonus. Three swishes in a row = On Fire: ball burns, all points x2 until a miss. Misses cost one of 3 basketballs (shown as balls on a crate); a run ends when all 3 are gone; every 5 makes in a row returns one ball (max 3). Each shot is taken from a new spot on the current rooftop (distance and angle change, hoop moves on screen). Every 8 makes you jump to the next rooftop, which adds a modifier.
games.controls: One thumb: swipe up from the ball to shoot (aim by angle, power by length/speed). Keyboard: Left/Right to aim, hold Space to charge power, release to shoot.
games.progression: Rooftops in a fixed order, each adding one basketball rule: 1 Laundry Roof (close range, plain shots), 2 Water-Tower Roof (longer shots), 3 Chimney Roof (bank shots: a marked chimney, skylight or water tank glows, and hitting it before the hoop pays triple, using the same plane collision as the backboard), 4 Gantry Roof (the hoop slides slowly on a window-cleaning gantry), 5 Clock Roof (a 24-second shot clock on a big rooftop clock face; every ball released within 3 s of the last earns a quick-release bonus, and the clock running out costs a ball), 6 Rival Roof (an AI shooter on the next roof alternates with you in a letter-elimination game: when they make a shot and you miss yours, you take a letter, chalked on the roof; spell their word and you lose a ball, make them spell it and you win one back). After rooftop 6 the cycle repeats with a higher difficulty number (more distance, a faster gantry, a shorter clock, a sharper rival). Shot spots are seeded per rooftop, so each roof feels the same on replays but different from the others. There is no wind in this game. Best score and best streak are kept.
games.art: A sprawling brick-and-water-tower city at blue hour, flat and dense along a river, seen from a rooftop court. Sky: a vertical gradient from tangerine #FF7A3D at the horizon through rose #E0567A to indigo #1B1035. Background layers: 3 parallax skyline silhouettes (#2A1B4F, #3B2766, #523A80), each with a pre-rendered scatter of lit windows in sodium #FFC857 and teal #2EC4B6 that twinkle at random; distant bridge lights strung across the river; an elevated train crossing far away. Foreground: chain-link fence (a pre-rendered diagonal mesh), water tanks, string bulbs that sway and glow, a rooftop court surface #3A2A5C with chalky painted lines #F2E9E4. Hoop: orange rim #FF5B2E, white backboard with a scuffed box, a net drawn as 8 strands that bulge and whip on swish (spring per strand). Ball: orange gradient with seam lines rotating with spin, soft contact shadow on the court. Lighting: a warm key light from a street lamp, a multiply vignette, and bloom on the On Fire ball (additive flame particles). HUD: spray-paint stencil style - the score is drawn as stencilled digits on a brick wall panel at the top-left with drips; balls left are basketballs on a milk crate at the bottom-right; streak shown as tally marks. Shell theme: spray-paint stencil on brick, with tangerine drips and Unbounded headings.
games.audio: Music: laid-back lo-fi hip-hop loop at 84 BPM, swung drums (kick, snare with noise tail, closed hat), a warm square-wave bass and a two-chord electric-piano pad; while On Fire a bright arpeggio layer joins. SFX: ball bounce (low sine thump with pitch drop), rim clank (short metallic FM ping), backboard thud, swish (filtered noise sweep), crowd-of-neighbours 'ooh' (layered noise formant), fire ignite (rising noise whoosh), ball lost (dull drop and a cat-hiss-like noise), new rooftop (rising three-note stinger).
juice: Swish: net whips, the camera dips 4px, 6 frames of hit-stop, chalk-dust burst from the net and a '+3' stencil stamp that slams onto the wall
On Fire: the ball trails additive flame particles, string bulbs flash in sequence, music arpeggio kicks in, the stencil score turns flaming orange
Rim rattle: ball wobbles on the rim with clank sounds rising in pitch before dropping in or out - suspense moment
Ball lost: the crate ball rolls off the crate and drops off the roof edge with a tiny screen shake

Rooftop jump: the camera pans across the skyline to the next roof while the score counts up. Chimney bank: the chimney puffs a ring of soot and a 'x3' stencil sprays onto the brick as the ball drops in
Long shot made (beyond 'three-point' line): neighbours' windows light up and confetti from a balcony
games.teach: The title shows the live court with a ghost thumb flicking a ball in a loop. First shot is from directly under the hoop with the ghost hand visible until the first make; a dotted arc shows the ideal flick for the first two shots only. No text needed beyond the hint 'Flick up to shoot'.
games.scenes: art: Chimney Roof at blue hour, seeded, the ball On Fire mid-arc off a glowing chimney toward the rim with its flame trail, net slightly lifted, no HUD. shot1: rooftop 2 mid-run, ball in flight, stencil score and crate visible. shot2: an On Fire swish on the Gantry Roof with a '+6' stamp, confetti and the streak tally.
games.feasibility: Risks: pseudo-3D ball physics and rim collision could get fiddly; flick feel is make-or-break. Mitigation: physics is a single 3D point against one circle and one rectangle (no rigid-body), with a fixed 120 Hz substep, so it is ~100 lines; flick mapping uses a lookup tuned so a natural 250 px swipe from 'spot 1' is a make, and an aim-assist cone that shrinks with rooftop number. Shot spots, bank targets and the rival's shots are seeded per rooftop (Kit seeded RNG). Test hook: start() begins a run on rooftop 1; lose() empties the crate; a ?debug function shoot(angle,power) lets the Playwright test fire scripted shots and assert scoring (a known perfect flick swishes, a weak flick misses and costs a ball). Net is 8 spring strands, cheap. Skyline layers pre-rendered to offscreen canvases.

games.title: Switchback
games.pitch: A runaway ore cart on a canyon railway. Jump the gaps, flip the switches, never stop.
games.hook: The ore cart is already rattling downhill. A lever ahead blinks its lamp toward the upper line; you flick up and the cart clatters over the points onto a high trestle just as the lower track ends in a broken gap. Two seconds in, you know the whole game.
games.loop: Side view. The cart rolls right on up to 3 stacked rail lines that split and merge at switch points. Each switch is marked by a lever whose lamp lights 0.8 s ahead. Swipe up or down before a switch to take the upper or lower line. Tap to jump broken rails and dynamite crates. Hold on a downhill to brake (rail sparks), so the cart does not fly off a curve or the end of a trestle, and release on uphills to keep speed. Speed is the score multiplier, so every brake is a cost. Gems sit on the risky lines, and a gold nugget chain pays only if you never touch the brake through it. Hazards: collapsing trestles (planks drop away in sequence), rockfall shadows that grow on the track, a rival bandit cart on a parallel line that tries to cut over at switches, and tunnels where the cart's headlamp shows the next switch. One crash ends the run. Score = distance x speed multiplier + gems + nugget chains.
games.controls: One thumb: swipe up or down to pick the line at the next switch, tap to jump, hold to brake. Keyboard: Up/Down pick the line, Space jumps, hold Shift (or Left) to brake.
games.progression: Endless seeded chunks with difficulty tiers, travelling through five stretches of the line: the desert canyon, the red-rock arches, the salt mine (white crystal tunnels), the cactus flats at sunset, and a storm stretch where lightning lights the tracks. Switch density, gaps and the bandit's aggression rise per tier, and the collapsing trestles get longer. Best score and longest nugget chain are saved.
games.art: A sunlit desert canyon, a palette no other game in the catalogue uses: terracotta and burnt-orange rock (#b5532a, #e08a4c) in banded strata, a pale turquoise sky (#8fd1d0) with #2f6f73 teal shade in the canyon's shadowed side, and crisp hard shadows from a high sun. Timber trestles are drawn with cross-bracing and their own shadows on the rock, rails glint, and dust plumes trail the cart. The cart is a riveted iron tub with a swinging headlamp and a goggled prospector hunched inside; the bandit cart's rider wears a bandanna. The salt mine is white crystal walls lit warm by the headlamp (warm partial light, never a black mask), the sunset flats are long orange light with saguaro silhouettes, and the storm is slate purple with lightning flashing the scene white. HUD: the score on a painted mileage board, the speed multiplier on a brass pressure gauge, gems collected in a tin. Shell theme: stencilled railway timber.
games.audio: Music: a twangy desert shuffle at 120 bpm (plucked synth guitar, a harmonica-like square with vibrato, brushed snare) whose tempo follows the cart's speed. The rail clack rhythm (a click at every rail joint) speeds up with the cart too. SFX: brake screech with sparks, switch clank, jump creak and landing thud, dynamite boom, rockfall rumble, the bandit's whistle, a gem chime and an ascending nugget-chain ding, and tunnels add an echo (feedback delay).
juice: Braking throws a shower of sparks under the wheels and the headlamp swings forward
Switches throw with a heavy clank and the lever animates as you pass
Jumps lift the cart in a puff of dust, and the landing squashes it with a camera bump
Collapsing trestle planks fall away in sequence just behind the cart
Crash: the cart flips in 0.3 s of slow motion and ore and gems scatter down the canyon
games.teach: The first chunk teaches one thing at a time with ghosts: a single switch with a ghost swipe, then a gap with a ghost tap, then a downhill curve with a ghost hold and a speed sign that glows when you are too fast. The only text is 'Swipe to switch, tap to jump, hold to brake'.
games.scenes: art: the cart mid-jump between two trestles over a red-rock canyon, dust plumes behind and the bandit cart on the lower line, no HUD. shot1: 6 s in, approaching a switch with its lamp lit and the mileage-board HUD. shot2: the storm stretch, lightning lighting the tracks, a trestle collapsing behind the cart and a nugget chain of 6.
games.feasibility: Low risk, about 1500-2000 lines. Rails are polylines per line, the cart is a point on a line plus a ballistic jump state, switches are scripted choices, and chunks are seeded from templates with difficulty weights, each validated to have a safe line. Background strata and trestles are pre-rendered per chunk. Test hook: Arcade.test {start, lose, state}; ?debug window.__game {start(seed), switchTo(line), jump(), brake(bool), step(ms), lose(), state()} with the upcoming switches in state(), so a bot can run 10 seeds and assert that every chunk is reachable.
